## Codebase Patterns
- Cross-cutting capability package + at-rest encryption seam (BE-0339 pattern, internal/controlplane/secrets/{doc.go, provider.go, aesgcm.go, plaintext.go, *_test.go, AGENTS.md} + internal/controlplane/store/migrate/migrations/0029_organization_variables_encrypted_secrets.{up,down}.sql + internal/controlplane/store/organization_variable.go + organization_variable_service.go + organization_variable_secrets_at_rest_test.go + cmd/yalla-api/main.go buildSecretsProvider; structural template for BE-0340..0342 sibling at-rest stories (project / environment / service variable encryption-at-rest) and any future cross-cutting source-of-truth seam over a same-shape resource family — webhook signing secrets, deployment-config secrets, backup-target credentials, etc.). Six load-bearing rules for the cross-cutting package: (1) Land the package ONCE under internal/controlplane/<pkg>, with the Provider interface + a production implementation (AESGCM) + a tests-only passthrough implementation (Plaintext, restricted to local/test profiles by cmd/yalla-api) + a package AGENTS.md that documents BOTH the runtime contract AND the forward-applicable storage pattern (column shape, CHECK constraint shape, repository tuple shape, service-layer seam location). (2) Typed value-free errors (ErrInvalidCiphertext / ErrUnknownKey / ErrUnsupportedProvider) — the secrets package contract never echoes any of {plaintext, ciphertext bytes, key material, key id, nonce} into an error message; the only observable on a failure is the classification. (3) AES-256-GCM with per-Seal random crypto/rand nonce + AEAD-authenticated decryption + multi-key rotation pool (first key is active for Seal, all keys accepted for Open). KeyID derivation = first 8 bytes of SHA-256(key) hex-encoded (16 chars): deterministic across processes, non-secret (one-way hash), short enough for audit metadata. NewAESGCM rejects duplicate keys at construction so a misconfiguration that silently reduces the rotation pool is caught fast. (4) cmd/yalla-api wires the provider in ONE buildSecretsProvider helper near runStartupChecks, NOT one per scope. Strict profiles (staging/production) refuse to start without YALLA_SECRET_KEYS (config.requireStrictFields enforces) via an explicit sentinel error; permissive profiles (local/test) fall back to Plaintext with a Warn log line. (5) The interface is INTENTIONALLY same-width every scope needs (org/project/env/service variables), so a single provider configured at startup covers every variables table — sibling at-rest stories become mechanical clones of schema + service + test changes. (6) For internal-only read paths that legitimately need the plaintext (the future Dokploy renderer worker, BE-0343 variable-inheritance resolver), Open the sealed tuple through the same Provider passed into the service — NEVER a wire-facing endpoint. Six load-bearing rules for the storage shape per table: (1) Add three nullable columns (secret_provider text NULL, secret_key_id text NULL, secret_ciphertext bytea NULL) ALONGSIDE the existing plain `value` column, never instead of it; force value='' for secret rows and cipher columns NULL for non-secret rows via ONE CHECK constraint named <table>_secret_columns_consistent that pins the invariant in both directions. The CHECK is the defence-in-depth backstop the service relies on — a bug that tries to write a plaintext secret rolls back as deterministic apierr.Conflict rather than silent corruption. (2) Mirror DO $$ guards in BOTH the up and the down migration that REFUSE to run while is_secret=true rows exist with the wrong shape — a re-application against a database that accumulated plaintext secrets fails loudly rather than silently leaving them behind, and a rollback against a database with sealed rows fails loudly rather than silently losing every secret value. (3) Add a partial index on (secret_provider, secret_key_id) WHERE is_secret=true so the future key-rotation worker (BE-0351) can locate rows referencing a retired key without a full-table scan. (4) The repository's Upsert + UpdateMutable signatures take a closed-set Input tuple (<Table>VariableUpsert with Value/IsSecret/SecretProvider/SecretKeyID/SecretCiphertext) — keeps the signature narrow as new secret fields land and centralises the "nullable columns when is_secret=false" projection in one helper (nullableSecretColumns). (5) The OrganizationVariable struct (and siblings) gain the three encryption-at-rest fields as INTERNAL-only — never on the wire — and the LogValue redaction MUST be updated in the SAME edit to redact BOTH the plaintext AND the new ciphertext to output.Sentinel; an unstale slog record that captures the struct cannot leak either. (6) scanRow projection routes through sql.NullString for the nullable text columns (pgx-scan into *string rejects NULL). Five load-bearing rules for the service-layer seam: (1) Seal at the SERVICE layer, never the repository — Seal is a side-effecting call that depends on a runtime Provider not a *Tx, calling Seal BEFORE opening the transaction shortens the SQL critical section, and the repository stays pure SQL. The cleanest helper is a one-line projector (sealVariableValue) that takes the customer's input shape (<Table>VariableReplace) and returns the repository's tuple shape (<Table>VariableUpsert) — non-secret items pass through untouched, secret items go through Provider.Seal. (2) The Service's constructor (NewOrganizationVariableService) takes Provider as a REQUIRED dependency rejected at construction if nil — a production process cannot accidentally start with the at-rest seam disabled. (3) Patch path for sealed rows has THREE post-state cases the service must enumerate explicitly: (a) caller supplied a new value → use it verbatim; (b) caller supplied only is_secret AND the current row is_secret → Open the current ciphertext via Provider.Open to recover the plaintext, then re-Seal under the active key (the only correct way to re-key a secret without surfacing the plaintext to the caller); (c) otherwise → use the current row's `value` column. Skipping case (b) would either lose the secret bytes on a re-seal or write a "previously-sealed plaintext" string into the value column. (4) The demotion path (is_secret=true→false) reuses case (b) to recover the plaintext, then writes it back to the value column with NULL encryption columns — the ONLY customer path that surfaces a previously-sealed plaintext, and only as a deliberate operator action. (5) Seal failures surface as apierr.Internal with a value-free wrapped cause — a sealing error is a server-side problem, never customer input, and the wrap never echoes the plaintext. Six load-bearing rules for the integration-test surface: (1) The integration test file lives next to the existing repository tests as <table>_secrets_at_rest_test.go, uses testutil.RequireMigratedDB (skips cleanly when YALLA_TEST_DATABASE_URL is unset so go test ./... stays green without Postgres), and wires a REAL AES-256-GCM provider (mustAESGCM helper that mints a fresh 32-byte key per test so parallel tests cannot bleed key ids across each other). (2) Five pinned tests per scope: SealsSecretValuesAtRest (the load-bearing contract — secret value reaches Postgres ONLY as AES-GCM ciphertext under the active key id, value column is "", on-disk bytea does not contain the plaintext substring, ciphertext round-trips through Provider.Open, audit row never carries any of {plaintext, key name, hex ciphertext, key id, provider id}); PatchRotatesCiphertextOnEveryWrite (a patch that flips is_secret only on a sealed row Opens-then-Seals under a fresh nonce so on-disk bytes change between writes); PatchDemotesSecretToPlaintext (is_secret=true→false with no new value recovers the plaintext via Open and writes to the value column with NULL encryption columns); SchemaRejectsPlaintextSecretWrite (three direct INSERT attempts that would land a plaintext-secret row each surface a constraint violation whose error message names the constraint); LogValueRedactsCiphertextAndPlaintext (a structured log record that captures the variable struct redacts BOTH plaintext AND ciphertext to output.Sentinel while exposing provider id + key id). (3) For the existing tests, fixture-shape changes (seedOrganizationVariable wrote plaintext into the value column for is_secret=true rows) need updating IN PLACE rather than introducing a second helper — the new helper writes the encryption columns under the Plaintext provider's wire identifiers ("plaintext-v1" / "plaintext") for is_secret=true fixtures, so every legacy seedOrganizationVariable(..., true) call site keeps working. (4) Pair the fixture change with a package-level test helper (revealVariableValue) that projects OrganizationVariable.Value back to the plaintext for both shapes — for the Plaintext provider, ciphertext IS the plaintext bytes, so the helper is one branch (if IsSecret → string(SecretCiphertext) else v.Value). Tests that previously asserted v.Value == "expected" become revealVariableValue(v) == "expected" with no further restructuring. (5) ActorKind in audit-fed test inputs MUST be one of {"", "usr", "sa", "system"} — the audit_events.actor_kind CHECK constraint will reject "user" / "human" / any other value as a 23xxx that surfaces as a misleading "an audit event with this id already exists" via mapWriteError's canonical conflict message. The actual diagnostic is the actor_kind CHECK, not duplicate id. (6) When extracting Value/Plaintext assertions out of failing tests against a contract change, FIRST stash the working tree and re-run the failing tests on HEAD to separate "I introduced this failure" from "this was already failing"; the diff of failure name sets is the cleanest signal that the new code is at parity with the baseline. BE-0339 used this to confirm 23 of the 25 store-wide failures and 3 of the 12 org-variable failures were pre-existing. NOT applicable to BE-0343 (variable inheritance resolver) — that story consumes the at-rest seam through Provider.Open against multiple scopes simultaneously and needs its own pattern around the merge order + per-scope Open call site. NOT applicable to BE-0351 (secret encryption key rotation) — that story consumes the partial index organization_variables_secret_routing_idx + the KeyIDs() / ActiveKeyID() surface to enumerate rows referencing a retired key and re-Seal them, but the rotation worker is a separate operational concern from the at-rest write path this pattern owns.
- Per-service-type renderer-subtype contract pin (BE-0301 pattern, internal/controlplane/dokploy/renderer_application_git_test.go; structural template for BE-0303 application-image, BE-0305 application-drop-artifact, BE-0307 compose, BE-0309..0317 database engines, BE-0319 worker, BE-0321 cron — every `provisioning-service-type` PRD story whose durable provisioning worker / dokploy_refs / quota-conversion seam is deferred to a later worker story but whose declarative-content contract is owed today): single t.Parallel test file in package dokploy_test, anchored on two per-subtype input-helpers (applicationGitDockerfileInput / applicationGitNixpacksInput) that reuse the shared validInput()/fixedID()/mustRender() helpers from renderer_test.go so canonical-id + per-level secret fixtures stay in lockstep with every other renderer pin. Seven load-bearing pins per subtype: (1) subtype-identity happy path per builder variant (asserts Service.Type, Build.Builder, builder-specific fields preserved verbatim, and the subtype boundary — the foreign-builder-only field stays empty); (2) DropsXField subtype-boundary test that submits the foreign-builder field and proves both renderer-drop AND that the submitted value never appears in Summary JSON / slog record / Summary.String() — the structural barrier against the SIBLING subtype story (BE-0301 vs BE-0303 boundary: Image dropped for dockerfile/nixpacks; BE-0303 will mirror with a DropsGitField test pinning git_branch/commit/dockerfile_path drop for builder=image); (3) RoleMatrix across (web / worker / cron) × (dockerfile / nixpacks builder) — closure-captured builder name in `string(builderInput.Build.Builder)` keeps subtest names readable; (4) ValidationFailures table per subtype using stable wantField + per-row leakyValues — every leaked-value candidate the mutate() introduces is added to a shared leakyValues slice so the no-echo assertion runs against ALL submitted values per case, not just the row's own input; (5) TierResourceDefaults pin across (tier × role × builder) — pins the load-bearing 2-replica production web default + 1-replica everywhere-else default and proves the builder choice does NOT affect resource allocation; (6) RedactsAllVariableValuesAcrossRoles that asserts BOTH (a) the verbatim RenderedSpec carries the secret value the worker needs AND (b) every debug surface (Summary JSON, slog JSON record, Summary.String()) shows output.Sentinel for EVERY variable value — Secret-flagged AND plain — so a future logging path cannot turn the non-secret variable channel into an exfiltration vector; (7) Determinism per builder. The pattern is the renderer-layer counterpart to the engine-pin pattern used for admin-action policy matrices (BE-0285 / BE-0288 / BE-0291 / BE-0294 / BE-0297 / BE-0300) — a state-independent file that pins the contract the future worker-side story must continue to satisfy. The acceptance-criteria coverage map per story: AC1 (renderer supports + validates required fields) is pinned by the success + validation table; AC2 (provisioning worker + dokploy_refs atomic) defers to the worker story but the renderer-side determinism + drop-foreign-field invariants are the structural barrier the worker depends on; AC3 (quota reserved before enqueue) defers — already pinned generically by BE-0323's projectservice + quota.Checker integration; AC4 (fake Dokploy create/update/deploy/poll/failure/retry/replay) defers to the worker story; AC5 (yalla.output.v1 / yalla.error.v1 envelopes) is already pinned globally by apienvelope/apienvelope_test.go — the renderer file just confirms apierr.InvalidInput surfaces; AC6 (unit tests for success/validation/auth/not-found) is pinned at the renderer layer for success+validation, auth+not-found defer to the wire-endpoint story; AC7 (integration tests against migrated Postgres) is the worker story's surface; AC8 (secrets redacted in logs/errors/audit/test output) is pinned per-role per-builder by the RedactsAllVariableValuesAcrossRoles permutation. NOT applicable to subtypes whose subtype-boundary lives outside the dokploy renderer's BuildSettings switch (e.g. BE-0305 application-drop-artifact will need a new builder constant first and a sibling pin that mirrors but also pins the new builder's renderer contract; BE-0309..0317 database engines pin Engine instead of Builder and the role field is dropped — those will follow the database variant of this template).
- BE-0303 application-image confirms the inverted-boundary clone of the BE-0301 pattern (internal/controlplane/dokploy/renderer_application_image_test.go): a single-builder subtype (Builder == BuilderImage) collapses the BE-0301 builderCase outer loop to a single role-only loop, swaps DropsImageField for DropsGitFields (submits leaky dockerfile_path + git_branch + git_commit and asserts every one is dropped AND never appears in Summary JSON / slog record / Summary.String()), and adds the image-builder-missing-image case to the ValidationFailures table (the case BE-0301 cannot pin because git-source builders never require an Image). The leakyValues slice grows to include the rendered Image reference so an echoed image-builder error also fails. The renderer's normaliseBuild() switch already encodes both invariants — Image is required for BuilderImage and every git-source field is dropped — so BE-0303 ships test-only (no production code change) as a structural barrier against accidental weakening. The same single-builder collapse applies to future BE-0319 worker (Role fixed to RoleWorker, drops domains) and BE-0321 cron (Role fixed to RoleCron, drops domains, requires cron_schedule) sibling pins.
- BE-0319 worker is the FIRST role-axis clone of the BE-0301 pattern (internal/controlplane/dokploy/renderer_worker_test.go): when the per-PRD-story subtype identity is the Role (Role == RoleWorker) rather than Build.Builder, Service.Type, or Service.Engine, the renderer-subtype pin generalises with four structural swaps from the canonical Builder-axis template. (1) The two input helpers (workerApplicationInput / workerComposeInput) span the two ServiceType variants where the worker role applies (application + compose), mirroring how the BE-0301 helpers span two builder variants — the orthogonal axis becomes ServiceType because the role is now the fixed axis. Both helpers explicitly clear Domains and CronSchedule in their bases, so the "submit a foreign-axis value and prove the drop" assertion stays load-bearing. (2) The DropsXField pin (TestRenderWorkerDropsWebAndCronFields) submits BOTH a leaky domain host and a leaky cron schedule in one test, proving the worker drops TWO foreign-axis fields at once (web's Domains + cron's CronSchedule); the same Summary-JSON / slog-record / Summary.String() redaction sweep used by BE-0303 catches leaks of either value. This is the role-axis analogue of "git fields dropped for image builder" — the structural barrier against any future refactor that would weaken the silent drops at lines `cronSchedule = ""` and the "rendered only for web" Domains contract. (3) The BuilderMatrix subtest takes the place of the BE-0301 RoleMatrix: since Role is now the fixed axis, the orthogonal axes become (ServiceType × Builder) yielding 2×4=8 subtests that prove every supported builder works on every supported service type while preserving the worker shape (no domains, no cron, no replica bump). The check closure per builder stays mechanical — same pattern as BE-0303's single-builder verification but generalised to a four-builder set. (4) The ValidationFailures table deliberately OMITS the cron_schedule legs (missing schedule, bad schedule) because a worker is never a cron service — those legs are owned by the role's own pin (BE-0301/0303/0305/0307 already cover them via web-role inputs flipped to cron, and BE-0321 will own them on the cron-role side). The TierResourceDefaults pin shrinks from a 6-row (tier × {web, worker}) matrix to a 3-row (tier-only) matrix because the worker role is fixed; every row pins replicas=1, the INVERSE of BE-0301/BE-0307's production-web replica bump. Production code change: zero — the renderer already drops Domains and CronSchedule for non-web/non-cron roles. The role-axis pin is the FOURTH structural template in the renderer-subtype family after the Builder axis (BE-0301/0303/0305), the ServiceType axis (BE-0307), and the Engine axis (BE-0309..0317). BE-0321 (cron) will be the FIFTH role-axis variant, cloning this file with a 3-token swap (Worker→Cron in identifiers, RoleWorker→RoleCron, label value) plus one structural addition: a CronScheduleValidation leg in ValidationFailures, since the cron role IS subject to cron_schedule validation while the worker role is not — the inverse omission to the one this file documents.
- BE-0307 compose is the FIRST type-boundary clone of the BE-0301 pattern (internal/controlplane/dokploy/renderer_compose_test.go): when the per-PRD-story subtype identity is the ServiceType ITSELF (Service.Type == ServiceCompose) rather than the Build.Builder, the seven-pin template is preserved with three structural swaps. (1) Input helpers (composeDockerfileInput / composeNixpacksInput) carry the SAME two git builders as application-git — the boundary is NOT what the builder is — and the only difference vs applicationGit*Input is `in.Service.Type = dokploy.ServiceCompose`. (2) The Drops* test becomes a SubtypeBoundaryFromApplication test that renders BOTH composeDockerfileInput() AND applicationGitDockerfileInput() side-by-side and asserts each rendered Service.Type matches its input verbatim — neither is silently coerced — AND that the `yalla.service-type` label in spec.Service.Labels reflects the same value, because that label is the audit/observability surface a downstream consumer queries to distinguish a compose stack from a single-container application without re-reading the spec body; an alternate seam-coverage shape preserves the structural barrier when there is no foreign-builder-only field to drop. (3) The ValidationFailures table expands to cover EVERY builder's failure path that the subtype can reach — compose may use any of dockerfile/nixpacks/image/drop-artifact, so BE-0307's table includes BOTH the image-builder-missing-image case (from BE-0303) AND the drop-artifact-builder-missing-artifact-url case (from BE-0305) PLUS the bad-builder case — the leakyValues slice grows to carry the rendered Image AND ArtifactURL references so any echo from those branches fails too. The RoleMatrix / TierResourceDefaults / Redaction / Determinism pins keep the seven-pin shape intact, but RoleMatrix and the per-test invariants assert `Service.Type == ServiceCompose && Image == "" && ArtifactURL == "" && Engine == ""` (engine is database-only — that is the OTHER per-type seam BE-0309..0317 will pin). The load-bearing production-web 2-replica default participates here too: defaultResources() in renderer.go gates the bump on `(typ == ServiceApplication || typ == ServiceCompose)`, so TestRenderComposeTierResourceDefaults pins the compose half of that disjunction directly — a future regression that narrowed the disjunction to ServiceApplication-only would flip this pin. Forward-applicable to ANY future per-service-type subtype whose differentiator is the ServiceType itself (currently only compose vs application; future "function" / "edge" / similar would clone this template); NOT applicable to the BE-0309..0317 database engines, which pin Engine instead of either ServiceType or Builder, drop the role field entirely (effectiveRole := "" for ServiceDatabase in renderer.go:351), and need a database variant whose RoleMatrix collapses to a single (no-role) case and whose Engine-required + Image-dropped invariants supersede the Build.Builder switch's normalisation. The test-only-no-prod-code-change shape from BE-0303 is preserved — BE-0307 ships purely as a structural barrier against accidental weakening of the renderer's existing service-type discrimination.
- Real-quota concurrent oversubscription integration test (BE-0323 pattern, internal/controlplane/store/project_quota_concurrent_test.go; structural template for BE-0324..0338 — every other quota-dimension PRD story that needs to prove "parallel requests cannot oversubscribe the quota" against the dimension's owning Service.Create call): one Go test, t.Parallel, against testutil.RequireMigratedDB; wires a REAL *quota.Checker over a REAL *store.QuotaRepository + quota.StaticPlanResolver, and a REAL *store.<Resource>Service + REAL *store.AuditRepository, with the only fakes being the Authorizer and JobEnqueuer (recordingAuthorizer / recordingJobs from projectservice_test.go) which always succeed because their failure-path stories are covered elsewhere. Six load-bearing rules: (1) pre-seed quota_usage with used_value=0 for (org, dimension) BEFORE the race so the SELECT FOR UPDATE inside Checker.LockUsage acquires an existing row rather than racing inserts — the lock contract under test is row-lock serialisation, not row-creation; (2) seed quota_policies as scope_kind='plan_default' (not 'organization' override) so the plan-default fallback path inside QuotaRepository.EffectiveLimit is the one exercised — the org-override path has its own dedicated repository test (TestQuotaRepositoryEffectiveLimitPrefersOrgOverride); (3) launch attempts > limit goroutines (BE-0323 uses 20 attempts / limit 5 — 4:1 ratio gives a comfortable margin against any future pool-size or scheduling change without inflating runtime past ~0.5s); each goroutine generates its OWN canonical resource id via domain.MustNewID + a unique canonical slug fmt.Sprintf("p-%02d", i) so a slug conflict cannot disguise itself as a quota rejection; (4) assert successes == limit AND rejections == attempts - limit exactly, NOT >= / <= — the lock contract guarantees an exact split, and a "successes >= limit / <= attempts" range would silently let a regression through; (5) for EVERY rejection, assert all five ExceededDetail fields (Resource, Limit, Requested=1, Reserved==limit, Current==0) because at the moment the lock yields to a losing transaction every winning reservation is already committed — anything less than Reserved==limit means the lock did not serialise — and assert the diagnostic string never echoes any caller input (the i-indexed slug, display name, request id, or correlation id) so a future logging path cannot turn the error into a content channel; (6) post-race assertions cover three independent surfaces of the same invariant: raw count of projects rows for the org (must equal limit), raw count of active quota_reservations rows for the dimension (must equal limit), AND quotaRepo.SumActiveReservations through Store.Read (must equal limit) — the third surface catches a future regression where the table content diverges from the repository's view. Fake-call assertions pin step order at the unit-of-work level: authz.calls == attempts (every transaction reaches authorization) but jobs.calls == limit (rejected transactions never reach the JobEnqueuer because quota fails first and rolls back the whole tx). The dimension constant comes from the public store.QuotaResource* surface (BE-0323 uses store.QuotaResourceProjects) so a future rename surfaces as a compile error rather than a flaky test. NOT applicable to quota dimensions whose enforcement seam lives outside the *Service.Create unit of work (e.g. cpu_millicores / memory_mb / storage_gb where the dimension is summed across child resources — those need a different shape that exercises the dimension's actual enforcement gate). The CapDeploy concurrent_deployments dimension is the load-bearing precedent for "summed across rows" enforcement (DeploymentService.Create at deployment_service.go:209+691) and would clone this template by swapping the Service + dimension while keeping the six rules intact.
- testutil.Factory id-prefix gotcha (BE-0324 surfaced while cloning the BE-0323 pattern): the in-memory factory builds IDs with prefixes "prj"/"env"/"svc" but domain.KindProject is "proj" — the "prj_" form does NOT pass domain.ParseID. Tests that pass a factory Project.ID into an input which re-validates project_id (CreateEnvironmentInput, CreateServiceInput, etc.) get rejected with E_INVALID_INPUT. Workaround: seed parents with raw SQL using domain.MustNewID(domain.KindProject).String() (mirror seedDomainOrg). Owed: align the factory's id prefixes with the canonical domain.Kind values in a focused triage story.
- Race-safe local fakes for concurrent integration tests (BE-0324 pattern, internal/controlplane/store/environment_quota_concurrent_test.go atomicAuthorizer / atomicJobs): the shared recordingAuthorizer / recordingJobs / recordingQuota fakes in projectservice_test.go use plain int counters with no synchronisation, so the BE-0323-pattern 20-goroutine concurrent integration test trips the race detector against a live Postgres (BE-0323's TestProjectServiceCreateRejectsParallelOversubscriptionForProjectsQuota fails under -race for the same reason — a pre-existing issue documented under "Known pre-existing -race-with-DB failures" and owed to a focused triage story). For BE-0325..0338 (and any new concurrent integration test) define LOCAL race-safe fakes in the new test file: type atomicAuthorizer struct{ calls atomic.Int64 } satisfying the Authorizer port with calls.Add(1) on Authorize, and the equivalent atomicJobs for the JobEnqueuer port. Read counts with .Load() after wg.Wait(). Keeps the new test green under -race without touching the shared recording fakes or 80+ unrelated test files; the migration back to shared fakes belongs to the triage story when those are made atomic.
- Endpoint-pinned twin of an action-level engine-only policy matrix (BE-0288 pattern, internal/controlplane/policy/admin_dokploy_reconcile_endpoint_policy_test.go, sibling of BE-0285's admin_reconcile_policy_test.go): when two PRD stories cover two distinct WIRE ENDPOINTS that share the SAME action constant (admin.reconcile here — GET /v1/admin/dokploy/drift + POST /v1/admin/dokploy/reconcile), each story gets its own engine-only matrix file, structurally parallel but state-independent. Three load-bearing rules: (1) every canonical id (project / sibling / service-account principal) is renamed with the endpoint-distinguishing suffix so a future shared helper cannot accidentally couple the two matrices — BE-0288 uses canonicalAdminReconcileEndpointProjectID / canonicalAdminReconcileEndpointSiblingID and ServiceAccount IDs suffixed `_reconcile_endpoint`, deliberately distinct from BE-0285's `_reconcile` suffix; (2) docstrings frame the engine pin around the SPECIFIC endpoint's failure mode — BE-0285's file frames the action as "the contract admin.reconcile must satisfy regardless of which endpoint surfaces it" (action-level), BE-0288's file frames it as "the engine contract specifically for the mutating reconcile verb where an asymmetric regression that left listing intact but downgraded mutation capability cannot ship without flipping one of these expectations" (endpoint-level); (3) the test surface is structurally identical seven-function shape (Roles / Revoked&Expired / WrongOrg / Project / Env / Service / OrgGrant / ForeignHomeOrg) and verdict matrix is byte-identical to the action-level twin — the point of the duplication is endpoint-specific regression coverage, not behavioural difference at the engine seam. Applicable to any future PRD story pair where the wire endpoint differs but the policy action is shared (currently unique to admin.reconcile in BE-0285+0288; future similar pairs would clone this template). NOT applicable when two endpoints have distinct action constants — those follow the BE-0279/0282 sibling-action template instead, where the differentiator is the action's capability not the endpoint's role.
- Engine-only policy-matrix file pattern for CapSupport actions (BE-0285 admin.reconcile, applicable to admin.import / admin.read / admin.break_glass when their wire endpoints have not landed): same structural shape as the BE-0282 (job.cancel) CapDeploy template, but with three load-bearing flips: (1) role matrix collapses to one allow (Support) + five denies — the photo-negative of CapDeploy actions, (2) cross-tenant test flips Support from DENY (ReasonDeniedCrossTenant) to ALLOW (ReasonAllowedBySupport) because CapSupport sits INSIDE the engine's `required == CapRead || CapSupport` exception clause — the single most load-bearing distinction from BE-0279/0282 and the structural barrier against any future catalog drift that demoted admin.reconcile out of CapSupport, (3) grant-containment cases use RoleSupport for the "happy path" grant role and RoleAdmin for the "wrong capability" deny because only RoleSupport holds CapSupport at any role-grant combination. Resource Kind is KindOrganization with only Scope.OrganizationID pinned (admin actions operate on the source-of-truth view of an entire organization, no project/env/svc leg), so every project/env/service-scoped grant denies via ReasonDeniedOutOfScope (one-way covers()) — admin actions are unreachable through any scoped grant other than org-level Support. The foreign-home-org "stolen scoped key" test uses a ServiceAccount principal with empty Role and a foreign-org Support grant: the principal's empty `Role.roleCaps()` does NOT contain CapSupport, so the cross-tenant exception clause does NOT fire even though the grant nominally pins RoleSupport — empty Role is treated as "no role caps", NOT as ReasonDeniedUnknownRole, because the engine checks `if principal.Role != "" && !roleOK` before denying unknown roles. Canonical project id pair (`canonicalAdminReconcileProjectID` / `canonicalAdminReconcileSiblingID`) is deliberately distinct from sibling-file ids (`canonicalJobCancelProjectID`, etc.) so the read/retry/cancel/reconcile matrices cannot accidentally share state through a future shared helper.
- Operations artefact verification leaf (BE-0409 pattern, internal/controlplane/build/{doc.go, AGENTS.md, api_dockerfile_test.go}; structural template for BE-0410 worker Dockerfile, BE-0411 compose, BE-0412 k8s/Helm, BE-0413 systemd, BE-0414+ migration / seed-admin / backup / restore commands, BE-0418 config example files): canonical shape for ANY operations artefact (Dockerfile, docker-compose, k8s manifest, systemd unit, deploy script) the backend ships at the repo root. One Go test file per artefact in this package (api_dockerfile_test.go, worker_dockerfile_test.go, compose_test.go, ...), package `build_test` (external _test package) so the verification surface has no production-code dependency. Tests locate the artefact via repoRoot(t) which walks up from os.Getwd() until it finds go.mod — hard-coded relative paths break when the test moves. The verification surface is structural (regex over Dockerfile text, set-membership over .dockerignore lines, YAML parse + key lookup for compose/k8s) rather than a real `docker build` because the audit properties operations review cares about (non-root user, pinned tags, no baked secrets, EXPOSE matches the production listen address from config.ProfileProduction's apiAddr default) are textual, not behavioural. Forbidden-secret list MUST track config.Config's secret fields (DatabaseURL, SigningKeys, DokployToken) plus the most common database-side secret (POSTGRES_PASSWORD); extend it in lockstep when future config stories add new secret fields. ENV NAME=VAL, legacy `ENV NAME VAL`, and `ARG NAME=VAL with non-empty default` are ALL three banned forms — a developer who pastes `ARG YALLA_DOKPLOY_TOKEN=local-dev-token` into a Dockerfile fails this test in CI. Distroless static-debian12:nonroot is the canonical runtime image for any CGO_ENABLED=0 Go binary in this repo (UID/GID 65532, no shell, no package manager); HEALTHCHECK is intentionally omitted because the image has no curl/wget/sh — orchestrators probe /healthz and /readyz over HTTP directly. The BuildKit cache mounts (`--mount=type=cache,target=/go/pkg/mod` and `/root/.cache/go-build`) require the `# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1.7` directive at the top of the file; without that line the syntax silently falls back to legacy and the cache mounts become no-ops. GO_VERSION and RUNTIME_IMAGE are ARGs with pinned defaults so a downstream operator can override them without editing the file — and the verification test asserts the ARG defaults themselves are not :latest. The .dockerignore is documented as defence-in-depth, not an authorization boundary (secrets must never be checked in regardless); the required-exclusion set tested includes .git, .env, secrets/, *.pem, *.key. EXPOSE port is pinned to 8080 to match ProfileStaging/ProfileProduction's apiAddr default in internal/controlplane/config/load.go — drift here would force operators to read the source to know which port to map.

- Hard DELETE endpoint on a versioned bare-{id}-resolver child resource (BE-0244 pattern, DELETE /v1/services/{service_id}/domains/{domain_id}, store/service_domain.go ServiceDomainRepository.DeleteByID with optional If-Match + classifyServiceDomainConcurrencyMiss reuse, store/service_domain.go ServiceDomainService.Delete orchestrator (no in-tx Authorize — reserved for Create; structural-identifier-only audit metadata; no caller-body fields because a DELETE has none), httpapi/service_domains.go ServiceDomainDeleter port + deleteServiceDomainHandler (parseIfMatchVersion + 200 OK + snapshot payload — never 204, keeps wire shape uniform with the other service-domain endpoints), httpapi/routes.go DELETE entry with serviceIDResolver, contract suite at service_domains_delete_test.go, policy matrix at service_domains_delete_policy_test.go): canonical shape for any future bare-{id} DELETE on a versioned child where the row is removed outright (no soft-delete column, no scheduled-deletion stamp — the resource is a routing artefact, not a continuing audit-trail tie). The "deleter MUST never run on any deny path" assertion is the destructive-op counterpart of the updater-not-reached invariant — more load-bearing for DELETE because a row destroyed in the background while the wire reports 403 is the worst possible failure mode. Mechanically clonable from the PATCH twin (BE-0241+0242+0243) by s/Update/Delete/ + s/update/delete/ + s/Patcher/Deleter/ + action swap.
- Port-arity sweep tooling (BE-0244 mechanical refinement of the BE-0175 ALL-FOUR-FORMS rule): when bumping NewHandler's arity by one positional port, the cleanest mechanical sweep across every test's NewHandler call site is `perl -i -pe 's/fakePREVIOUS\{\},/fakePREVIOUS{}, fakeNEW{},/g' $(grep -rl 'fakePREVIOUS{}' internal/controlplane/httpapi/)` keyed on the IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING fake type literal. BE-0244 sweep updated 69 test files in one pass. The single non-literal call site (a `var, fakeService...` pattern where the previous port is bound to a local variable rather than the bare struct literal) is fixed by hand with one extra perl. Then `go build ./...` confirms the arity matches end-to-end; the new fake type itself is declared once in the new test file (here: fakeServiceDomainDeleter in service_domains_delete_test.go) and is visible to every test file in the same package.
- Repository tenant-isolation for a tenant-root table (BE-0426 pattern, internal/controlplane/store/organization_tenant_isolation_test.go; structural template for BE-0428/0430/0432/0434/0436 and every future tenant-root-table isolation story): the strongest isolation guarantee in the codebase lives on the row-id-keyed tenant root (organizations) and the proof shape is "byte-identical snapshot of the OTHER tenant across every mutation path the repository exposes". Skeleton: one Go test file per table, one t.Parallel test per (mutation × leg) — Get returns-only-named-tenant + Get unknown-id-is-NotFound (cross-tenant + missing render the same yerr.CodeNotFound — no oracle); Update only-touches-named-tenant (snapshot orgB, Update orgA, re-read orgB, assert byte-identical across slug, display_name, version, updated_at, deletion_scheduled_at; assert orgA's update DID land so a no-op repository can't pass trivially); Update-with-mismatched-If-Match also-does-not-touch-orgB (catches "fall back to unconditional UPDATE on stale" regressions); ScheduleDeletion only-touches-named-tenant (stamp on orgA, orgB byte-identical incl. DeletionScheduledAt == nil); Get-of-soft-deleted-tenant-does-not-mask-other (soft-delete is per-row, not SQL-level hide; the scheduled row is still readable and orgB unchanged); Insert enforces-global-slug-uniqueness (typed yerr.CodeConflict + non-empty user-facing Message; first row's slug unchanged; second row's id is yerr.CodeNotFound on follow-up Get — the failed Insert lands no row). Three load-bearing rules: (1) anchor on BOTH version (trigger-bumped on every UPDATE so a missing WHERE bumps every row) AND updated_at (trigger-refreshed; same property) — either one catches a WHERE-less UPDATE independently of the other, keep both; (2) the "stale-If-Match" leg is structurally distinct from the "successful update" leg and exercises the conflict-detection path which historically falls back to extra reads/writes that could leak across tenants; (3) Insert conflict-message assertions anchor on yerr.CodeConflict + non-empty Message ONLY, never on a substring (the static "an organization with this slug already exists" message is a stable contract but story-specific prose checks are brittle). Tenant-root tables have NO ListByParent method at this layer (no parent to scope by) — the "list queries don't leak total counts" acceptance criterion is vacuously satisfied for tenant-root tables; the corresponding proof for /v1/me/organizations lives in membership tests. Document this absence in the test file's package-doc comment so a future reader does not look for a missing test. CHILD-TABLE variant (BE-0428+ for users/memberships/projects/environments/services/api_keys/etc.) extends this skeleton with one additional leg: a cross-tenant parent_id probe — passing org A's parent_id (project_id, etc.) alongside org B's organization_id must render NotFound, NEVER A's row, NEVER a 500 leaking the cause. Use docker compose up -d postgres + YALLA_TEST_DATABASE_URL=postgres://yalla:yalla@127.0.0.1:5432/yalla go test -race -count=1 -run 'TestXxxRepository' to verify; the suite skips cleanly when the env var is unset, so CI without Postgres remains green. Known pre-existing -race-with-DB failures in environment-service / api-key-service Create paths and organization_variable_patch audit metadata are NOT introduced by this pattern (confirmed by stashing the new test file and re-running each failing case); a focused triage story should pick them up before BE-0500+ verification stories run.
- Operator-driven health probe (BE-0039 pattern, internal/controlplane/backup/{doc.go, AGENTS.md, health.go, health_test.go} + httpapi/routes.go GET /healthz/backup + docs/operations/backup-restore.md): canonical shape for ANY unauthenticated probe that surfaces operator-written state the Yalla process did not produce itself — database backup timestamp, WAL position, replication lag, external queue depth, cloud-bucket presence, certificate expiry, etc. Layout: a LEAF package under internal/controlplane that owns the parsing + redaction contract (Status struct + Reporter interface + a concrete FileReporter and an Unconfigured() helper); a single new entry in newRouteTable with tagOperations + a stable operationId (getHealthzBackup mirrors getHealthz/getReadyz/getVersion); a wire-DTO struct with omitempty pointers for every optional field so the four wire-shape variants (configured-and-healthy / configured-and-stale / configured-but-empty-sentinel / unconfigured) share one shape. Five load-bearing rules: (1) the leaf reads exactly one external resource — a path or URL the operator supplied via a YALLA_* env var; never reads the database, never invokes Dokploy, never logs the source content; (2) error messages from the leaf name the configured path or url but never echo the source's content (a status file accidentally seeded with a secret cannot leak through the leaf's parse-error string, pinned by a TestFileReporterParseErrorRedactsContent-style test); (3) the HTTP handler never echoes the reporter's error message in the wire response either — it forwards a stable handler-side message via apienvelope.WriteErrorStatus(yerr.CodeUnavailable, ...) and the redaction proof lives in a TestXxxErrorMessageDoesNotLeakReporterError test on the http side; (4) a sentinel "configured but no value yet" path (ErrNoBackupRecorded shape) renders 200 with configured=true + fresh=false + a human-readable detail string — a freshly provisioned environment is healthy, it just hasn't fired its first event yet; (5) an unconfigured Reporter renders 200 with configured=false (NOT 404) so operators can wire the integration later without restarting clients that already probe the route. The four BE-acceptance-criteria slots map onto the new endpoint as: success = source returns a value; validation failure = wrong HTTP method (router-driven 404/405; the BE-0039 "no input to validate" version of a validation test); authorization failure = explicit unauthenticated-with-and-without-bearer-header test that fails loudly if a future regression wraps the route in RequireAuth; not-found behavior = the sentinel path (configured but no value yet recorded). Config layer gains TWO env vars per probe — a YALLA_XXX_PATH/URL (string, optional, must be absolute when set) and a YALLA_XXX_MAX_AGE (Go duration, optional, ≥ 0) — with Validate rejecting a relative path and the RedactedConfig+LogValue+String chain surfacing the non-secret fields. NewHandler grows ONE positional port (Reporter backup.Reporter or similar) at the head of the operational-args block (after meta, before authenticator); a nil Reporter is rewritten to Unconfigured() inside NewHandler so every test path still serves the route. The positional-arg sweep across ~60 test files is dominated by three Python regexes anchored on the common test helpers (`nil, nil, a, policy.NewEngine()` literal-a, `nil, nil, AuthIdent{}, policy.NewEngine()` struct-literal-auth, multi-line `nil, nil, a,\n\t\tpolicy.NewEngine()`); the all-nils newRouteTable shape tests bump by one nil; the bootstrap-endpoints list test in server_test.go adds the new path. The runbook in docs/operations/ is part of the deliverable — it pins the SLO (frequency, retention, RTO/RPO, encryption), the operator-pipeline handshake (the exact file format + atomic-rename write contract), the four wire-shape variants the probe emits, and the rehearsal procedure for staging. Forward-applicable to every future operator-driven health probe (queue depth, replication lag, certificate expiry, cloud-bucket presence, archive freshness, license validity, KMS key health).
- Cross-cutting policy package = retention-shaped leaf (BE-0038 pattern, internal/controlplane/retention/{doc.go, AGENTS.md, policy.go, policy_test.go}, third instance of the pure-package layout after reconcile and migrateimport): canonical shape for ANY cross-cutting authority over a closed-set domain enum + a validated config + boundary-style predicates — retention windows, rate-limit tiers, idempotency horizons, audit-redaction policies, plan-limit ladders, etc. Layout: doc.go (boundary + the invariants the predicates encode), policy.go (closed-set ResourceKind + a Window struct of just-durations + an immutable Policy value with a private map; DefaultPolicy() returning the production values + NewPolicy(map) that validates every kind is present and every Window passes validate() + copies the input map so caller mutation cannot tamper with a live Policy + Window/Restorable/RestorableAt/RestoreDeadline/RemainingRestore/ReapableAt/ReapDeadline/AllowsSlugReuse predicates over (kind, stampedAt, now)), policy_test.go (every kind × every transition + boundary case + zero-value-Policy safety + NewPolicy validation table + caller-mutation defense + cross-predicate coherence (restorable → held → reapable monotone) + closed-set guard via AllKinds()), AGENTS.md (boundary + invariants). Three load-bearing rules: (1) the boundary comparisons MUST be strict-less-than at the upper bound of RestorableAt and `>=` at the lower bound of ReapableAt so the two predicates are mutually exclusive at the exact instant of transition (a row never reports as both restorable and reapable at the same nanosecond); (2) the package is a LEAF — it imports only std-lib (time, fmt, sort, errors-only-from-tests) and is imported by store/httpapi/worker, so its predicates are cheap to call from anywhere without dragging a database or network dependency along; never let retention import apierr/store/audit; (3) "soft delete where safe" in the BE-0038 description is a real qualifier — memberships do not get a soft-delete column because role_version invalidates sessions at the auth layer and audit_events outlives the resource via the organization-level cascade, so KindMembership.SoftDeleteColumn() returns "" and Policy.SupportsSoftDelete(KindMembership) is false by design (a future schema migration that adds a removed_at column to memberships must update both in lock-step, and the closed-set test will fail until they do). Two follow-up wirings the package was designed for but does not yet require: a future teardown worker (BE-0203+) iterates retention.AllKinds(), looks up each kind's SoftDeleteColumn(), scans rows where the column is non-NULL and the stamp is older than ReapAfter, and calls the kind-specific hard-delete repository method; a future CapAdmin admin-purge endpoint calls retention.Policy.AllowsSlugReuse before bypassing the wait — the slug-reuse predicate is the contract those two consumers will share. Forward-applicable to every future cross-cutting policy module (plan tiers, audit redaction horizons, idempotency-key TTL, rate-limit ramp).
- Pure orchestrator / workflow package = reconcile-shaped vertical (BE-0033 pattern, internal/controlplane/migrateimport/{doc.go, AGENTS.md, types.go, importer.go, importer_test.go}, the second instance of this shape after internal/controlplane/reconcile): canonical shape for ANY workflow that ingests external state, classifies it, and writes through ports — Dokploy import, drift reconciliation, billing reconciliation, compliance scanning, lifecycle teardown, etc. Package layout: doc.go (boundary + plan/apply + dry-run + redaction sections), AGENTS.md (conventions), types.go (every port interface PLUS every value type those interfaces reference — Scanner/Repository ports, Snapshot/Existing*/Create*Input value types, OwnerAssignment, PlanItem and Plan with stable JSON tags because the Plan IS the dry-run yalla.output.v1 payload; ItemStatus + ItemReason as the closed classification surface), importer.go (Config with Scanner + Repository + Logger + Now + Redactor; New() returns apierr.Internal on a missing port; Plan(ctx, in) is pure and never writes; Apply(ctx, plan) is best-effort and collects per-item failures in Result.Failures with redacted error strings; classify*() helpers are unit-testable in isolation; wrap{Scanner,Repository}Err() preserves catalogued apierr.* codes and upgrades untyped errors to apierr.DokployUnavailable (scanner) / apierr.StoreUnavailable (repository) / apierr.Internal (defensive contract assertions); a resolvedParents map seeded with the org-root entry lets the apply loop resolve child-after-parent in a single pass through the hierarchy-ordered items). The test file houses an in-package fakeScanner + fakeRepo with concurrent-safe mutexes and call recording, and covers: construction port validation (one nil per case → CodeInternal); Plan input validation (every required field, every kind/format check → CodeInvalidInput with the named field recoverable via apierr.ViolationsOf); the dry-run-doesn't-query-Repository contract (no-assignment Plan never calls the repo); every classification Status × Reason combination as a positive case (StatusReady / StatusSkipDuplicate / StatusSkipMissingParent / StatusSkipUnsupported / StatusSkipAlreadyImported / StatusPendingOwner); Scanner failure surfaces as the right apierr code (DokployUnavailable → yerr.CodeServer, NOT CodeUnavailable — that's for Yalla-owned dependencies); Repository failure preserves catalogued codes; secrets redacted in error strings AND in log buffer (slog over a bytes.Buffer, output.NewRedactor(secret), assert secret never appears); Apply persists in hierarchy order (organization → project → environment → service, asserted by scanning the recorded calls slice for ordering invariants); Apply continues past per-item failures (inject failServiceByDokployID for one specific service create, prove sibling creates still succeeded); Apply ctx-cancellation propagates (errors.Is(err, context.Canceled)); Apply on no-ready-items is a valid no-op accounting Skipped count. The Plan JSON shape is PUBLIC compatibility contract before the customer-facing endpoint even exists — stable field names, no pointers in PlanItem, no embedded interfaces, no time.Time on the wire — because the eventual POST endpoint (BE-0289 et al) serialises it as-is. Canonical test fixture ID format: kind prefix + "_" + 26-char Crockford base32 lowercase suffix from "0123456789abcdefghjkmnpqrstvwxyz" (no i, l, o, u); use "org_01hz00000000000000000000xx" style (4-char prefix + 20 zeros + 2-char tag = 26) — the testutil factory's IDs are deliberately non-canonical for some tests and will fail strict ParseID. Slug derivation goes one-way: domain.NormalizeSlug(dokployName) for the Dokploy → Yalla direction (a NormalizeSlug rejection is itself a classification, NOT an error to propagate); domain.DokployName(label, yallaID) is the OPPOSITE direction and must not be reused here. supportedServiceType(svc) AND-s dokploy.ServiceType.Valid() with the database-requires-engine rule and collapses both failure modes into a single StatusSkipUnsupported reason — the operator's remediation is the same. Reconcile and migrateimport are siblings under this pattern; future "resource lifecycle worker", "drift admin reconciler", "billing reconciler" packages should reuse the package layout verbatim.
- POST sub-action endpoint on a deep resource by bare id (BE-0163 pattern, POST /v1/environments/{environment_id}/clone, store/environmentservice.go EnvironmentService.Clone + CloneEnvironmentInput + validateCloneEnvironmentInput, httpapi/environments.go cloneEnvironmentHandler + EnvironmentCloner): canonical shape for ALL sub-action POSTs on a bare-id route (clone, restart, rollback, cancel, restore, etc.). The path carries the SOURCE id and a verb suffix, and the resolver pins only (OrganizationID, ID) — scoped grants pinning ProjectID are denied by covers() (one-way containment, the same boundary GET/PATCH/DELETE inherit on the bare-id route family). The structural parent_id of the new row (project_id for env.clone, etc.) is DERIVED FROM THE SOURCE ROW inside the same tx, NEVER from the body or path — the request body strictly omits the parent_id field, and the strict decoder rejects any caller who tries to supply one (proven by an explicit RejectsUnknownField contract test). The service-layer orchestrator composes Create-style steps PLUS a source-row read at the front PLUS a lifecycle-state guard before any write: read source under (orgID, sourceID) → reject DeletionScheduledAt != nil as Conflict (a lifecycle-dead row is not a valid source) → in-tx Authorize → Quota.Reserve → Repository.Insert (the new row inherits source.ProjectID) → JobEnqueue → Audit.Append with Metadata{"slug","project_id","cloned_from": source.ID} (the cloned_from / restored_from / rolled_back_to entry records non-secret structural provenance — the audit trail's only handle on "where did this row come from"). Reuse the EXISTING action constant rather than minting a sub-action one (environment.create on a clone route, not environment.clone): the PRD-mandated action is the same CapWrite, same role matrix, same grant containment, and a new action constant would force a sweep of the action catalog, builtinRoleCaps, every policy matrix test, and the OpenAPI surface for zero contract benefit. The HTTP handler reuses environmentIDResolver (the bare-id family's shared resolver), returns 201 Created (a Create-style sub-action), and mirrors row.Version into the ETag header via writeOrganizationETag. Service-level tests MUST seed with seedDomainOrg / seedDomainProject / seedDomainEnvironment helpers (canonical 26-char-suffix IDs via domain.MustNewID — the testutil factory's IDs are deliberately non-canonical and the service's strict ParseID validation correctly rejects them); repository-level tests can use either helper. - PATCH endpoint for a deep resource by bare id (BE-0157 pattern, PATCH /v1/environments/{environment_id}, store/environment.go EnvironmentRepository.Update + classifyEnvironmentConcurrencyMiss, store/environmentservice.go EnvironmentService.Update + buildEnvironmentUpdate, httpapi/environments.go updateEnvironmentHandler): canonical shape for ALL deep-resource PATCH endpoints. Repository.Update takes a fully-formed row + *int64 ifMatchVersion, runs a tenant-scoped (organization_id, id) UPDATE that touches only the mutable columns (slug, display_name — NEVER the composite tenant key), and classifies a zero-row return via a classify*ConcurrencyMiss helper that disambiguates gone-vs-stale by Get-in-same-tx. The service-layer orchestrator runs the validation BEFORE the transaction is opened (buildXxxUpdate is split out for unit-testability, rejects empty patches as 400, never echoes submitted values in violations), then in ONE Store.Write: read current row, check If-Match pre-condition (stale -> ConflictStale with row's authoritative version BEFORE the version-checked UPDATE — even a trivial no-op patch with stale If-Match surfaces the conflict), apply patch in-memory, call Repository.Update, append audit row. UNLIKE Create, the orchestrator does NOT invoke the in-tx Authorizer or QuotaReserver — the HTTP RequireAuth gate is authoritative for the update path; the in-tx Authorize is reserved for Create's defence-in-depth against grant-change races during quota reservation. The HTTP handler reuses the shared parseIfMatchVersion + writeOrganizationETag helpers (yes, the helper is org-named but it is the SHARED chokepoint for every endpoint mirroring versions to ETag — do not duplicate it per resource family). Body is strictly decoded with `slug *string` and `display_name *string` (pointer nil-ness IS the partial-update contract); the body intentionally exposes no organization_id/parent_id/self_id field — tenant isolation is structural. Response is yalla.output.v1 carrying the same wire shape GET returns, plus ETag header. Path with NO parent_id (bare-id route): the resource scope pins only OrganizationID + the deep id, so the engine's covers() rule DENIES every scoped grant at the policy boundary (a grant with a pinned ProjectID cannot cover a resource with no ProjectID); principals whose only access is a scoped grant must use a parent-scoped route. Every NewHandler positional-arg addition triggers a ~50-site sweep across ~35 existing test files — anchor on `fakeXxxReader{}, nil)` and `fakeXxxReader{}, logger)` plus the `reader, nil)` / `reader, logger)` outliers in the resource's own get/policy test helpers. - DELETE endpoint for a deep resource by bare id (BE-0160 pattern, DELETE /v1/environments/{environment_id}, migration 0016_environment_deletion_schedule, store/environment.go EnvironmentRepository.ScheduleDeletion, store/environmentservice.go EnvironmentService.ScheduleDeletion + DeleteEnvironmentInput, httpapi/environments.go deleteEnvironmentHandler + EnvironmentDeleter): canonical shape for ALL deep-resource SOFT-delete endpoints. The migration is structurally identical to 0013_project_deletion_schedule — `ALTER TABLE <resource> ADD COLUMN deletion_scheduled_at timestamptz` + a partial index `WHERE deletion_scheduled_at IS NOT NULL` for the future teardown-worker scan. The repository ScheduleDeletion is an SQL-IDEMPOTENT unconditional UPDATE stamping `deletion_scheduled_at = now()` returning the row in column order (so callers see the trigger-refreshed updated_at + bumped version); the already-scheduled distinction is the service's job (the repository must remain SQL-idempotent for non-customer callers — workers, admin jobs — that retry). ifMatchVersion uses the SAME pattern as Update — nil disables, non-nil adds `AND version = $N` to the WHERE — and classify*ConcurrencyMiss disambiguates the no-rows case (gone vs stale) by Get-in-same-tx. The service-layer orchestrator validates blank-input BEFORE opening the tx (typed InvalidInput, missing actor org is Internal — wiring error, never client input), then in ONE Store.Write: read current row, check If-Match pre-condition (stale -> ConflictStale BEFORE the already-scheduled check, so a stale caller learns version-stale instead of an already-scheduled message that races with concurrent edits they did not see), reject already-scheduled as apierr.Conflict (rolls the whole tx back so the audit record can never name a deletion that did not change resource state), call Repository.ScheduleDeletion, record the resolved deletion_scheduled_at stamp as audit metadata (`event.Metadata["deletion_scheduled_at"] = row.DeletionScheduledAt.UTC().Format(time.RFC3339Nano)` — a non-secret timestamp, safe to record verbatim), append audit row. UNLIKE Create, the orchestrator does NOT invoke the in-tx Authorizer or QuotaReserver — the HTTP RequireAuth gate is authoritative for the delete path; the in-tx Authorize is reserved for Create's defence-in-depth against grant-change races during quota reservation. The HTTP handler reuses parseIfMatchVersion + writeOrganizationETag + telemetry.FromContext for correlation; returns 202 Accepted (the scheduling is durable but the destructive teardown is a later worker job). The wire DTO (projectEnvironment / projectResource) gains a `DeletionScheduledAt *string \`json:"deletion_scheduled_at,omitempty"\`` field so a live row's JSON shape is byte-identical to before (omitempty + nil pointer = field absent), while a scheduled row exposes the stamp as RFC 3339 — mirror this on every resource DTO that gains a soft-delete column. Run `go vet ./...` AFTER each sweep — Go's positional-arg compile error tells you exactly which call sites the regex missed. The store-side integration tests cover repo happy-path + NotFound + tenant-scoped + nil-tx-rejection plus service happy-path-with-audit + already-scheduled-rolls-back-AND-stamp-unchanged-AND-only-one-audit-row + NotFound-no-audit + tenant-scoped-no-audit + stale-If-Match + blank-input + missing-actor-org. - New top-level resource family that already has its persistence table from an earlier migration (BE-0148 pattern, environments table from 0002 + version column from 0011, store/environment.go, httpapi/project_environments.go): a reader-only scoped-child vertical lands JUST the GET endpoint and pairs with the existing table — NO new migration. Crucially, environments carry NO credential material (the table stores only id, organization_id, project_id, slug, display_name, version, created_at, updated_at) so the HTTP projection (projectEnvironmentOf) needs no value-redaction chokepoint — every field is structural — but the projection STILL exists as a single chokepoint so a future column added to store.Environment is reviewed for its wire exposure here rather than leaking by default. The integration tests (store/environment_test.go) prove ordering, tenant scoping (a cross-tenant (orgA, projB_id) pair yields no rows), the empty-project shape (non-nil empty slice), the reader's project existence check, and that a cross-tenant id surfaces as apierr.NotFound WITHOUT leaking any of the foreign tenant's environment id / project id / slug into the error message. The HTTP layer adds a new operation tag (tagEnvironments = "environments") because environments will get their own /v1/environments/{environment_id} surface later; the list endpoint is tagged [tagProjects, tagEnvironments] mirroring how project_variables uses [tagProjects, tagVariables]. NewHandler and newRouteTable signatures each grow ONE positional port (projectEnvironments ProjectEnvironmentReader at the TAIL of the arg list, after projectVariableReplacer); cmd/yalla-api/main.go wires *store.EnvironmentReader at startup. A Python regex sweep over 33 test files anchored on `fakeProjectVariableReplacer{}, nil)` -> `fakeProjectVariableReplacer{}, fakeProjectEnvironmentReader{}, nil)` (44 sites) plus a second sweep on `fakeProjectVariableReplacer{}, logger)` (server_test.go + me_contract_test.go) plus the named-replacer outlier `fakeProjectVariableReader{}, replacer, nil)` -> `..., replacer, fakeProjectEnvironmentReader{}, nil)` (project_variables_test.go's replaceProjectVariablesHandlerFor) plus the openapi-only newRouteTable form `fakeProjectVariableReader{}, fakeProjectVariableReplacer{})` -> `..., fakeProjectEnvironmentReader{})` (project_variables_test.go's BE-0142 OpenAPI test) handled the NewHandler/newRouteTable churn (54 sites total). The all-nil newRouteTable form with 32 nils received one trailing nil to become 33 (6 sites). projects_delete_test.go + projects_restore_test.go newRouteTable calls ended `fakeProjectGrantReader{}, nil, nil, nil)` and got one MORE trailing nil to become `nil, nil, nil, nil)`. The KindEnvironment domain Kind ("env") already existed and is in the valid-kinds map from earlier work; no domain/id.go changes were needed. Forward-applicable to every future reader-only vertical on a hierarchy resource whose table predates the story.
- env.read-on-{project_id}-resolver policy matrix (BE-0144, internal/controlplane/httpapi/projects_variables_get_policy_test.go) is the structural sibling of the project.grants.read-on-{project_id}-resolver matrix (BE-0138, projects_grants_policy_test.go) — same CapRead capability class, same projectIDResolver scope (`{principal home org, path project_id}`), same six-roles-all-allow matrix via ReasonAllowedByRole, same support cross-tenant exception at the engine (ReasonAllowedBySupport — pinned even though projectIDResolver structurally blocks it on the customer-facing wire), same engine cross-tenant deny matrix for non-support roles, same scoped-grant containment shape (sibling project denied, env-/service-scoped grants denied against the project resource, org-level Viewer grant allowed via ReasonAllowedByGrant). The load-bearing distinction is the wire-redaction chokepoint: project_variables rows carry credential material (a non-null Value that flips to output.Sentinel when IsSecret), so the deny-body leak guard (variablesDenyBodyLeak) anchors on BOTH structural identifiers (canonical project/var ids, keys, non-secret values) AND the seeded secret plaintext (canonicalVariablesSecretPlaintext). project_grants rows store no credential material, so grantsDenyBodyLeak omits a plaintext anchor. The allow-path test also asserts secret rows project as output.Sentinel and that the seeded plaintext never appears in the response body — pinning projectVariableOf as the chokepoint independent of how authority was earned (role / org-level grant / project-level grant). Forward-applicable to every future env.read matrix that resolves into a project-, env-, or service-level scope on a variables route: keep the role / disabled / wrong-org / grant-containment skeleton, swap the action+resolver for the new endpoint's, and ALWAYS add a secret-plaintext needle to the leak guard plus a Sentinel-projection assertion to every allow-path tie-in.
- environment.read-on-bare-{environment_id}-resolver policy matrix (BE-0156, internal/controlplane/httpapi/environments_get_policy_test.go) is the structural sibling of the {project_id}-resolver siblings (BE-0144 env.read on the variables route, BE-0150 environment.read on the parent-scoped route) for endpoints that use a BARE-ID resolver (environmentIDResolver, future serviceIDResolver / deploymentIDResolver). TWO load-bearing distinctions from the projectIDResolver siblings. (1) The resolver pins NO ProjectID leg on the resource scope (`policy.Scope{OrganizationID: principal.home, EnvironmentID: r.PathValue("environment_id")}`), so the engine's one-way Scope.covers() rule (internal/controlplane/policy/policy.go) denies EVERY scoped grant at the boundary via ReasonDeniedOutOfScope — project-scoped, env-scoped, AND service-scoped grants all DENY on this route, even when the grant names the target environment's own id or the target environment's own parent project, because the grant scope pins ProjectID and the resource scope does not. The acceptance criteria's three containment properties (sibling project not reached / staging-grant-doesn't-imply-production / service-grant-shields-parent-env-secrets) are still pinned at the engine against their natural resources (project / env / service Resource), but the wire tie-in INVERTS the projectIDResolver shape: instead of "project-scoped grant on target ALLOWS, sibling DENIES," every scoped-key type DENIES with ReasonDeniedOutOfScope on this route and only org-wide roles + the org-level grant allow. The org-level Viewer grant remains the load-bearing ALLOW because its grant scope pins nothing past OrganizationID — covers() matches a resource without ProjectID. Pin a "grant on the SAME environment id as the path names" engine-level deny too, so a future relaxation of covers() (e.g. admitting `Scope{EnvironmentID: env_X}` to cover `Resource{Scope{EnvironmentID: env_X}}` regardless of ProjectID) cannot land without failing this test. (2) The support cross-tenant exception is suppressed on the wire by construction — environmentIDResolver pins OrganizationID to principal.home — so the support cross-tenant ALLOW only fires at the engine layer against a hand-built foreign-org Resource. The wire-level "wrong organization" probe surfaces as 404 E_NOT_FOUND from the tenant-scoped GetByID query (never 403, which would confirm existence), and the body must not echo the foreign org id. The contract-test helper bakes in a single canonical principal (getEnvironmentHandlerFor takes `t, reader` only, with authForEnvGet's hardcoded principal), so this matrix introduces a per-test identity-injected helper LOCAL to the policy file (getEnvironmentByIDHandlerForIdentity, signature `(id auth.Identity, authErr error, reader EnvironmentReader) http.Handler`) modelled on listProjectsHandlerFor / listProjectEnvironmentsHandlerFor — adding the helper locally avoids modifying the 9 contract tests that already use the simpler form. ACTION-CONSTANT gotcha to pin: routes.go:574 sets `RequiredAction: string(policy.ActionEnvironmentRead)` for this route, NOT `policy.ActionEnvRead` — both are CapRead per catalog.go but they're different catalog entries (env-vars vs env entity); mixing them up silently swaps which catalog row a future tier-upgrade watches. Forward-applicable to every future bare-id matrix on a deep resource (service.read on /v1/services/{service_id}, deployment.read on /v1/deployments/{deployment_id}, etc).
- environment.read-on-{project_id}-resolver policy matrix (BE-0150, internal/controlplane/httpapi/projects_environments_get_policy_test.go) is the structural sibling of the env.read matrix at the same resolver (BE-0144) with TWO narrowings worth pinning because the persistence row carries NO credential material: (1) drop the secret-plaintext deny-body leak anchor — environmentsDenyBodyLeak anchors ONLY on canonical structural identifiers (project id/slug/display_name + per-env id/slug/display_name) because the environments table has nothing that needs redaction; (2) drop the "secret row still projects as output.Sentinel even when authority came via a project-level or org-level grant" allow-path assertion — projectEnvironmentOf has no value-redaction chokepoint to anchor. Forward-applicable to every future CapRead-on-{X}-resolver matrix where the underlying row carries no credential material (org_grants, members, audit_events, etc.): keep the four-test skeleton, swap action+resource Kind, and drop the secret-plaintext anchor + Sentinel-projection assertion.
- CapAdmin-on-{project_id}-resolver policy matrix (BE-0141, internal/controlplane/httpapi/projects_grants_put_policy_test.go) is the structural sibling of the CapWrite-on-{project_id}-resolver matrix (projects_delete_policy_test.go) but ONE TIER UP — Developer JOINS the deny set at the role boundary (it holds CapWrite, not CapAdmin) and the org-level Developer grant flips from ALLOW for project.delete to DENY for project.grants.write. The load-bearing pair is org-level Admin grant ALLOW + org-level Developer grant DENY: that pair locks the CapAdmin requirement against the grant path so a future catalog change that downgraded project.grants.write to CapWrite would still pass the allow check but fail the deny check (silently letting every developer key rewrite a project's authority), and the regression direction is documented as a structural test, not only catalog assertion. The cross-tenant engine matrix DENIES every role including Support (CapAdmin is OUTSIDE the engine clause `roleCaps.has(CapSupport) && (required == CapRead || required == CapSupport)`); the CapRead-on-{project_id}-resolver siblings (project.grants.read at BE-0138 etc) ALLOW Support cross-tenant via ReasonAllowedBySupport — pinning the same-shape distinction in both directions documents that read-vs-write is the load-bearing axis for the support exception. Mutating-policy-matrix tests carry TWO directions of leak guard: a request-body leak guard (replaceGrantsRequestBodyLeak, anchored on distinctive caller-supplied identifiers like usr_request_matrix that NEVER appear in the canonical fixture data) and a would-have-returned-data leak guard (grantsDenyBodyLeak, anchored on canonical fixture data the fake replacer would return on an allow path) — used together on every deny path so a future renderer that gained either a "render request body on error" or "render would-have-returned data on 403" mode fails here. A read endpoint needs only the second; a write endpoint needs both. CI must be listed EXPLICITLY in both the per-role deny rows and the cross-tenant engine deny loop, because CapDeploy (which CI holds) is its own axis — neither CapWrite nor CapAdmin. The "scoped key planted in a foreign home org" engine assertion (a principal whose home org is org_sibling but whose grant scope still names a project in org_acme, authorized against org_sibling's resource) is independent of CapAdmin/CapWrite/CapRead — the engine refuses to consider the grant at all because the principal's OrganizationID no longer matches the grant scope's OrganizationID. Pin this on every grant-containment test so a stolen scoped key documentedly cannot be smuggled across tenants by anyone who finds it.
- env.write-on-{project_id}-resolver policy matrix (BE-0147, internal/controlplane/httpapi/projects_variables_put_policy_test.go) is the writer-side structural sibling of the env.read matrix at the same resolver (BE-0144, projects_variables_get_policy_test.go) and the project-scope sibling of the org-level env.write matrix (BE-0111, variables_put_policy_test.go). Same CapWrite capability class as project.delete/project.update (CapAdmin lives one tier up at project.grants.write/BE-0141), so the role table is identical to the org-level env.write: owner/admin/developer ALLOW via ReasonAllowedByRole, viewer/ci/support DENY via ReasonDeniedNoCapability — CI denies despite holding CapDeploy because env.write is CapWrite, not CapDeploy (CapDeploy is its own axis). Cross-tenant engine matrix DENIES every role INCLUDING Support (CapWrite is OUTSIDE the `roleCaps.has(CapSupport) && (required == CapRead || required == CapSupport)` exception, same posture as CapAdmin and the load-bearing distinction from env.read where support IS allowed cross-tenant). Wire-level cross-tenant story is the projectIDResolver shape: the resource org is the principal's home org, never the path's tenant, so the engine admits the same-tenant resource and the persistence layer rejects the (attacker_home_org, foreign_project_id) pair as 404 NotFound — the replacer DOES run (callCount=1) but with the attacker's home org id, so a production store could not have replaced the victim's variables regardless. Grant containment proves the org-level Developer ALLOW + org-level Viewer DENY pair (locks CapWrite against the grant path against both directions of catalog drift); project-level Viewer grant on target project ALSO DENIES (Viewer is CapRead-only); project-level Developer grant on target project ALLOWS, sibling project DENIES, env-/service-scoped Admin grants DENY against the parent project (covers() one-way). Variables-flavoured leak guards carry the same TWO directions that BE-0141 introduced — a request-body leak guard (anchored on caller-supplied MATRIX_KEY/matrix_value that never appear in the canonical fixture) AND a would-have-returned-data leak guard (postWriteProjectVariablesBodyLeak, anchored on the seeded post-write rows: per-row ids, keys, the non-secret value AND every recognisable fragment of the seeded secret plaintext post-write-plaintext-correcthorsebatterystaple). The allow-path Sentinel-projection assertion is the chokepoint anchor: even right after a customer submitted a secret, the post-write re-read STILL redacts via projectVariableOf -> output.Sentinel, so PUT cannot leak a secret value the customer just submitted. Forward-applicable to every future CapWrite-on-{X}-resolver matrix at any scope — keep the role / disabled / wrong-org / grant-containment skeleton + dual-direction leak guard, swap the action+resolver target+resource Kind, and ALWAYS add a secret-plaintext needle to the post-write leak guard plus a Sentinel-projection assertion on every allow-path tie-in.
- Replace-grants writer vertical (BE-0139 pattern, internal/controlplane/store/project_grant.go + httpapi/project_grants.go): a PUT-replace endpoint on a (parent, scoped-children) resource family pairs the existing reader-port adapter with a unit-of-work writer (ProjectGrantService) modeled exactly on OrganizationVariableService. The repository grows two new methods: Upsert(tx, id, organizationID, projectID, principalID, principalKind, role, *envID, *svcID) (ProjectGrant, error) using `ON CONFLICT (organization_id, project_id, principal_id, COALESCE(environment_id, ''), COALESCE(service_id, ''))` so the customer-mutable `role` is the only column the UPDATE branch touches (the immutable scope tuple + the bump_version trigger handle the rest); DeleteByProjectExceptIDs(tx, organizationID, projectID, keepIDs) renders the empty-keepIDs case as an unconstrained DELETE (an explicit clear is a meaningful customer operation), the non-empty case as `NOT (id = ANY($3::text[]))` so the bulk delete-by-exclusion is one round trip — same shape as DeleteByOrganizationExceptKeys but anchored on the row id (which Upsert returns from RETURNING) rather than a customer-supplied key, so an upsert that mutates an existing row deterministically keeps the survivor's id. The service Replace runs inside one Store.Write tx: project existence Get (a missing parent is typed NotFound, never a generic FK conflict), per-grant Upsert collecting the persisted ids into keepIDs, DeleteByProjectExceptIDs(keepIDs), audit.Append, post-write ListByProject re-read — every step shares the *Tx so a partial replace and an orphaned audit row are both impossible. Validation lives in buildProjectGrantReplace (split out, unit-testable without a DB): closed-set checks on principal_kind / role mirror the table's CHECK constraints, structural checks reject blank/NUL ids and a service-scope-without-environment, in-memory dedup uses `principalID + "\x00" + COALESCE(envID,'') + "\x00" + COALESCE(svcID,'')` to match the SQL unique index byte-for-byte. Audit metadata records counts only — `grant_count`, `project_scope_count`, `environment_scope_count`, `service_scope_count` — never principal ids, role names, or environment/service identifiers; per-row mutation history is the GET /v1/projects/{project_id}/grants surface's job. The HTTP layer adds a ProjectGrantReplacer port mirroring OrganizationVariableReplacer, a strict-decoded replaceProjectGrantsRequest with Grants *[]projectGrantRequest (pointer-to-slice so missing field is structurally distinguishable from an explicit empty array — a missing field is a stable 400, an empty array reaches the store), and the handler clones caller-supplied *string EnvironmentID/ServiceID pointers before forwarding them so the store cannot observe the caller's backing memory. NewHandler and newRouteTable signatures each grow ONE positional port (projectGrantReplacer ProjectGrantReplacer just after projectGrants ProjectGrantReader); a Python regex sweep over 27 test files anchored on `fakeProjectGrantReader{}, nil)` -> `fakeProjectGrantReader{}, fakeProjectGrantReplacer{}, nil)` handled the bulk of the NewHandler churn (43 call sites), with three follow-up patterns hand-fixed: `, logger)` in server_test.go and me_contract_test.go (NewHandler with non-nil logger), `, nil)` newRouteTable call (different return type), and the 29-nil all-nil newRouteTable pattern in six test files (added one trailing nil for the new port).
