Three load-bearing rules: (1) the gate wraps every route INSIDE RequireAuth in server.go's per-route loop (`h = rateLimit(h); if RequiresAuth: h = RequireAuth(...)(h)`) so the resolved principal (org id, key id, auth method) is on the request context when the limiter decides — public endpoints fall back to the IP bucket alone; (2) the internal-worker exemption is wired through a new package-private context helper `withAuthMethod` / `AuthMethodFromContext` in middleware.go that BOTH RequireAuth and RequireInternalWorker stamp with id.Method, so the rate-limit gate can recognise auth.MethodInternalWorker and pass `Exempt=true` to the limiter without re-running the credential store; (3) the "first exhausted bucket wins" rule short-circuits downstream debits (org denied -> key & ip buckets untouched) so a single throttled tenant cannot drain a shared NAT'd IP bucket of every neighbour. Bucket map is sync.Mutex'd with lazy eviction on the request path (no background goroutine; pruning sweeps every IdleTTL); the freshly-created bucket MUST set lastUsed=now BEFORE the sweep runs so the sweep cannot reap the bucket it just inserted (initial zero-value lastUsed is older than any cutoff and was a real bug caught by tests). The 429 wire shape is the standard yalla.error.v1 envelope with apierr.RateLimited(scope, retry) attaching `scope` (bucket dimension name only — "organization" / "api_key" / "ip", NEVER the tenant id or key id or IP) and `retry_after` (integer seconds, clamped to >=1 because the wire Retry-After header cannot carry sub-second); the response also sets the matching `Retry-After: N` header. NewHandler grew ONE new trailing parameter (RateLimiter) — sweep all 64 NewHandler call sites in tests via a Node script that walks the source with depth-tracking parens and appends `, nil` before each closing `)`. Config plumbing: new YALLA_RATE_LIMIT_* env vars (ORG/KEY/IP × READ/WRITE × RPS/BURST + IDLE_TTL + DISABLED master switch) layered over per-profile defaults; ProfileTest defaults to Disabled=true so contract tests across the whole repo never accidentally trip the limiter. The limiter constructor takes a `func() time.Time` clock injection point so deterministic tests (`fixedClock.Advance(d)`) can drive refill behaviour without sleeping. Forward-applicable to any future throughput cap (per-resource, per-tenant-tier, per-route-specific) — extend Specs/Specs.For pairs rather than adding a new bucket dimension. Redaction backstops: the 429 envelope, the Retry-After header, the WARN log record on denial, and every rate-limit identifier flow through telemetry.LogAttrs / apienvelope's regex-based scrubber so a bearer-token in the Authorization header on a throttled request NEVER reaches a log file (TestRateLimitDenialLogsNoSecretValue is the regression pin).
- Pagination contract package (BE-0037, internal/controlplane/pagination): every customer-facing list endpoint composes the shared pagination.Params + pagination.Cursor + pagination.Page[T] envelope rather than reimplementing limit/cursor/sort/filter parsing. ParseParams(url.Values, ParseOptions) parses ?limit= ?cursor= ?sort= ?direction= ?filter.<k>= with stable apierr.InvalidInput (E_INVALID_INPUT) violations whose Reason text NEVER echoes the submitted value (only classification + accepted range — protects against reflection-style content channels), accumulates multiple violations into one envelope, enforces the package MaxLimit=200 ceiling even when an endpoint misconfigures its own, and rejects a cursor whose embedded Sort/Direction disagrees with the request as a stable 400 "fetch the first page again" instead of silently serving overlapping pages. Cursor is base64url-encoded JSON {v: "yalla.cursor.v1", p: Position, s: Sort, d: Direction} — opaque to clients, deterministic (same input -> same encoding so HTTP fixtures diff byte-for-byte), URL-safe (RawURLEncoding, no '+/='), and DOES NOT carry an organization_id / tenant / principal field by contract (a TestDecodeCursorTenantIsolationCannotBeBypassed test guards this so adding one is impossible without breaking the suite — tenant isolation stays the persistence layer's responsibility, cursor only encodes a within-set position). Page[T any] is the wire shape: Items always non-nil (BuildPage guarantees []T{} for empty), NextCursor omitempty (empty string == end of stream — agents do NOT compare len(Items) to limit), TotalEstimate *int64 omitempty (nil = "not cheap to compute", endpoints must NOT fabricate a value). BuildPage uses the over-fetch strategy: store fetches Limit+1 rows, BuildPage trims to Limit and encodes next_cursor from the last retained row's position via a PositionFunc[T] adapter. Cursor stability under inserts is proven end-to-end by TestCursorIsStableUnderInserts: seed N rows, page once, insert NEWER rows after the cursor boundary, prove page 2 still returns exactly the remaining originals (no duplicates, no skips, no newly-inserted rows leaking onto page 2 because the cursor is a strict upper bound on (sort_key DESC, id DESC)). Future list endpoints replace their bespoke parseXxxLimit / list payload struct with one ParseParams call + a BuildPage projection — the existing GET /v1/organizations/{org_id}/audit-events (BE-0103) and break_glass list are pre-pagination-contract and should migrate in their own stories.
- Bare-id route on a deployment (BE-0211+0212+0213 pattern, GET /v1/deployments/{deployment_id}, store/deployment.go DeploymentReader.GetServiceDeployment, httpapi/deployments.go DeploymentGetter port + deploymentIDResolver + getServiceDeploymentHandler + getServiceDeploymentPayload, routes.go GET /v1/deployments/{deployment_id} entry, server.go NewHandler DeploymentGetter parameter, cmd/yalla-api/main.go wires the SAME *store.DeploymentReader as BOTH DeploymentLister AND DeploymentGetter): canonical shape for ALL bare-id read endpoints on a Deployment-level deep resource. Two LOAD-BEARING structural differences from the environment / service bare-id routes (BE-0154 / its services sibling): (1) policy.Scope has NO DeploymentID leg — the Scope hierarchy stops at ServiceID (Organization -> Project -> Environment -> Service), so the resolver pins ONLY OrganizationID, NOT (org + DeploymentID) the way environmentIDResolver pins (org + EnvironmentID). The resource scope carries no inner leg at all, which makes the engine's covers() rule deny EVERY scoped grant (project/env/service) at the boundary via ReasonDeniedOutOfScope — even a service-scoped grant naming the deployment's actual parent service is denied, because covers() is one-way (a grant scope that pins ServiceID cannot cover a resource scope that does not). Principals whose only access is a scoped grant must use a parent-scoped route family to address a deployment. (2) The store-layer adapter intentionally skips the parent-prefetch the list adapter performs: DeploymentReader.GetServiceDeployment composes only DeploymentRepository.GetByID inside a short-lived Store.Read tx (no service prefetch), because the schema's composite foreign keys on the deployments table already guarantee (organization_id, project_id), (organization_id, environment_id), and (organization_id, service_id) cannot diverge across the deployment row — a tenant-scoped GetByID is itself a complete tenant-isolation check, and a prefetch would only duplicate the work of the schema. This is the load-bearing distinction from the list adapter ListServiceDeployments (which DOES prefetch the service to disambiguate "service missing" from "service has no deployments"). The wire shape (serviceDeployment + serviceDeploymentOf in service_deployments.go) is REUSED verbatim — an agent that listed deployments for a service does not re-parse a different shape to fetch one of them by id. Production wiring passes the same *store.DeploymentReader pointer twice (deploymentService, deploymentReader, deploymentReader, breakGlassService, ...): one concrete adapter satisfies BOTH the DeploymentLister AND DeploymentGetter port interfaces, so adding a second read port costs zero new constructors / dependencies. The contract test suite (deployments_get_test.go, 12 tests) and policy matrix (deployments_get_policy_test.go, 4 parent tests) follow the BE-0210 list-side template structure verbatim, with one structural extension in the grant-containment matrix: a service-scoped grant naming THIS deployment's actual parent service is also denied at the wire, because the bare-id resource scope has no ServiceID leg to match. Future bare-id read endpoints on deep resources whose Scope leg does not exist (deployments today; jobs / runs in later stories) should adopt this exact pattern.


- Bare-id read endpoint on a deep resource with a worker-deferred upstream (BE-0229+0230+0231 pattern, GET /v1/services/{service_id}/logs, store/service_log_reader.go ServiceLogReader.ListLogs, httpapi/services_logs.go ServiceLogReader port + serviceLogLine/listServiceLogsPayload wire DTOs + parseServiceLogsLimit + listServiceLogsHandler, routes.go GET /v1/services/{service_id}/logs entry, server.go NewHandler + newRouteTable + cmd/yalla-api/main.go wiring, services_logs_test.go contract suite + services_logs_policy_test.go matrix): canonical shape for ANY observability read endpoint whose real upstream is the Dokploy worker (logs, metrics — BE-0232..0234 next; future events/traces) and whose true content adapter is deferred to a later worker story. Three load-bearing rules: (1) the store-level adapter (store.ServiceLogReader, the second instance of the typed-input-typed-output read adapter shape after store.ServiceReader.GetService) performs the tenant-scoped parent existence check inside a Store.Read transaction so a cross-tenant or unknown service_id surfaces as a deterministic apierr.NotFound at the persistence boundary — never disguised as an empty success and never disguised as a 500 — and then returns an empty Lines slice with the ServiceID populated; the real Dokploy log fetcher is wired in BE-0301+ alongside the provisioning worker, matching the noopJobEnqueuer pattern for placeholder upstreams; (2) the wire DTO is a closed tuple `(service_id, lines[]{occurred_at, stream, message})` with NO pointer-typed fields, NO embedded interfaces, and an empty lines slice that marshals as `[]` not `null` so an agent does not need to special-case the absent-vs-empty distinction; the occurred_at field is RFC3339-nanosecond UTC; the stream enum is the closed set {stdout, stderr, system} so an agent can branch on the value without escape-decoding it; (3) the ?limit= query parameter is clamped at the boundary via parseServiceLogsLimit (the second instance of the bounded-limit-query-parser shape after parseAuditEventLimit, range [1, 1000] default 100), and the error path never echoes the submitted value — only the classification and the accepted range — so a typo can never become a reflection-style content channel. The CapRead policy matrix shape is the structural sibling of services_get_policy_test.go (BE-0184) — all six built-in roles allow same-tenant via ReasonAllowedByRole, support is allowed cross-tenant via ReasonAllowedBySupport at the engine level (defence-in-depth — the customer-facing route cannot reach this branch because serviceIDResolver pins the resource to the principal's home org), every project-/env-/service-scoped grant is denied OutOfScope on the bare-service-id path via the engine's one-way covers() rule, and an org-level Viewer grant is ALLOWED end-to-end (the load-bearing distinction from services_start_policy_test.go where the same grant is denied because service.start is CapDeploy, not CapRead). Limit assertion subtlety pinned by tests: the no-echo check on the invalid-limit deny path must restrict to non-numeric submitted values because numeric out-of-range inputs may legitimately share digits with the accepted-range message ("0" is a substring of "1000" in the "must be between 1 and 1000" string) — only the non-numeric case (where caller-controlled byte content could realistically reach the response body) is asserted. Test-only nil-port test: a typed-nil ServiceLogReader is needed (a bare `nil` literal does not satisfy the interface positional argument), so `var nilReader ServiceLogReader` is the pattern. Port-arity sweep: dominant `fakeServiceStopper{}, fakeServiceVariableReader{}` -> `fakeServiceStopper{}, fakeServiceLogReader{}, fakeServiceVariableReader{}` across 63 test files (108 sites) plus a minor variant `fakeServiceStopper{}, reader, fakeServiceVariableReplacer{}` -> `fakeServiceStopper{}, fakeServiceLogReader{}, reader, fakeServiceVariableReplacer{}` in service_variables_test.go (the test injects a local fakeServiceVariableReader as `reader`, so the LogReader slot is the new positional argument); the `stopper, fakeServiceVariableReader{}` variant in services_stop_test.go is one of the 108 dominant sites. Forward-applicable to BE-0232+0233+0234 (GET /v1/services/{service_id}/metrics, metrics.read action — the OTHER CapRead observability endpoint on the same resolver), and to any future read endpoint whose true content adapter is the Dokploy worker (events, traces) — same vertical, same placeholder shape, same wire-contract guarantees while the real fetcher lands later. The OpenAPI `?limit=` query parameter today is documented only via the Description prose because openapi.Endpoint has no QueryParams field; a future BE story can add structured QueryParam metadata and the existing route entries (audit-events, logs) will switch over together. - POST create endpoint for a service-scoped child resource (BE-0250+0251+0252 pattern, POST /v1/services/{service_id}/backups, mirrors the service_domains POST trio BE-0238+0239+0240; clonable for BE-0264 previews, BE-0289 import previews, and any future bare-id child create): the store-layer composition is the canonical create-unit-of-work shape — ServiceXxxRepository.Insert (single-statement INSERT...RETURNING + mapWriteError mapping driver errors to typed apierr.Conflict whose message is value-free) + ServiceXxxService.Create orchestrator that opens a Store.Write Tx, runs the tenant-scoped parent existence check first (so a cross-tenant or unknown parent id surfaces as a deterministic apierr.NotFound, NEVER a 500 or silent success), runs an in-tx Authorize (defence-in-depth against grant-change races between the HTTP authorize and the desired-state write — the ONLY operation that runs in-tx Authorize; the in-transaction Authorizer is reserved for Create), runs the Insert, and Appends the immutable audit record — all inside the same *Tx so a row can never be persisted without its audit trail. Validation runs BEFORE the Tx is opened (validateCreateXxxInput against a shared validate.Collector so a request rejecting on more than one field surfaces every violation in one typed apierr.InvalidInput; submitted values NEVER appear in violation reasons). The customer-facing create pins any lifecycle status column to a fixed initial value (e.g. ServiceBackupStatusPending) so a customer cannot forge a 'succeeded' / 'completed' status through the public API surface — the worker is the authority for closed-taxonomy transitions; the status column is NOT in the createXxxRequest decoder shape and the validator overwrites in.Status in the validated struct. The audit Metadata records ONLY fields the application layer can prove redaction-safe by construction: structural identifiers (service_id), closed-taxonomy enums (status, certificate_type), and bounded primitives (retention_count, version, enabled flag rendered as "true"/"false"); caller-supplied free text (display_name, schedule, hostname even — schedule is a cron-style expression but is still caller-controlled bytes) is NEVER recorded verbatim, because a customer pasting a token into one of those fields is exactly the footgun a defensive convention avoids. The httpapi-layer composition is the canonical create-handler shape — createXxxRequest decoder (Enabled / boolean-default-true fields are pointers to preserve the absent-vs-explicit-false distinction at the JSON seam — `*bool` decoded; an omitted field collapses to the default at the handler boundary, an explicit `false` rides through unchanged; integer fields take their schema-side default when zero) + createXxxPayload + createXxxHandler that gates on RequireAuth + the typed-internal nil-creator guard + validate.DecodeJSON (strict, max-body-bytes, unknown-field rejection, no input echo on parse failure) + creator.Create + http.StatusCreated yalla.output.v1 envelope projecting through serviceXxxOf. Action is CapWrite (ActionXxxCreate -> CapWrite in catalog.go): owner / admin / developer allowed by role; CI / viewer / support denied via ReasonDeniedNoCapability — load-bearing distinction: a CapDeploy sibling action (e.g. ActionBackupRun, ActionDeploymentCreate) WOULD admit CI. The wire route uses serviceIDResolver (no parent_project_id leg pinned on the resource scope), so EVERY project-/env-/service-scoped grant is denied at the boundary via the engine's one-way covers() rule (ReasonDeniedOutOfScope); only an organization-wide write role or an org-level write grant reaches the handler. Cross-tenant: the resolver pins resource scope to the principal's home org id (never the path service's tenant), so cross-tenant service_ids hit the persistence layer with the home org id and surface as a deterministic apierr.NotFound — engine cross-tenant deny is pinned at the engine level (defence-in-depth: EVERY role including Support is denied cross-tenant for CapWrite — the support cross-tenant exception covers only CapRead / CapSupport). Contract test surface: success with full plumbing assertions (principal home org id forwarded, path service id forwarded, actor id forwarded, no caller-body org id trusted), boolean-default-true and explicit-false at the pointer seam, request_id propagation, validation failure propagated from creator as E_INVALID_INPUT (handler delegates validation to the store-layer orchestrator), strict-decode unknown-field rejection BEFORE creator runs, unauthenticated 401, role-deny 403 (handler never reached), cross-tenant 404 with principal home org forwarded, duplicate-id Conflict 409, store-unavailable 503, nil-creator typed Internal 500. Policy matrix test surface mirrors service_domains_create_policy_test.go one-for-one. Wiring footprint: adds ONE new positional arg (ServiceXxxCreator) to newRouteTable (~slot 57) and NewHandler (~slot 60); ~70 test files / ~120 call sites need a `fakeServiceXxxCreator{}` insertion via bulk substitution `fakeServiceYyyReader{}, fakeServiceZzzReader{}` -> `fakeServiceYyyReader{}, fakeServiceXxxCreator{}, fakeServiceZzzReader{}` (where Yyy is the sibling Reader and Zzz is the next port after the new slot in the signature); the special cases are the in-package contract-test helper for the new resource (`reader` -> `..., reader, fakeServiceXxxCreator{}, ...`) and any sibling test where the local `reader` variable is bound to a DIFFERENT port type that happens to share an adjacent slot (e.g. service_variables_test.go's `reader` is a ServiceVariableReader, NOT a backup reader, so its slot ordering needs a separate substitution). Re-runnable via a small Python script that pattern-matches and applies the three substitutions in order — see the BE-0232+0233+0234 description above for the ast-walking variant if a new arg needs to be inserted at a structural offset rather than between two named neighbours.

- Verb-on-child-resource endpoint pattern (BE-0253+0254+0255, POST /v1/services/{service_id}/backups/{backup_id}/run; sibling of the services_restart verb-on-parent shape, but adds a tenant-scoped child existence check; clonable for any future "trigger an action on a worker-driven child resource" endpoint — backup PATCH/DELETE, future preview-run, future deployment-retry triggers): the store-layer composition is the canonical run-unit-of-work shape — XxxRepository.GetByID (composite (org, parent, child_id) read; pgx.ErrNoRows -> apierr.NotFound(kind, child_id) — the kind/id NEVER contains the org or parent so the customer-facing message stays free of identifiers the principal cannot already prove they own) + XxxRepository.MarkPending (UPDATE...RETURNING flipping the worker-observable status column; the bump_version trigger from the resource's migration owns version, so MarkPending NEVER writes it itself — preserves optimistic-concurrency invariants for future If-Match callers) + RunXxxInput (plain-string actor/correlation seam — no policy/telemetry import in the store package) + XxxService.Run orchestrator (validate IDs before Tx; in Tx: parent-resource tenant-scoped Get -> child-resource tenant-scoped Get -> precondition 409s on closed-taxonomy state (enabled=false, status=running) -> in-tx Authorize (defense-in-depth against grant-change races; on the SAME *Tx as the write) -> MarkPending -> audit append with status_before/status_after metadata; ALL state mutations + audit commit atomically). - BE-0309 postgres is the FIRST database-engine clone of the BE-0301/BE-0307 per-service-type renderer-subtype pattern (internal/controlplane/dokploy/renderer_database_postgres_test.go; structural template for BE-0311 mysql / BE-0313 mariadb / BE-0315 mongo / BE-0317 redis). Four structural swaps vs the BE-0307 type-boundary clone: (1) Input helper collapses from two (per-builder) to ONE (databasePostgresInput) — databases do not vary by builder because the renderer's normaliseBuild() still runs but its output is not the subtype's identity. (2) The Drops* test becomes a single DropsRoleDomainsAndCron pin that asserts each of the three application/compose-only fields is dropped AND that none of their submitted values appear in Summary JSON / slog record / Summary.String() (the customer-submitted hostname "db.acme.example" and cron schedule "0 2 * * *" are the canonical leak candidates) — same no-leak structural barrier as the BE-0307 boundary, applied to a different drop surface. (3) The SubtypeBoundaryFromApplication shape gains an engine-label dimension: the renderer adds a new conditional yalla.engine label only for ServiceDatabase services (mirroring how yalla.role is conditional on a non-empty role), so the boundary test asserts BOTH yalla.service-type (must be "database") AND yalla.engine (must be "postgres") on the postgres case AND that yalla.engine is ABSENT entirely on the application case — the new label is the audit/observability surface that distinguishes a postgres database from a future mysql/mongo/redis database without re-reading the spec body. (4) RoleMatrix collapses entirely to a no-role tier-only matrix (database services have effectiveRole := "" set unconditionally in renderer.go); TierResourceDefaults pins that databases do NOT participate in the production-web 2-replica bump (the disjunction in defaultResources() is `(typ == ServiceApplication || typ == ServiceCompose) && role == RoleWeb` — ServiceDatabase is excluded by both conjuncts), so every tier defaults to one replica regardless. The production-code seam this story introduces is the validEngine() closed whitelist in renderer.go: BE-0309 ships only EnginePostgres = "postgres"; BE-0311..0317 EACH add one engine constant and one line to validEngine's switch — purely additive, no per-engine validation logic changes. The Render() engine validation expands from a single "required for database services" gate to a switch that ALSO rejects unsupported engines with a stable Reason "must be a supported database engine" (no value echo — the message text never names the rejected engine, so the BE-0311..0317 stories that add engines do NOT need to change the message). The ValidationFailures table includes an "unsupported engine" case keyed on "sqlite" — chosen because Yalla will never manage sqlite (file-based, no engine to provision), so the case stays stable across the entire BE-0309..0317 family even as the whitelist grows. The Determinism + RedactsAllVariableValues pins are direct ports of the BE-0307 shape. database.golden in testdata/renderer/ needs the +yalla.engine=postgres label added (regenerable via `go test -count=1 -run TestRenderGolden ./internal/controlplane/dokploy -args -update-golden` — the -update-golden flag is registered as a real *flag.Bool via init() in internal/testutil/golden.go, so it MUST be passed AFTER `-args`, not as a top-level go-test flag, or the binary errors out with "flag provided but not defined"). Forward-applicable verbatim to BE-0317 redis (BE-0311 mysql, BE-0313 mariadb, BE-0315 mongo all landed: validEngine extended to `case EnginePostgres, EngineMysql, EngineMariadb, EngineMongo`; renderer_database_{mysql,mariadb,mongo}_test.go each pin their per-engine contract; the closed-set extension is one comma + one identifier per remaining sibling): each sibling adds ONE engine constant + ONE line to validEngine's switch + a per-engine test file cloned from renderer_database_postgres_test.go with the Engine constant swapped in databasePostgresInput's analogue and the engine label assertion updated. - Per-subtype quota dimension on the services Create unit of work (BE-0326 pattern, internal/controlplane/store/serviceservice.go ServiceService.Create + internal/controlplane/store/service_quota_applications_concurrent_test.go; structural template for BE-0327 compose_stacks, BE-0328 databases — every per-subtype dimension whose denominator is a SUBSET of the services table filtered by Kind): the create unit of work calls svc.quota.Reserve TWICE in the same *Tx for a service whose kind consumes a per-subtype dimension — first the existing QuotaResourceServices reservation (counts every service), then a conditional `if service.Kind == ServiceKindXxx { Reserve(QuotaResourceXxx) }` AFTER it and BEFORE the services.Insert. Order matters: the services reservation locks first so a tenant who exhausts the services dimension cannot acquire the per-subtype counter at all; the per-subtype reservation locks second so a tenant who exhausts ONLY the per-subtype dimension still gets a typed apierr.QuotaExceeded whose ExceededDetail.Resource names the per-subtype dimension specifically. Both reservations roll back together on any later failure (Insert, Enqueue, audit Append). Test pattern (clone of BE-0325): TWO quota_usage rows + TWO quota_policies seeded (per-subtype TIGHT at 5, services LOOSE at attempts*2 so the per-subtype dimension is the boundary that bites), assert detail.Resource == QuotaResourceXxx, assert BOTH active reservation tables == success count (because every winning Create reserved one of each). A second non-concurrent test exhausts the per-subtype dimension then proves a sibling-kind Create (compose / database for BE-0326) still succeeds — pins the per-subtype boundary as a regression barrier against a future refactor that drops the Kind guard. BE-0326 already lands the kind-guard inside ServiceService.Create at the same line where Reserve(services) returns nil; BE-0327 and BE-0328 each add ONE more conditional Reserve call right below the BE-0326 block (Kind == ServiceKindCompose / ServiceKindDatabase) and ONE more test file cloned from service_quota_applications_concurrent_test.go with the dimension constant + Kind constant + sibling-kind sanity-success cases swapped. NOT applicable to dimensions that span MULTIPLE service kinds with a non-trivial denominator (cpu_millicores / memory_mb / storage_gb — those count a numeric column on every kind and belong to a different per-numeric-resource pattern still to be designed).
- Per-Kind quota facet on environments (BE-0330 pattern, internal/controlplane/store/environmentservice.go + migrate/migrations/0025_environment_kind.{up,down}.sql + internal/controlplane/store/environment_quota_preview_environments_concurrent_test.go): structural template for ANY future per-Kind environment quota dimension (analog of the BE-0326/0327/0328 services per-Kind dimensions, now ported to the environments table). The FIRST per-Kind environment story lands the seam: a `kind` text column on environments with NOT NULL DEFAULT 'standard' and a CHECK constraint mirroring the closed Go enum one-to-one; a partial index on (organization_id, project_id) WHERE kind = '<minority-kind>' for the future sweeper; a `Kind` field on Environment, CreateEnvironmentInput, and CloneEnvironmentInput; a validateEnvironmentKind helper that normalises blank to the default member so legacy callers stay green; a closed `EnvironmentKind*` const set; and a conditional Reserve(QuotaResource<KindFacet>) on BOTH EnvironmentService.Create AND EnvironmentService.Clone (environments are the only resource with two create-shape entrypoints, both must be gated together). Subsequent per-Kind environment quota stories ship test-only — the seam is in place after BE-0330. The Reserve gates run in the SAME *Tx as Reserve(QuotaResourceEnvironments) and the desired-state write, so a tenant that exhausts either dimension cannot half-write an environment row whose other dimension passed. The default-on-blank Go validator MUST match the SQL DEFAULT so the migration is forward-compatible with in-process callers that predate the Kind field.

- Dimensional (magnitude-axis) quota dimension on a Create unit of work (BE-0331 pattern, internal/controlplane/store/projectservice.go QuotaReserver port + internal/controlplane/quota/quota.go Checker + internal/controlplane/store/serviceservice.go serviceCPUMillicoresByKind + internal/controlplane/store/service_quota_cpu_millicores_concurrent_test.go; structural template for BE-0332 memory_mb / BE-0333 storage_gb / and every future quota dimension whose allocation is a numeric magnitude per request rather than a +1 count). The FIRST dimensional story widens the load-bearing seam ONCE for the entire dimensional-quota family: the store-layer QuotaReserver interface gains a second method `ReserveAmount(ctx, tx, orgID, resource string, amount int64) error`, and the real adapter quota.Checker implements it as the canonical lock + sum-active + insert-reservation path with the amount parameterised. The count-axis convenience `Reserve(ctx, tx, orgID, resource string) error` is refactored to a one-line delegate `return c.ReserveAmount(...,1)`, so every prior count-axis call site is byte-identical and proves the new path is structurally compatible with the old. amount<=0 is rejected as Internal (wiring error — release is a separate path, not a negative reservation). The Checker validates amount, plan, resource, and limit BEFORE acquiring any row lock so a bad amount cannot block another tenant. The unit-of-work call site (ServiceService.Create) sources the per-request magnitude from a per-Kind constant map (serviceCPUMillicoresByKind: application=250, compose=500, database=500) via a `cpuMillicoresForServiceKind(kind)` helper — the map lives at the store layer so the dependency graph does not reach into the dokploy renderer's tier-aware defaults. The ReserveAmount call runs in the SAME *Tx as the count-axis Reserve calls, the desired-state write, the job enqueue, and the audit append; ordering is "every count-axis Reserve first, then the dimensional ReserveAmount" so a tenant who simultaneously exhausts a count dimension AND the dimensional dimension sees the count-dimension Resource surface in ExceededDetail (the LAST Reserve that fires produces the error). Three fakes (noopQuotaReserver in cmd/yalla-api/main.go, nopQuotaReserver in store/internal_test.go, recordingQuota in store/projectservice_test.go) need a one-line ReserveAmount addition to satisfy the widened interface; no other fakes exist because the concurrent tests use the real Checker. Test pattern: clone the BE-0326 concurrent test, replace the count-axis assertions with magnitude-axis ones — (1) policy LIMIT is a multiple of the per-Kind magnitude (cpu_millicores=1000 = 4 × 250-millicore apps); (2) expectedSuccesses = limit / per-Kind-magnitude; (3) detail.Requested is asserted to equal the per-Kind magnitude (NOT 1) — a regression hard-coding it back to 1 fails closed here; (4) detail.Reserved is expectedSuccesses × magnitude; (5) the active-reservations SUM(amount) assertion replaces / complements COUNT(*) — COUNT alone cannot tell whether the magnitude reached the reservation row Amount column, SUM(amount) closes the gap. A second non-concurrent test creates services across multiple kinds (application=250, database=500), exhausts the dimension exactly, then proves both a compose-kind request (would-reserve 500) and an application-kind request (would-reserve 250) are rejected — and that the two rejections report DIFFERENT detail.Requested values. The single equality check `composeDetail.Requested != appDetail.Requested` is the cheapest possible proof the per-Kind map actually fans out instead of collapsing to one constant. A SQL GROUP BY amount on quota_reservations confirms the magnitude distribution end-to-end (2 rows at 250 + 1 row at 500 for the canonical fixture). After BE-0331, EVERY future dimensional quota story (BE-0332 memory_mb, BE-0333 storage_gb, BE-0335 monthly_deployments) only needs a per-Kind/per-trigger magnitude helper and ONE ReserveAmount call site — the port is already widened and the real Checker implementation does not need to change again. The Reserve(...) call site convention stays for every count-axis dimension; ReserveAmount(...) is reserved for dimensions whose amount actually varies per request.
- BE-0332 memory_mb is the SECOND instance of the dimensional-quota template (BE-0331) and confirms the template clones without any port widening, Checker change, or fake update — only (a) a per-Kind magnitude map + helper in serviceservice.go (serviceMemoryMBByKind: application=512, compose=1024, database=1024), (b) one additional ReserveAmount call site inside ServiceService.Create AFTER the prior dimensional reservation, and (c) a structural clone of the concurrent integration test file with resource constant / magnitudes / limit swapped (service_quota_memory_mb_concurrent_test.go). Two load-bearing additions the template now records explicitly: (1) reservation order is part of the diagnostic contract — the LAST Reserve that fires produces the ExceededDetail.Resource surfaced to the caller, so a clone must seed the prior dimensional dimension(s) LOOSE in its concurrent test if it wants its own Resource to be the one that surfaces; a regression that reorders the reservations is detected by the clone test failing with the wrong detail.Resource (cpu_millicores instead of memory_mb, or vice versa). (2) The combined concurrent regression sweep across all dimensional tests requires `go test -race -parallel=2` (or lower) — two tests at 20 goroutines each saturate Postgres max_connections under default parallelism and surface as E_UNAVAILABLE instead of E_QUOTA_EXCEEDED. The per-test focused run remains green at full parallelism; this is a test-harness contention concern, not a code defect. Any future dimensional-dimension story (BE-0333 storage_gb / BE-0335 monthly_deployments / etc.) adds another concurrent test to the family and inherits both rules.
- Quota-dimension story whose call site is NOT yet wired (BE-0337 api_keys pattern, internal/controlplane/store/apikeyservice.go + internal/controlplane/store/migrate/migrations/0027_quota_resource_api_keys.{up,down}.sql + internal/controlplane/store/apikey_quota_api_keys_concurrent_test.go + cmd/yalla-api/main.go; structural template for BE-0338 members and ANY future dimension story whose owning Service.Create predates the QuotaReserver port — applies whenever a dimension story is the FIRST to wire its service-layer Reserve, distinct from the BE-0331..BE-0336 'call site already there' siblings whose owning unit-of-work already reserves the dimension). The minimum atomic delivery is FOUR change axes: (1) closed-set expansion — a new `NNNN_quota_resource_<name>.{up,down}.sql` migration that follows the BE-0326 backup_schedules template verbatim (DO block looking up the inline DOMAIN CHECK by `contypid = 'quota_resource'::regtype AND contype = 'c'` so the migration is robust to any Postgres-assigned constraint name, then `ALTER DOMAIN quota_resource ADD CONSTRAINT quota_resource_check CHECK (VALUE IN (...))` with the prior set + the new label; the .down.sql is structurally identical and narrows back to the prior set, accepting that any row carrying the new label fails the restored CHECK — that is the correct behaviour, silently dropping rows would lose audit-relevant state); plus the matching `QuotaResource<Name>` constant + membership-set entry in internal/controlplane/store/quota.go; plus updating the `valid` slice in internal/controlplane/store/quota_internal_test.go::TestQuotaResourceValid which pins `len(valid) == len(quotaResources)` — the test is a sealing-trap that catches a forgotten membership-set entry but ALSO fires on a forgotten valid-slice entry; both must change together. (2) Constructor port widening — the existing service struct grows a `quota QuotaReserver` field, the constructor parameter list grows the same port, the nil-guard switch grows a `case quota == nil` arm placed BETWEEN the last existing repo arm and the audit arm (the convention is store → parent repos → own repo → authz? → quota → jobs? → audit), and the Create unit of work grows a `svc.quota.Reserve(ctx, tx, key.OrganizationID, string(QuotaResource<Name>))` call placed AFTER every existence/parent-lookup check and BEFORE the desired-state Insert so a 404 on the parent is never disguised as a quota rejection AND a row-level conflict (slug, prefix, unique constraint) rolls the reservation back with the rest of the unit of work. (3) Constructor call-site fanout — three call sites change: cmd/yalla-api/main.go grows a `<name>Quota := noopQuotaReserver{}` placeholder (the real quota.Checker adapter is wired separately by a cross-cutting plan-resolver story; placeholder mirrors the projectQuota / environmentQuota / serviceQuota convention exactly), the in-package `package store` constructor-nil test grows a `nopQuotaReserver{}` local + a new `{nil quota, ...}` case wedged BETWEEN the last existing nil case and the audit case (positional ordering must mirror the constructor's nil-guard switch), and the `package store_test` integration-test helper grows the shared `&recordingQuota{}` (defined in projectservice_test.go — not a local `noopQuotaReserver{}`, which is only visible to cmd/yalla-api; the store_test package has its OWN allow-all fake hierarchy and the convention is to reuse `recordingQuota` for happy-path constructors). (4) Concurrent integration test — clone of the BE-0336 concurrent_deployments test with five structural simplifications when the owning service has no Authorizer / JobEnqueuer ports (api_keys is pure Yalla identity with no Dokploy mirror, so APIKeyService takes neither): no `atomicAuthorizer` / `atomicJobs` fakes need to be defined or counted; no `authz.calls == attempts` and no `jobs.calls == successes` assertions; the per-goroutine input loop calls `auth.Generate()` INSIDE the goroutine so every concurrent attempt mints its own unique (prefix, secret_hash) pair via crypto/rand (the prefix column is UNIQUE so a shared pair would deterministically conflict and mask the quota race); the parent-row seed is only an `organizations` row (no project/environment/service chain — api_keys live directly under the tenant); and the leaky-input candidates in the rejection-message scan use the resource-specific prefix (`key-%02d` / `req_apikeys_%02d` / `corr_apikeys_%02d`) so an echoed input still fails the message guard. The 'second test' sibling (TestXxxCreateAppliesXxxQuotaIndependentlyOfOtherDimensions) seeds ONLY the dimension under enforcement, exhausts it sequentially, asserts a SIXTH Create surfaces the dimension-specific rejection, and asserts no reservation row exists on TWO unrelated dimensions (services / projects) — the symmetry guard that catches a future regression that drops the Reserve call OR accidentally chose a different resource string. The whole pattern compiles + passes -race against a real Postgres without touching ANY of the 70+ httpapi fake-fixture call sites because the service's HTTP layer is owned by a separate seam (the api_keys handler already calls APIKeyService.Create with the same input shape; only the store-layer wiring changes). Pre-existing test failures gotcha: TestAPIKeyService* and TestEnvironmentService* / TestOrganizationVariableServicePatch* fail on HEAD due to testutil.Factory id-prefix vs ParseSlug drift — confirmed by stashing the BE-0337 changes and reproducing the identical 23-test set on the base commit. NOT introduced by this pattern, owed to a focused triage story before BE-0500+ verification stories run.

- What was implemented: GET /v1/organizations/{org_id}/audit-events, the

    AuditRepository.ListByOrganization through a short-lived read-only

    are inherited for free and the adapter cannot smuggle a mutation past
    Store.Write. The constructor rejects a nil store at construction
    rather than on the first request (fail-fast posture).
  - internal/controlplane/store/auditreader_test.go (new): four
    integration tests against an isolated migrated Postgres database —
    happy-path read with newest-first ordering, tenant isolation
    (two-org seed proves a cross-tenant id never returns another tenant's

    NewAuditEventReader(nil) rejection.

    port + listAuditEventsHandler. Request shape: only the {org_id} path
    parameter and an optional ?limit= query in [1, 200] (default 50,
    handler-side parseAuditEventLimit clamps + validates before any
    database work runs, so a malformed or out-of-range limit is the
    stable 400 E_INVALID_INPUT). Response is yalla.output.v1 carrying
    {events: [...]}: actor and resource are nullable nested OBJECTS
    (mirroring the limit/null convention the usage endpoint pins) — an
    unauthenticated denied event has Actor=null; an organization-root
    action has Resource=null. The wire trusts the persistence-layer
    redaction contract: metadata, IP address, and user agent reach this
    handler already redacted by audit.Auditor, so the projection renders
    them verbatim — a TestAuditEventProjectionDoesNotReintroduceRedaction
    proves the handler must NOT silently un-redact a sentinel value. The
    handler is thin: read principal, parse limit, call port, render.
  - internal/controlplane/httpapi/audit_events_test.go (new): 11 contract
    tests in package httpapi exercising the real NewHandler + real policy
    engine (fake Authenticator + fake AuditEventReader only) — happy-path

    resource project correctly), empty-list for an org with no history,

    rejection), out-of-range-limit 400 (table-driven over 0/-1/201/9999),
    store outage 503 (no raw-cause leak), unauthenticated 401 (reader
    never runs), cross-tenant 403 (reader never runs, no events leaked),
    viewer-without-CapAdmin 403 (the load-bearing distinction from
    CapRead actions: a viewer can list members but cannot list the audit

- Remaining risks / follow-ups:
  - BE-0104 (contract tests for GET /v1/organizations/{org_id}/audit-events)
    and BE-0105 (policy matrix coverage, the unblocked p=1) are now ready
    to land. audit_events_test.go already covers BE-0104's surface
    closely — the explicit-redaction proof, all four CRUD-style failure
    modes, and the viewer-denied property — but the two remain separate
    PRD stories. BE-0105 should table every built-in role x audit.read,
    revoked/expired Disabled principals, and a wrong-organization
    principal (the same pattern as limits_policy_test.go and
    usage_policy_test.go).
  - Filtering (by action, by decision, by actor, by date range) and
    cursor-based pagination are NOT in scope here — the endpoint serves
    the newest N rows in [1, 200]. A separate "audit events filtering"
    story would add query parameters; the wire envelope is
    forward-compatible (events[] can grow optional sibling fields).
  - The wire projection trusts the persistence-layer redaction contract.
    If a future "raw audit event admin view" surface is needed for
    Yalla operators, it must NOT go through this customer-facing
    endpoint — it would be a separate /admin/... route with its own
    policy action and its own redaction policy.
- Learnings for future iterations:
  - For a NewHandler signature change with ~19 call sites in *_test.go,
    a single bulk substitution covers the bulk of the churn IF the
    target substring is regular. The two regular forms in this codebase
    are single-line `fakeUsageReader{}, fakeAPIKeyReader{}` and
    multi-line `fakeUsageReader{},\n\t+fakeAPIKeyReader{}`. The
    exceptions are (a) helpers that pass a named parameter at the new
    port's position (e.g. `, reader,`) and (b) "missing-reader" tests
    that pass nil at the new port's position. Both need targeted follow-up
    edits — a perl/python pass over the common pattern + a manual `grep
    -rn 'fakeOldReader,\n\t+fakeAPIKeyReader{}'` for the residue is the
    reliable workflow.
  - audit_events.go is the third endpoint to use the
    "nullable-nested-object" wire convention (after usage.go and the
    actor/resource pair here). The pattern: when N coupled scalar fields
    are EITHER all-present OR all-absent, project them as a single
    nullable nested object on the wire (`actor: {id, kind}` vs
    `actor: null`), not N coupled-nullable scalars. The agent reads one
    boolean (actor != null) instead of validating N invalid combinations.
    Adding a new field to the nested object later is forward-compatible
    with existing readers.
  - The store contract for audit metadata is "already redacted at
    persistence". A consumer (HTTP handler, future audit-event admin
    surface) must NOT silently un-redact a sentinel value — the wire
    mirrors persistence verbatim. The
    TestAuditEventProjectionDoesNotReintroduceRedaction test pins this
    structurally: feed a fake reader rows whose IP/UA/metadata-value
    are output.Sentinel and assert the wire renders Sentinel, not the
    empty string. A future regression that "cleans up" sentinel values
    in the projection fails this test.
  - audit.read is the load-bearing example of "a read action that is
    NOT CapRead". A viewer (CapRead, CapDeploy in the catalog) cannot
    list the audit log; only CapAdmin (owner, admin) and CapSupport
    (cross-tenant) can. This means the boilerplate "list endpoint" tests
    must NOT assume "every role allowed in the tenant" — the policy
    matrix lands per-action. A viewer-denied contract test (not just a
    matrix test) is good defence-in-depth because it makes a future
    accidental drop to CapRead a contract-test failure, not only a
    matrix-test failure.

- Learnings for future iterations:
  - ON CONFLICT against a PARTIAL unique index MUST repeat the WHERE
    predicate in the conflict_target clause: Postgres treats the partial
    index as not eligible for ON CONFLICT otherwise. The pattern is `ON
    CONFLICT (cols) WHERE <same predicate> DO UPDATE`.
  - Adding a new dependency to a constructor with ~17 call sites (the
    NewHandler / newRouteTable signature) is genuinely O(N) churn in tests
    — but every test file follows the same wiring pattern, so a single
    consistent substring substitution covers the bulk of it. The two
    files where the substring differed (api_keys_test.go used `reader,
    fakeAPIKeyReader`, limits_test.go used `nil, fakeAPIKeyReader{}` in
    the missing-reader test) needed targeted edits, but the rest fell out
    of one mechanical search/replace.
  - For numeric request fields whose zero is meaningful (a limit of 0
    forbids the resource), use `*int64`. A non-pointer int64 cannot
    distinguish "field omitted" from "set to zero", and the body decoder
    would silently treat the latter as the former — leaking a real client
    intent through a default-zero floor.
  - The handler's "at least one entry / every entry supplies limit_value"
    rejection mirrors the store layer's identical violation. This is
    intentional symmetry — both layers must validate at the boundary —
    not duplication. The field paths match byte-for-byte
    ("limits[i].limit_value"), so a future caller cannot tell whether the
    rejection came from the handler or the store, which keeps the wire
    contract stable across refactors.

## 2026-05-15 - BE-0036
- What was implemented: internal/controlplane/validate, the centralized
  request-validation toolkit (validate.go, network.go, resources.go, refs.go,
  json.go).
  - Collector accumulates apierr.FieldViolation entries (stable dotted field
    path + value-free reason) and produces exactly one apierr.InvalidInput via
    Err(); OK()/Violations()/Add()/Addf() round it out.
  - Validators: Name (display name: trimmed, UTF-8, no control chars, rune
    bound), Slug (delegates domain.ValidateSlug), ID (domain.ParseID + kind
    check, value-free reason so a cross-tenant probe is not an oracle), Path
    (repo-relative; rejects absolute, backslash, NUL, ".." traversal),
    URL (http/https only, rejects userinfo so a token cannot leak into stored
    state), Domain (DomainOptions.AllowWildcard gates a single leading "*."
    label — caller resolves feature flag + quota; per-label DNS validation),
    Resources (cpu/memory/replicas: zero=unset, reject negative/over-ceiling,
    per-dimension sub-paths), EnvVars (POSIX names, UTF-8/NUL/length on values,
    duplicate detection; secret vs non-secret split via the ".secret[i]" path
    segment + MaxSecretValueLen ceiling), GitRepoURL (https/ssh/git + scp-like
    git@host:path, rejects embedded credentials), GitBranch (check-ref-format
    subset), GitCommit (7-40 hex), ImageRef (Docker reference subset, rejects
    ".." components + uppercase repo + malformed tag/digest).
  - DecodeJSON: strict, size-capped (custom limitedReader -> errBodyTooLarge),
    DisallowUnknownFields, rejects trailing data; every failure maps to a
    body-free apierr.Invalid / apierr.InvalidInput so a secret in a malformed
    body never leaks through the decode error.
  - Tests: validate_test.go (Collector, every validator success+failure,
    secret/non-secret separation proof, "never echoes the value" proofs for
    Name/Slug/ID/URL/EnvVars/DecodeJSON) + fuzz_test.go (8 fuzz targets:
    FuzzName/Path/Domain/EnvVarName/EnvVarValue/DecodeJSON/ImageRef/GitBranch,
    each seeded with long strings, invalid UTF-8, path traversal, control
    chars; each asserts no panic and re-derives the accept invariants).
  - internal/controlplane/validate/AGENTS.md documents the Collector pattern,
    the no-echo rule, options-not-lookups, field-path conventions, and the
    fuzz-every-validator convention.
- Files changed: internal/controlplane/validate/{validate.go,network.go,
  resources.go,refs.go,json.go,validate_test.go,fuzz_test.go,AGENTS.md} (new),
  ralph/prd.json, ralph/progress.txt.
- Verification run: gofmt -w .; go mod tidy; go build ./...; go vet ./...;
  go test ./...; go test -race ./...; plus a 4s -fuzztime smoke of all 8 fuzz
  targets.
- Results: all passed. goimports, golangci-lint, staticcheck, govulncheck not
  installed locally (documented in earlier iterations).
- Remaining risks / follow-ups:
  - Acceptance criteria "stable yalla.output.v1/error.v1 envelopes",
    "isolated Postgres migrations", and "authorization failure / not-found
    unit tests" are N/A: validate is a pure, in-memory package with no HTTP
    surface, no Postgres, and no auth — covered success + validation-failure
    + fuzz exhaustively instead (the established pattern for pure packages).
  - validate defines its own EnvVar/ResourceRequest input shapes rather than
    importing dokploy's Variable/ResourceLimits — validate is the request
    layer, dokploy is the provisioning layer, and validate must not depend on
    dokploy. When handlers land they will validate the request DTO, then map
    the validated values into the dokploy/store shapes.
  - The validators are implemented and tested but not yet wired into any
    handler (no customer-facing endpoints exist yet). The first endpoint
    story will call validate.New() + the relevant validators in its handler.
- Learnings for future iterations:
  - apierr.InvalidInput already trims + de-dups blank violations and sorts
    deterministically, so a Collector can append freely and rely on it.
  - The Crockford ID alphabet INCLUDES z but EXCLUDES i/l/o/u — to build an
    intentionally-malformed ID suffix for a test, use 'l' (or i/o/u), not 'z'.
  - io.LimitReader reports io.EOF at the cap, indistinguishable from a
    truncated body. For a "body too large" error you need a custom reader
    that returns a distinct sentinel (limitedReader -> errBodyTooLarge).
  - encoding/json reports an unknown field as a plain errors.New whose message
    is `json: unknown field "<name>"` — there is no typed error to errors.As
    against; match on the message prefix.
  - "Separates secret and non-secret fields" was satisfied structurally: the
    EnvVar.Secret flag selects both the length ceiling and the field-path
    segment (".secret[i]" vs "[i]"), so the path alone tells a caller which
    kind failed without inspecting the value.

## 2026-05-14 - BE-0007
- What was implemented: Structured per-request logging middleware for the control-plane API.
  - internal/controlplane/telemetry/logging.go (new): RequestLogging(logger) middleware emitting
    exactly one JSON record per request after the handler runs — method, route (r.Pattern, the
    ServeMux-matched route, falling back to URL path), target (redacted RequestURI), status,
    latency_ms, bytes, plus request_id/correlation_id from LogAttrs(ctx). statusRecorder wraps the
    ResponseWriter to capture status + byte count (defaults to 200 on an implicit write). Level
    follows the outcome: 5xx error, 4xx warn, else info. Headers and bodies are never logged; the
    target is run through output.NewRedactor() (logRedactor) so a smuggled ?token= is scrubbed.
    requestFields is a request-scoped mutable holder seeded onto the context; SetOrgID/
    SetPrincipalID let the future auth/policy layers enrich org_id/principal_id, which are emitted
    only when non-empty. A nil logger disables logging (io.Discard) without panicking.
  - internal/controlplane/telemetry/logging_test.go (new): one-record-per-outcome table
    (success/validation-failure/auth-failure/forbidden/not-found/server-error → level + fields +
    request_id matches response header), redaction (Authorization header, Cookie, query token,
    body field — none appear in the log; target shows [REDACTED]), org/principal included when set
    and omitted when unknown, configured-level gating (INFO suppressed under ERROR threshold, 5xx
    still emitted), nil-logger safety, implicit-write status defaults to 200.
  - internal/controlplane/httpapi/server.go: NewHandler now takes logger *slog.Logger and wraps
    the routed mux in telemetry.RequestLogging(logger) just inside telemetry.Correlate.

  - http.Request.Pattern is populated in place by http.ServeMux during ServeHTTP, and since the

    never triggers WriteHeader, matching net/http's implicit-200 behavior.

    ("INFO"/"WARN"/"ERROR"); tests decode those keys directly.

    []any of slog.String(...) (as LogAttrs returns) splats in cleanly.

## 2026-05-14 - BE-0008
- What was implemented: OpenAPI 3.1 generation + validation for the control-plane API.
  - internal/controlplane/openapi/openapi.go (new): the OpenAPI document builder.
    Build(Info, []Endpoint) -> Document. Endpoint is the neutral per-route metadata
    type (method/path/operationId/summary/description/tags/RequiresAuth/SuccessStatus/
    SuccessDescription/SuccessSchema). Every operation documents a success response and
    a "default" error response, both referencing component schemas. Components always
    define SchemaSuccessEnvelope (yalla.output.v1), SchemaErrorEnvelope (yalla.error.v1),
    SchemaErrorBody, SchemaOpenAPIDocument, and the ApiKeyAuth http/bearer security
    scheme. Public endpoints emit security:[] explicitly; RequiresAuth emits
    [{ApiKeyAuth:[]}]. All map types (Paths/PathItem/Responses/ContentMap/SchemaMap/
    SecuritySchemeMap) marshal with sorted keys via marshalSortedMap so the artifact is
    byte-stable. Examples render secret-shaped values with output.Sentinel; the
    security-scheme description carries a redacted sample bearer token. Document exposes
    HasOperation(method,path) + OperationCount() for the route-coverage test.
  - internal/controlplane/httpapi/routes.go (new): newRouteTable(build, readiness) is
    the single source of truth — []apiRoute pairing a served http.HandlerFunc with its
    openapi.Endpoint. Moved the /healthz, /readyz, /version handlers here from server.go.
    openAPIEndpoint() is the /openapi.json metadata (kept separate because its handler
    is built from the doc itself); openAPIDocument(build, table) folds it back in so the
    published document lists the discovery endpoint. endpointsOf projects metadata out.
  - internal/controlplane/httpapi/server.go: NewHandler now builds the route table,
    generates the OpenAPI doc once at startup (json.MarshalIndent; panics on a marshal
    error since the input is static), appends the /openapi.json route (serves the raw
    document — deliberately NOT enveloped, since OpenAPI tooling expects the standard
    format — with no auth), and registers every table entry on the mux in a loop.
  - internal/controlplane/openapi/openapi_test.go (new): 3.1 identity, envelope+error
    schemas defined, ApiKeyAuth scheme, every endpoint documents both responses + custom
    success status honoured, public security:[] vs authed ApiKeyAuth, HasOperation
    case-insensitive, deterministic marshal (5x) + valid JSON, examples use output.Sentinel
    and contain no unredacted secret-shaped token.
  - internal/controlplane/httpapi/server_test.go: TestHandlerServesOpenAPIDocument
    (200, application/json, openapi=3.1.0, info.version echoes build, paths include all
    routes, body is the raw doc not an envelope, no auth header sent),
    TestEveryRegisteredRouteIsDocumented (CI guard — every registered route in the doc,
    no extras), TestRegisteredRoutesAreServable (every documented route reachable,
    unknown path still 404), TestOpenAPIDocumentRedactsExampleSecrets.
- Files changed: internal/controlplane/openapi/{openapi.go,openapi_test.go} (new),
  internal/controlplane/httpapi/{routes.go (new),server.go,server_test.go},
  internal/controlplane/AGENTS.md, ralph/prd.json, ralph/progress.txt.
- Verification run: gofmt -w .; go mod tidy; go build ./...; go vet ./...; go test ./...;
  go test -race ./...; go test -race ./internal/controlplane/....
- Results: all passed. goimports, golangci-lint, staticcheck, govulncheck not installed locally.
- Remaining risks / follow-ups:
  - Endpoint has no request-body modelling yet (no endpoint has a request body). When the
    first mutating endpoint lands, extend openapi.Endpoint with request schema metadata
    and add a RequestBody to operationFor — keep it data-driven from the route table.
  - The route-coverage guard proves newRouteTable -> document parity. It cannot catch a
    raw mux.HandleFunc added outside the table; AGENTS.md forbids that and TestRegisteredRoutesAreServable
    plus the convention are the backstop. If a future story needs a hard guard, expose a
    mux-introspection hook.
  - Acceptance criterion 5 ("all public responses use stable JSON envelopes") does not
    apply to /openapi.json itself: the OpenAPI document is a standardised format and is
    served raw so OpenAPI tooling can consume it. Every API *operation* response still
    uses the envelopes. Validation/authorization-failure unit-test criteria are N/A —
    /openapi.json takes no input and needs no auth; covered success + not-found instead.
  - Postgres integration-test criterion is N/A for a pure API-contract story.
- Learnings for future iterations:
  - In a Go composite literal of map[string]*Schema, element values can elide &Schema{}
    (write just {...}); but a *Schema struct *field* (e.g. Items) still needs explicit
    &Schema{...}. Map/slice elements allow elision, struct fields do not.
  - json.RawMessage with `json:",omitempty"` is the clean way to embed deterministic
    example bodies — map[string]any examples would marshal with random key order and
    break a determinism test. MarshalIndent does not re-indent RawMessage, so keep
    embedded examples compact.
  - A custom MarshalJSON on a named map type makes json.Marshal deterministic without
    touching call sites; nest them (Paths -> PathItem -> Operation) and each level sorts
    independently. omitempty still works on a named map type — it is evaluated on the Go
    value (len==0) before MarshalJSON is called.
  - The /openapi.json route is self-referential (its handler needs the doc the routes
    describe). Pattern: keep its metadata in a separate openAPIEndpoint(), have the doc
    builder append it, and register the serving route last in NewHandler.

## 2026-05-14 - BE-0010
- What was implemented: Postgres migration system for the control plane.
  - internal/controlplane/store/migrate/migrate.go (new): the migration runner.
    Migration/AppliedMigration/Status types; LoadMigrations(fs.FS) parses+validates
    NNNN_name.(up|down).sql files (malformed names, missing up, empty up, conflicting
    names, duplicates -> errors), sha256-checksums each up script, returns them sorted.
    Migrator (New = embedded FS, NewWithFS = arbitrary FS for tests): Up applies pending
    migrations in order, idempotent; Down rolls back newest-first to a target version;
    Status reports applied/pending/current/dirty. Up/Down serialise via a pg session
    advisory lock, bootstrap the schema_migrations ledger (version bigint PK, name,
    checksum, applied_at, dirty), and run each migration in its own transaction (row
    inserted dirty -> SQL -> row finalised clean; a SQL failure rolls the whole tx back
    leaving no row). verify() refuses dirty / unknown-version / checksum-mismatch via
    errors.Is sentinels ErrDirtyDatabase/ErrUnknownVersion/ErrChecksumMismatch;
    ErrIrreversible guards Down across a migration with no down script.
  - internal/controlplane/store/migrate/migrations/0001_baseline.up.sql + .down.sql (new):
    baseline migration — installs pgcrypto + citext extensions and the set_updated_at()
    BEFORE UPDATE trigger function (the timestamp convention every later table uses).
    Domain tables are deliberately NOT here; they land in BE-0013 (tenant hierarchy),
    BE-0021 (quota), BE-0023 (audit), etc.
  - internal/controlplane/store/migrate/migrate_test.go (new): pure unit tests via
    fstest.MapFS (embedded parse, 6 validation-failure rows, fixture-FS success, nil
    pool); integration tests against an isolated per-test throwaway database
    (testPool helper: CREATE DATABASE / connect / DROP DATABASE ... WITH (FORCE) on
    cleanup, t.Skip when YALLA_TEST_DATABASE_URL unset): up-from-empty (ledger row +
    checksum + PK constraint + extensions + function), idempotent up, refuses
    dirty/unknown/checksum-mismatch, down is reversible + re-migratable, failed
    migration rolls back leaving no row, Status pending/applied.
  - internal/controlplane/store/AGENTS.md (new): migration conventions, domain-table
    timestamp/tenant-scoping rules, integration-test approach.
  - docker-compose.yml (new): local Postgres 16 (user/db "yalla", CREATE DATABASE priv).
  - go.mod/go.sum: added github.com/jackc/pgx/v5 v5.9.2 (+ pgxpool).
- Files changed: internal/controlplane/store/migrate/{migrate.go,migrate_test.go,
  migrations/0001_baseline.up.sql,migrations/0001_baseline.down.sql} (new),
  internal/controlplane/store/AGENTS.md (new), docker-compose.yml (new), go.mod, go.sum,
  ralph/prd.json, ralph/progress.txt.
- Verification run: gofmt -w .; go mod tidy; go build ./...; go vet ./...;
  go test ./...; go test -race ./...; go test -race ./internal/controlplane/store/...
  with YALLA_TEST_DATABASE_URL pointing at a local Postgres 16 container (all 8
  integration tests RUN, not skipped, and PASS).
- Results: all passed. goimports, golangci-lint, staticcheck, govulncheck not installed
  locally (documented). Integration tests skip cleanly when YALLA_TEST_DATABASE_URL is
  unset, so CI without Postgres still goes green; CI WITH Postgres exercises them.
- Remaining risks / follow-ups:
  - The runner is not yet wired into cmd/yalla-api or cmd/yalla-worker startup.
    BE-0009's runStartupChecks + runtime.Meta.SetMigrationVersion are the seams: a
    later story (or BE-0013 when there is real schema to apply) should connect a
    pgxpool, run Migrator.Up, resolve Status().Current onto runtime.Meta, and gate
    the "migrations" readiness check on it.
  - Acceptance criterion 3 ("constraints for tenant isolation, uniqueness, FKs") is
    only partially demonstrable here — there are no domain tables yet. BE-0010 ships
    the migration *system* + the baseline conventions (set_updated_at, extensions);
    the schema_migrations ledger's PK is the one constraint validated by tests.
    Domain-table constraints land with BE-0013/BE-0021/BE-0023 migrations.
  - Criteria 5 (JSON envelopes) and the "authorization failure / not-found" half of
    criterion 6 are N/A: migrate is a persistence-layer package with no HTTP surface.
    Covered success + validation-failure thoroughly instead.
  - BE-0011 (persistence test harness) should generalise the testPool helper into
    internal/controlplane/testutil so every persistence package shares one isolated-
    database fixture instead of re-implementing it.
- Learnings for future iterations:
  - pgx v5 routes Exec/tx.Exec by argument count: a query with ZERO args uses the
    simple query protocol, which allows multiple ;-separated statements in one call —
    so a single .up.sql file with several DDL statements (and dollar-quoted $$ bodies)
    runs fine via one conn.Exec(ctx, mig.UpSQL). A query WITH args uses the extended
    protocol (one statement only).
  - The advisory lock must be held on a single pinned connection: acquire one with
    pool.Acquire(ctx) and run lock + all migration work + unlock on that *pgxpool.Conn,
    not on the pool (the pool hands out different conns).
  - Release the advisory lock on context.WithoutCancel(ctx) so an already-cancelled
    caller context still releases it.
  - Per-test isolation: pgx.Identifier{name}.Sanitize() safely quotes a generated DB
    name; DROP DATABASE ... WITH (FORCE) (PG13+) evicts stragglers. Register cleanups
    so they run LIFO: admin pool close FIRST (runs last), then DROP, then test pool
    close (runs first) — pool closed before drop, admin still open to drop.
  - slog.New(slog.DiscardHandler) (Go 1.24+) is the clean nil-logger fallback.
  - Validation logic that takes an fs.FS (LoadMigrations) is unit-testable with
    fstest.MapFS — no database needed for the "validation failure" acceptance criterion.

    pure unexported function (lookupAdminDSN, scanLeaks) and white-box unit-test
    THAT; the testing.TB wrapper is then trivial glue. White-box (package
    testutil) and black-box (package testutil_test) test files coexist fine in
    one directory.
  - A test helper taking testing.TB (not *testing.T) works in benchmarks and
    nested helpers too; t.Skip/Fatalf/Cleanup/Helper/Errorf are all on TB.
  - t.Run waits for a non-parallel subtest INCLUDING its t.Cleanup callbacks
    before returning — so "provision in an inner subtest, then assert it was
    cleaned up" is a reliable way to test cleanup behaviour.
  - Cleanup ordering is LIFO: register admin-pool Close first (runs last), the
    DROP DATABASE second, the test-pool Close last (runs first) — so the pool
    is closed, then the DB dropped while the admin pool is still open.
  - An import cycle is decided at the PACKAGE level: migrate's own _test.go
    files are package migrate, so they cannot import testutil even though
    they're "just tests". Bootstrap-layer packages keep local helpers.

  testdata/fuzz crash files written). goimports, golangci-lint, staticcheck,
  govulncheck not installed locally (documented).
- Remaining risks / follow-ups:
  - testutil/fixtures.go builds FAKE deterministic IDs with its own prefixes
    (it uses "prj" where domain uses "proj") — deliberately independent of the
    domain package. When BE-0013 lands real domain tables, a repository-backed
    seeder should mint real domain.NewID values; the testutil structs are the
    shape that seeder will consume. Aligning testutil's fake prefixes with the
    domain kinds is optional cleanup, not required.
  - Slug uniqueness "within parent scope" (acceptance #2) is half here: domain
    guarantees well-formedness; the per-scope UNIQUE constraint lands with the
    BE-0013 tenant-hierarchy migration.
  - Acceptance #3 ("Dokploy names include deterministic Yalla IDs"): DokployName
    embeds the full ID. The actual Dokploy mapping (org->project->env->service)
    is consumed by the provisioning worker stories, not this one.
  - Acceptance #5-7 (JSON envelopes / authz / not-found / Postgres integration)
    are N/A for a pure domain-primitive package with no HTTP or DB surface;
    covered success + extensive validation-failure + fuzz instead. #8
    (redaction): IDs and slugs are not secrets — N/A, but error messages
    deliberately do not echo untrusted input (TestParseIDErrorDoesNotEchoInput).
- Learnings for future iterations:
  - golang.org/x/text/transform.Chain is STATEFUL and NOT safe for concurrent
    use. A package-level transform.Chain shared across t.Parallel() subtests
    panics in (*link).src. Pool it (sync.Pool) or build per-call. This will
    bite any future package doing Unicode normalisation.
  - cases.Fold() (golang.org/x/text/cases) does full Unicode case folding,
    which is what maps ß -> "ss"; strings.ToLower and NFKC do NOT. Put it first
    in the chain, before NFD/NFKC.
  - 16 random bytes encode to exactly 26 base32 chars with no padding (5 bytes
    -> 8 chars; 16 = 3*5 + 1 -> 24 + 2 = 26). Crockford lowercase alphabet is
    "0123456789abcdefghjkmnpqrstvwxyz" (i/l/o/u removed).
  - Go fuzz: f.Add seeds live in code; generated "interesting" corpus goes to
    the build cache, NOT testdata/ — testdata/fuzz/ files appear only on a
    failure. A clean fuzz run leaves the working tree untouched.
  - Keep domain primitives free of apierr/apienvelope imports — return plain
    sentinel errors and let the HTTP layer translate. This keeps the dependency
    arrow pointing one way (httpapi -> domain, never the reverse).

## 2026-05-14 - BE-0013
- What was implemented: the tenant hierarchy schema — organizations, users,
  memberships, projects, environments, services, and dokploy_refs — as
  migration 0002, plus schema-level integration tests.
  - internal/controlplane/store/migrate/migrations/0002_tenant_hierarchy.up.sql
    (new): the seven tables. organizations is the tenant root; users is a
    GLOBAL identity table linked to orgs only through memberships. projects/
    environments/services each carry organization_id (+ parent IDs) and are
    tenant-isolated by COMPOSITE foreign keys — environments reference
    projects(organization_id, id), services reference
    environments(organization_id, project_id, id) — so a child can never cross
    the tenant boundary. Each parent exposes the matching UNIQUE(organization_id,
    [project_id,] id) constraint the composite FK needs. Slugs are citext and
    unique within parent scope (org for projects, project for environments,
    environment for services), never globally. Every table has created_at/
    updated_at + a set_updated_at() BEFORE UPDATE trigger. memberships PK is
    (organization_id, user_id) with a role CHECK (owner/admin/member). services
    has a kind CHECK (application/database/compose). dokploy_refs is the
    polymorphic Yalla-resource -> Dokploy-object map (yalla_kind/yalla_id +
    dokploy_resource/dokploy_id covering organization/project/environment/
    application/compose/database/domain/backup); tenant-scoped via the
    organization_id FK, UNIQUE(dokploy_resource, dokploy_id) so an object is
    claimed once, UNIQUE(organization_id, yalla_id, dokploy_resource, dokploy_id)
    against duplicate rows while still allowing many domains/backups per
    resource. ON DELETE CASCADE everywhere from organizations down.
  - 0002_tenant_hierarchy.down.sql (new): drops the seven tables newest-first;
    DROP TABLE removes each table's indexes + trigger. set_updated_at() itself
    belongs to the baseline migration and is left in place.
  - internal/controlplane/store/schema_test.go (new, package store_test):
    integration tests via testutil.RequireMigratedDB + testutil.NewFactory —
    tables-exist, full-chain insert + hierarchy walk, FK enforcement (missing
    org, env/service crossing the tenant boundary via the composite FK), slug
    uniqueness within parent (incl. citext case-insensitivity + same slug
    allowed in a different org), cascade delete (descendants gone, global users
    row survives), cross-tenant isolation (org-scoped count), dokploy_refs
    constraints (object claimed once, duplicate rows rejected, bad
    dokploy_resource rejected, org FK), membership constraints (one per org,
    role CHECK, user FK). Constraint violations matched via *pgconn.PgError
    SQLSTATE class 23.
  - internal/controlplane/store/migrate/migrate_test.go: TestMigrationsUpIs
    Idempotent's Status().Current assertion now derives the expected version
    from m.Migrations() instead of the literal 1, so future migrations don't
    break it.
  - internal/controlplane/store/AGENTS.md: documented the composite-FK tenant
    boundary, global users table, dokploy_refs polymorphism, the no-ID-prefix-
    CHECK decision, and where schema integration tests live.
- Files changed: internal/controlplane/store/migrate/migrations/
  0002_tenant_hierarchy.{up,down}.sql (new), internal/controlplane/store/
  schema_test.go (new), internal/controlplane/store/migrate/migrate_test.go,
  internal/controlplane/store/AGENTS.md, ralph/prd.json, ralph/progress.txt.
- Verification run: gofmt -w .; go mod tidy; go build ./...; go vet ./...;
  go test ./...; go test -race ./... — the last two also run with
  YALLA_TEST_DATABASE_URL pointing at the docker-compose Postgres 16 (all 8
  schema integration tests RUN, not skipped, and PASS under -race).
- Results: all passed. goimports, golangci-lint, staticcheck, govulncheck not
  installed locally (documented). Integration tests skip cleanly without the
  env var so CI without Postgres stays green.
- Remaining risks / follow-ups:
  - No repository layer yet: BE-0014 (transaction pattern) + later repo stories
    add the tenant-scoped query methods. The testutil.Factory builds in-memory
    fixtures whose column shape matches these tables — a repository-backed
    seeder should consume them. Note Factory.User carries an OrganizationID but
    the users table is global; the seeder must create a separate membership row.
  - Acceptance criteria 5-6 (JSON envelopes / authorization-failure unit tests)
    are N/A for a pure schema migration with no HTTP surface; covered success +
    extensive constraint-violation (FK / unique / check) + not-found-style
    (cascade-deleted rows absent) instead.
  - Criterion 8 (redaction): no table stores secrets/tokens/env values — those
    land in dedicated later migrations; N/A here.
  - The migration runner is still not wired into cmd/yalla-api startup; that
    seam (runStartupChecks + runtime.Meta.SetMigrationVersion) is still open.
- Learnings for future iterations:
  - Composite foreign keys are the database-level tenant-isolation primitive:
    child FK (organization_id, parent_id) -> parent UNIQUE(organization_id, id)
    makes "child in a different org than its parent" unrepresentable. Every new
    hierarchy table should follow this and expose the UNIQUE its children need.
  - package migrate cannot import testutil (testutil imports migrate). Schema
    integration tests therefore live in a sibling package store_test, which CAN
    import testutil. This is the home for every future domain-table test.
  - pgx surfaces constraint violations as *pgconn.PgError; SQLSTATE class "23"
    (Code[:2] == "23") covers FK / unique / check / not-null uniformly — match
    on the class, not individual codes, for "the database rejected this" tests.
  - Adding a migration can break migrate_test.go assertions that hard-code the
    latest version. Only Status().Current was literal-bound; the rest already
    derive from len(m.Migrations()). Audit that file on every new migration.
  - citext columns give case-insensitive UNIQUE for free — 'shared-slug' and
    'SHARED-SLUG' collide within the same parent scope without a lower() index.
