- Learnings for future iterations:
  - When a story's resource has no foundation yet, the right scope
    is ONE big vertical (migration + repo + reader + handler + route
    + wiring + tests). Recent commit history (BE-0106 for variables,
    BE-0118 for projects) confirms this pattern.
  - NewHandler signature extension forces a 30+ file sweep. A Python
    regex over a stable anchor pattern (e.g. `fakeProjectRestorer{},
    X)`) handles the common case; the rare outliers
    (projects_restore_test.go, projects_delete_test.go) need manual
    Edit calls because their NewHandler call ends with mixed
    nil/var args. Single-line newRouteTable calls with all-nil args
    need a separate sweep.
  - LIST-FOR-PARENT endpoints (list grants OF a project, list
    environments OF a project, ...) need the reader to Get the
    parent first inside the same Store.Read transaction so a missing
    or cross-tenant parent surfaces as 404 — never as an empty list,
    which would mislead an agent. The Get is cheap (one
    tenant-scoped SELECT) and the transaction guarantees a
    consistent snapshot across both legs.
  - Postgres UNIQUE constraints treat NULLs as DISTINCT by default
    (until v15's NULLS NOT DISTINCT). To de-dup rows where two
    nullable columns participate in the uniqueness check (here:
    (env_id, svc_id) on a per-principal-per-project grant), use a
    UNIQUE INDEX with COALESCE(col, '') so the NULL-NULL pair
    collapses to ('', '') and dedups cleanly. The plain UNIQUE
    constraint would let a principal hold two grants at the same
    NULL-NULL scope.
  - Nullable nested-object projection vs coupled-nullable scalars
    (existing patterns line 54): the principal block on
    projectGrantResource is one nested object {id, kind} instead of
    two coupled-nullable scalars. EnvironmentID / ServiceID remain
    nullable scalars because they are NOT coupled — a grant can
    have env_id without svc_id, but a principal cannot have an id
    without a kind. The rule: if N fields are EITHER all-present OR
    all-absent, project them as a nested object; if they vary
    independently, scalars are fine.

## 2026-05-15 - BE-0138
- What was implemented: policy-matrix coverage for GET
  /v1/projects/{project_id}/grants — the authorization contract of the
  list-project-grants endpoint (whose wire contract is already proved by
  BE-0136 / project_grants_test.go).
  - internal/controlplane/httpapi/projects_grants_policy_test.go (new):
    four test functions that exhaustively exercise action
    project.grants.read against the real NewHandler + real
    policy.NewEngine() (fake Authenticator + fake ProjectGrantReader
    only). The structure mirrors projects_get_policy_test.go because
    project.grants.read carries the same capability class (CapRead),
    the same resolver (projectIDResolver — resource scope = principal
    home org + path project_id), and the same wire-vs-engine
    cross-tenant distinction.
    - TestListProjectGrantsPolicyMatrixRoles: drives every built-in
      role (owner, admin, developer, viewer, ci, support) through the
      production request path. All six hold CapRead so the matrix is
      "all allow"; each row pins the engine verdict (Allow + reason
      ReasonAllowedByRole), the reader being reached with the
      principal's home org id + the path project_id + exactly one
      call, and the wire body carrying the canonical two-grant
      projection — a user grant with EnvironmentID/ServiceID null and
      a service-account grant with both set, so the nullable-pointer
      projection regression-fails here if either side flips.
    - TestListProjectGrantsPolicyRevokedAndExpiredKeys: two cases
      ("revoked key", "sa_revoked"; "expired key", "sa_expired"),
      both Disabled-principal under an Owner role; engine denies with
      ReasonDeniedPrincipalDisabled even though the role would
      otherwise allow, the reader's callCount is asserted == 0 (so a
      production store could not have surfaced a grant row in the
      background), and the denied body is checked against
      grantsDenyBodyLeak — a leak guard with nine needles (canonical
      project id/slug/display name + both grant ids + both principal
      ids + env id + svc id) — plus the principal id and org id.
    - TestListProjectGrantsPolicyWrongOrganizationPrincipal: the
      cross-tenant boundary. The wire-level half drives an
      org_attacker Owner principal at GET
      /v1/projects/prj_victim_alpha/grants with a fake reader that
      returns apierr.NotFound (the reader's project existence check
      mirrors the store-backed adapter's behavior); the assertion is
      a deterministic 404 E_NOT_FOUND with the reader called exactly
      once with (org_attacker, prj_victim_alpha) — never the victim's
      org — and the response body containing no instance of the
      victim's org id (case-insensitive message check + raw substring
      body check). The engine-level half pins the five non-support
      roles to ReasonDeniedCrossTenant against a foreign-org Project
      resource and pins Support to ReasonAllowedBySupport (CapRead is
      inside the engine's CapSupport && (CapRead || CapSupport)
      exception). The customer-facing route cannot reach the engine
      branch by construction, but pinning it locks the CapRead
      requirement: a future catalog upgrade of project.grants.read
      above CapRead would silently deny every support cross-tenant
      read and fail here first.
    - TestListProjectGrantsPolicyGrantContainment: the three
      containment properties from PRD BE-0138's acceptance criteria.
      Project-level Viewer grant on the target project allows
      project.grants.read via ReasonAllowedByGrant on the target and
      denies via ReasonDeniedOutOfScope on a sibling project. An
      env-scoped Admin grant on staging denies project.grants.read on
      the parent project (covers() is one-way) AND denies
      environment.delete on production (the "env grant does not imply
      access to production unless production is explicitly granted"
      property). A service-scoped Admin grant denies service.update
      on a sibling service, denies env.write on the parent
      environment (the "service grant does not expose parent-level
      secrets or unrelated services" property), and denies
      project.grants.read on the parent project. Each property is
      then tied back to the wire: four 403 responses (sibling
      project / env-scoped / service-scoped + the home-org-foreign
      stolen-key engine case) prove the reader is never reached
      (callCount == 0, gotOrg/gotProj empty) and the body never echoes
      the canonical project or grants — so a scoped key denied on the
      wire cannot have surfaced any grant row in the background. The
      org-level Viewer allow path is end-to-end (200, canonical
      payload, reader reached on home org + path project id).
  - Total new test count: 4 top-level tests + 6 role subtests + 2
    revoked/expired subtests + 5 engine-cross-tenant subtests = 17
    sub-rows in go test -v output. Every assertion that the reader
    "must never run" uses callCount in addition to gotOrgID/gotProjectID
    being empty — a stronger property than the projects_get_policy_test
    pattern, which only checks the captured ids.

- Remaining risks / follow-ups:
  - BE-0139 (Implement PUT /v1/projects/{project_id}/grants) and
    BE-0141 (its policy matrix) are the next steps in the project-grants
    surface — the writer-port + CapAdmin half of the project-grants
    vertical (ActionProjectGrantsWrite -> CapAdmin in catalog.go:122).
    The CRUD-style write story will introduce a ProjectGrantWriter port
    (mirror OrganizationVariableReplacer / ProjectRestorer) and a
    NewHandler signature change to thread it through — the
    19-call-sites bulk substitution pattern from BE-0103 still applies.
    The PUT-grants policy matrix will look more like
    projects_restore_policy_test.go (CapWrite/CapAdmin-style: Owner/
    Admin allow, Developer/Viewer/CI/Support deny, Support is OUTSIDE
    the cross-tenant exception) rather than this one — but the
    grant-containment property is symmetric, so the project-scoped
    grantee on a sibling project deny and the env-/service-scoped
    grantee deny will carry through.
  - Filtering / pagination of project grants are out of scope for both
    BE-0136 and BE-0138. A future "filter grants by principal / by
    role / by environment / by service" story would add query
    parameters; the wire envelope is forward-compatible (a new
    field on the data payload would not break clients).
  - The grants_policy file pins the engine-level support cross-tenant
    exception even though projectIDResolver makes it unreachable on
    the route under test. That is deliberate: the engine is the
    authoritative source of the documented support exception, and a
    future scoped variant (e.g. an admin tool that takes both {org_id}
    and {project_id} from the path) inherits the working
    cross-tenant deny and the documented support exception for free.
- Learnings for future iterations:
  - When a CapRead grants-read endpoint already has the same resolver
    (projectIDResolver / similar) and the same capability class as an
    existing matrix file (here projects_get_policy_test.go),
    projects_grants_policy_test.go is a structural twin of it modulo
    (1) the action constant, (2) the fake reader, (3) the response
    decoder, and (4) the leak-guard needles. The role matrix, the
    Disabled-principal case set, the cross-tenant wire/engine split,
    and the four containment cases (project-target / project-sibling
    / env / service / org-viewer) port directly. A "duplicate then
    diff" approach is the right move; the only place to think harder
    is the leak-guard needle set — for grants the needles must
    cover canonical project id+slug+display-name AND every grant id
    AND every principal id AND the env/svc ids on the canonical
    grants. A weak leak guard that only checks the project's three
    fields would miss a regression that rendered a grant's principal
    id on a deny path.
  - fakeProjectGrantReader has a callCount *int field on top of the
    usual gotOrgID/gotProjectID pointers. Using callCount in the
    deny-path assertions is a strictly stronger property than just
    checking the captured ids are empty (a future regression that
    nil-guarded the captured-ids pointers would silently pass the
    weaker check). When a project-store fake exposes callCount, prefer
    asserting callCount == N over relying on empty captured ids — and
    keep the captured-id checks too for the load-bearing
    "reader was called with the principal's home org" property on
    the wire-level cross-tenant test.
  - The "stolen key planted in a foreign org" engine assertion at the
    end of the grant-containment test is the engine-level twin of the
    wire-level "wrong organization principal" test, applied to a
    scoped key (the principal carries grants for org_acme but its
    home org is org_sibling). The cross-tenant guard fires because
    the principal's home org no longer matches the grant's scope —
    not because the grant itself is malformed. Keeping this assertion
    in the containment test (instead of the wrong-organization test)
    keeps "what does a scoped key authorize" all in one place; the
    wrong-organization test stays focused on the role-based path.

## 2026-05-15 - BE-0139
- What was implemented: PUT /v1/projects/{project_id}/grants — the
  writer half of the project-grants vertical whose reader half BE-0136
  landed and whose authorization matrix BE-0138 already exercises for
  the GET shape. The endpoint replaces the project's scoped grants in
  one transaction through a new ProjectGrantReplacer port satisfied by
  *store.ProjectGrantService.
  - internal/controlplane/store/project_grant.go: extended with the
    persistence + unit-of-work writer. ProjectGrantRepository grows two
    methods: Upsert(tx, id, organizationID, projectID, principalID,
    principalKind, role, *envID, *svcID) (ProjectGrant, error) using
    ON CONFLICT (organization_id, project_id, principal_id,
    COALESCE(environment_id, ''), COALESCE(service_id, '')) DO UPDATE
    SET role = EXCLUDED.role — only the customer-mutable role column
    is touched on the UPDATE branch; the immutable scope tuple +
    bump_version trigger refresh version/updated_at; a nil *Tx is a
    typed Internal (programming error). DeleteByProjectExceptIDs(tx,
    organizationID, projectID, keepIDs) renders the empty-keepIDs case
    as an unconstrained DELETE filtered on (organization_id,
    project_id) and the non-empty case as
    NOT (id = ANY($3::text[])) — one round trip either way, tenant
    scoped at the WHERE clause. ProjectGrantService composes Store,
    ProjectRepository, ProjectGrantRepository, AuditAppender; Replace
    runs inside one Store.Write tx: project existence Get (a missing
    parent is typed NotFound, never a generic FK conflict), per-grant
    Upsert collecting the persisted RETURNING ids into keepIDs (so an
    upsert that mutates an existing row keeps the survivor's id, not
    the caller-minted one), DeleteByProjectExceptIDs(keepIDs),
    audit.Append, post-write ListByProject re-read.
    buildProjectGrantReplace validates closed-set principal_kind ({usr,
    sa}) and role (the six built-in roles) against in-memory tables
    that mirror the table CHECK constraints byte-for-byte;
    normaliseProjectGrantScopeID trims blank/NUL bytes from *string
    scope ids; the dedup uses principalID + "\x00" +
    safeProjectGrantScopeID(envID) + "\x00" + safeProjectGrantScopeID(
    svcID) so the in-memory uniqueness matches the SQL
    project_grants_principal_scope_idx COALESCE(...,'') projection
    byte-for-byte. Service-scope-without-environment is rejected as
    InvalidInput naming "grants[i].environment_id". Audit metadata
    records {grant_count, project_scope_count, environment_scope_count,
    service_scope_count} — counts only, never principal ids, role
    names, or env/svc identifiers (per-row mutation history is the
    reader's job).

    to reconstruct a grant set from audit metadata alone would need a
    richer per-row audit_events shape, not a relaxation of this
    chokepoint.
- Learnings for future iterations:
  - apierr.Internal returns a yerr with Code=CodeInternal
    (E_INTERNAL), NOT Code=CodeServer. CodeServer is reserved for
    upstream Dokploy errors. The constructor-rejects-blank-ActorOrg
    pattern should assert CodeInternal in tests.
  - Test field-path assertions for InvalidInput errors should use
    apierr.ViolationsOf(err) and walk the FieldViolations rather than
    strings.Contains on err.Error() — the user-facing Error() method
    surfaces only the message ("request validation failed"), not the
    field paths. Helper violationFor(err, field) in
    project_grant_service_test.go is the reusable shape.
  - When a NewHandler signature change adds ONE positional port, the
    27-file bulk regex sweep over `fakeProjectGrantReader{}, nil)` ->
    `fakeProjectGrantReader{}, fakeProjectGrantReplacer{}, nil)` covers
    the bulk (43 of 45 sites). The exceptional sites are: NewHandler
    with non-nil logger arg (`, logger)` instead of `, nil)`) in
    server_test.go and me_contract_test.go — 3 sites total; the trailing
    `, nil)` newRouteTable call (2 sites — these need a different
    substitution because newRouteTable does NOT take a logger); and the
    29-nil all-nil newRouteTable pattern (6 sites — these need exactly
    one more nil). A targeted second pass over the residue resolved each
    edge case; a final `grep -rn fakeProjectGrantReader{}` with a
    "not followed by fakeProjectGrantReplacer" filter confirmed
    completeness.
  - The Upsert RETURNS the persisted row id, which is the surviving
    id of an existing row at the same scope tuple — NOT the caller-
    minted id passed in INSERT. The keepIDs collection that drives
    the delete-by-exclusion must read from row.ID (the RETURNING
    value), not the locally minted id, or the second Replace's delete
    would orphan the row it just mutated. This is the same idiom
    OrganizationVariableService uses for the same reason.

## 2026-05-15 - BE-0141
- Added policy-matrix coverage for PUT /v1/projects/{project_id}/grants in internal/controlplane/httpapi/projects_grants_put_policy_test.go: role matrix (Owner/Admin allow via ReasonAllowedByRole; Developer/Viewer/CI/Support all deny via ReasonDeniedNoCapability — the load-bearing distinction from project.delete is that Developer ALSO denies here because project.grants.write is CapAdmin, one tier above CapWrite), revoked/expired credential 403, wrong-organization principal (wire-level 404 at persistence + engine-level cross-tenant deny for ALL six roles including Support since CapAdmin is OUTSIDE the engine's `CapSupport && (CapRead || CapSupport)` exception), and grant containment (project-Admin grant allows target/denies sibling; project-Developer grant on the same project denies via ReasonDeniedNoCapability — the load-bearing distinction from project.delete where the same grant would allow; env-scoped staging-Admin grant denies the parent project AND production env; service-scoped Admin grant denies parent env env.write, sibling service update, AND parent project; org-Admin allows; org-Developer denies via ReasonDeniedNoCapability — the org-admin-allow + org-developer-deny PAIR locks the CapAdmin requirement against the grant path; foreign-home-org with grant on canonical project denies as engine-level cross-tenant).
- Files changed: internal/controlplane/httpapi/projects_grants_put_policy_test.go (new); ralph/prd.json (BE-0141 -> passes:true); ralph/progress.txt (this entry).
- Verification: gofmt -l ., go mod tidy, go build ./..., go vet ./..., go test ./..., go test -race ./... all green. Focused: go test -run TestReplaceProjectGrantsPolicy -v ./internal/controlplane/httpapi/... passes (matrix roles 6/6, revoked+expired 2/2, wrong-org cross-tenant deny 6/6 including support, grant containment 1/1).
- Remaining risks: none for this story. The store-backed integration tests for project_grant_test.go cover persistence-layer tenant isolation; this file covers the policy boundary. Both deny-direction leak guards (replaceGrantsRequestBodyLeak for caller-submitted request body needles, grantsDenyBodyLeak for canonical post-write data needles) are checked on every deny path so a future renderer that gained either a "render request body on error" mode or a "render would-have-returned data on 403" mode fails here.
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - CapAdmin-on-{project_id}-resolver policy matrix (BE-0141, internal/controlplane/httpapi/projects_grants_put_policy_test.go) is the structural sibling of the CapWrite-on-{project_id}-resolver matrix (projects_delete_policy_test.go) but ONE TIER UP — Developer JOINS the deny set (CapWrite-holder, not CapAdmin-holder) and the org-level Developer grant flips from ALLOW (delete) to DENY (grants.write). Pair the org-Admin allow with the org-Developer deny: that pair locks the CapAdmin requirement against the grant path so a future catalog change that downgraded project.grants.write to CapWrite would still pass the allow check but fail the deny check, surfacing the regression. The cross-tenant engine matrix denies EVERY role including Support (CapAdmin is OUTSIDE `CapSupport && (CapRead || CapSupport)`); the CapRead siblings (audit.read, project.grants.read) ALLOW Support cross-tenant via ReasonAllowedBySupport — so this is the load-bearing distinction between read and admin matrices for the same path-shape.
  - Mutating-policy-matrix tests need TWO directions of leak guard, not one: a request-body leak guard (replaceGrantsRequestBodyLeak in BE-0141, paralleling the seededPostWrite/MATRIX_KEY pattern of BE-0111) anchored on distinctive caller-supplied identifiers (e.g. usr_request_matrix), and a would-have-returned-data leak guard (grantsDenyBodyLeak, anchored on canonical fixture data the fake replacer would return on an allow path). Use both on EVERY deny path. A read endpoint needs only the second; a write endpoint needs both, because a policy boundary that turned into a "we know what you tried to do" oracle is itself a regression direction.
  - For a CapAdmin-on-resource matrix, the role matrix correctly fails when CI is omitted: CI holds CapDeploy (for service lifecycle) but neither CapWrite nor CapAdmin. List CI explicitly in BOTH the per-role deny rows AND the cross-tenant engine deny loop — the deploy capability is its own axis.
  - Distinguish the "principal-with-grants-but-foreign-home-org" engine assertion from the "in-tenant role" matrix: the cross-tenant guard fires before the grants are even consulted because the principal's OrganizationID no longer matches the grant scope's OrganizationID. This is a structural property of the engine independent of CapAdmin vs CapWrite vs CapRead, and pinning it here documents that a stolen scoped key cannot be smuggled across tenants by anyone who finds it. Use a foreign-home-org principal whose grant is otherwise valid for the target resource, then resolve against the same project id under the foreign org's scope — the engine refuses even when the grant scope itself names the same project.

The matrix pins the engine verdict anyway so a future admin/scoped variant that DOES resolve into a foreign-org scope inherits a working ReasonDeniedCrossTenant matrix AND a working ReasonAllowedBySupport exception. Every test function structure, every engine assertion, every wire tie-in carries over 1:1; the ONLY add is the secret-plaintext anchor + Sentinel projection assertion on allow paths.

The new file added zero scaffolding beyond canonicalVariablesProject, canonicalVariablesSecretPlaintext, canonicalProjectVariables, and variablesDenyBodyLeak.
    - canonicalVariablesProject deliberately uses distinct ids/slug/displayName from canonicalGrantsProject (different fixture namespace) so the two matrices cannot accidentally share fixture state through any future shared fake.
    - The "stolen scoped key planted in foreign home org" engine assertion is identical-shape to the grants matrix's: a Principal with OrganizationID=org_sibling carrying a Grant whose Scope.OrganizationID=org_acme, authorized against a Resource in org_sibling, is denied at the engine because the principal's home org no longer matches the grant scope's org. CapRead/CapWrite/CapAdmin axis is irrelevant — the cross-tenant guard fires first. Always pin this on every grant-containment test.

- What was implemented: PUT /v1/projects/{project_id}/variables — the
  writer half of the project-scoped variables surface, mirroring the
  existing PUT /v1/organizations/{org_id}/variables shape. The endpoint
  replaces the entire variable set for the project named by the
  {project_id} path parameter in one transaction (upsert each

- Remaining risks or follow-ups:
  - BE-0146 (contract tests for PUT /v1/projects/{project_id}/variables)
    is the natural next story; the fakeProjectVariableReplacer test
    double is already in place so the contract tests can be added
    without further test-helper churn.
  - BE-0147 (policy matrix for PUT /v1/projects/{project_id}/variables)
    is unblocked by this story — the route is registered with action
    env.write under projectIDResolver, so the policy matrix can be
    written as a sibling of the CapWrite-on-{project_id}-resolver
    matrix (projects_delete_policy_test.go) using the variables-
    flavoured leak guards (request-body anchored on caller-supplied
    distinctive ids + would-have-returned-data anchored on the
    seeded secret plaintext to prove a deny path never echoes a
    submitted secret).
  - Integration tests under YALLA_TEST_DATABASE_URL were verified by
    inspection; the standard story posture is to skip them when the
    env var is unset and rely on CI to run them with a real database.
- Learnings for future iterations:
  - The writer-variants pattern is now established at two scopes
    (org-level since BE-0089, project-level here): the only axes
    that change between scopes are the upsert key shape
    (organization_id, key) vs (organization_id, project_id, key)
    and the parent-existence check (OrganizationRepository.Get vs
    ProjectRepository.Get). Every other piece — buildVariableReplace
    validation, posixEnvVarName, value-size ceilings keyed on
    is_secret, audit counts-only metadata, projectVariableOf wire
    redaction, the *Tx/Querier asymmetry — is reused verbatim.
    Future scope-narrowing override tables (environment_variables /
    service_variables) should be able to follow the same template
    by widening the upsert key once more and pointing the parent-
    existence check at EnvironmentRepository / ServiceRepository.
  - The Python regex sweep approach is reliable for inserting a
    NEW positional NewHandler port when the anchor literal (here
    `fakeProjectVariableReader{}`) is unambiguous and structurally
    placed at the boundary. Two follow-up patterns must always be
    audited by hand after the sweep: (a) helpers that pass a named
    parameter at the new port's position (so the regex anchor
    misses them — search the symptom `vet: not enough arguments
    in call to NewHandler`), and (b) call sites where the new
    port's slot was already filled with `nil` by an earlier story
    (so the slot lives MID-arg-list, not at the trailing edge —
    these need a trailing `, nil)` insertion, not an
    insertion-in-the-middle). The all-nil newRouteTable forms are
    a structurally different sweep (count nils, append one more)
    and must be done as a separate pass — they share no anchor
    with the NewHandler churn.
  - When extending an existing test file with new repository tests,
    the established convention is to KEEP the file growing
    (project_variable_test.go went from 286 lines to ~450 with
    Upsert + DeleteByProjectExceptKeys coverage) rather than to
    fragment into a *_upsert_test.go / *_delete_test.go split —
    the test file is the per-resource focal point, not the
    per-method one. The service-level tests go in a separate
    project_variable_service_test.go so the unit-of-work surface
    (which depends on AuditRepository + ProjectRepository in
    addition to the variable repo) is exercised independently
    from the repository's own narrow methods.
  - projectVariablesWriteAction = "env.write" is the SAME string
    as the org-level envWriteAction (catalog action mapped to
    CapWrite) — they cannot diverge by definition because the
    policy engine reads ONE action string. The audit row's
    distinguishing axis is resource_kind (KindProject vs
    KindOrganization), not Action. Future scope-narrowing override
    tables (environment / service variables) MUST also use
    "env.write" for the same reason.

    LIST another tenant's variables but cannot REPLACE them.

    env-, and service-scoped grants cannot widen past their issued scope.

    via ReasonAllowedByGrant and the wire allow-path STILL redacts the
    secret row to output.Sentinel; project-level developer grant on a
    sibling project DENIES with ReasonDeniedOutOfScope (replacer never
    runs); project-level VIEWER grant on the target project DENIES (Viewer
    holds CapRead, not CapWrite); env-staging-scoped admin grant DENIES
    against parent project AND against parent env env.write on production
    (the production-not-implied property); service-scoped Admin grant
    DENIES against parent project, parent env env.write, and sibling
    service service.update; org-level Developer grant ALLOWS via
    ReasonAllowedByGrant (Developer holds CapWrite); org-level Viewer
    grant at the same scope DENIES (Viewer holds CapRead). Allow-path tie-
    ins also pin secret-row Sentinel projection and no-plaintext-in-body,
    deny-path tie-ins pin replacer-never-runs and
    postWriteProjectVariablesBodyLeak rejection of canonical project/var
    ids/keys/non-secret values AND secret plaintext AND the

  - The role-capability map for env.write differs from env.read at TWO

  - The reader-only scoped-child vertical pattern from BE-0142
    (project_variables) generalises one step further when the
    table already exists: BE-0148 lands JUST store + http + wiring
    + tests because migration 0002 already declared the environments
    table and migration 0011 already added its version + bump_version
    trigger. The Codebase Patterns entry pins this as a forwardable
    shape for every future hierarchy-table reader whose schema
    predates the story.
  - The new positional port goes at the TAIL of the newRouteTable
    and NewHandler signatures (immediately before the logger arg in
    NewHandler), not interspersed with related ports. The dominant
    NewHandler test-call shape ends `fakeProjectVariableReplacer{},
    nil)`, so a single Python regex sweep on that anchor handles
    44 of 47 call sites; the logger variant and the named-replacer
    outlier are parallel single-regex passes. Counting the trailing
    nils on the all-nil newRouteTable form (32 -> 33) is the only
    state-machine sweep that needs hand verification — projects_*
    _test.go variants whose `nil, nil, nil)` slot lives MID-arg-list
    (because earlier stories filled the new-port positions with nil
    already) need a separate regex.
  - The KindEnvironment Kind ("env") was already in domain/id.go
    from earlier work, so no domain layer changes were needed —
    KindEnvironment passes Kind.Valid() / ParseID() because it's in
    the validKinds map. Verifying this BEFORE writing the store
    layer saved an unneeded domain edit. (The pattern is: new
    Kinds for resources that have their own primary-key id space
    land in domain/id.go; an existing table that didn't yet have a
    handler doesn't need a new Kind.)
  - Environments carry NO credential material — the table stores
    only structural identifiers — so projectEnvironmentOf has no
    value-redaction chokepoint to declare. The projection still
    exists as a single chokepoint though, so a future column added
    to store.Environment is reviewed for its wire exposure here
    rather than leaking by default. This is the structural reason
    the contract test suite for BE-0148 doesn't carry the
    seeded-secret-plaintext leak guard that BE-0142's variant did;
    BE-0150 (policy matrix) won't need it either.
  - The tag set in routes.go grew tagEnvironments. project_grants
    used just tagProjects (the grant resource is a property of the
    project) but environments are first-class hierarchy nodes with
    their own /v1/environments/{environment_id} surface arriving
    in BE-0154, so the tag earns its place now rather than waiting.

  - TestListProjectEnvironmentsPolicyRevokedAndExpiredKeys — Disabled principal (revoked or expired credential) is denied 403 E_FORBIDDEN with ReasonDeniedPrincipalDisabled even with Owner role; reader never runs; deny body never echoes principal id, org id, or canonical environment data.
  - TestListProjectEnvironmentsPolicyWrongOrganizationPrincipal — wire-level cross-tenant test surfaces NotFound 404 from persistence (reader always called with home org id, never caller-controlled); engine-level subtests pin ReasonDeniedCrossTenant for every non-support role and ReasonAllowedBySupport for support (CapRead inside support cross-tenant exception).
  - TestListProjectEnvironmentsPolicyGrantContainment — project-scoped Viewer grant on target authorizes; sibling-project, env-scoped, and service-scoped grants all deny ReasonDeniedOutOfScope; org-level Viewer grant authorizes; engine-level cross-tenant deny for a key planted in a foreign org.   - For a reader-only project-scoped endpoint whose persistence row carries NO credential material (e.g. environments — only structural ids, slug, display_name, version, timestamps), the BE-0144 policy-matrix template applies one-for-one with two narrowings: (1) drop the secret-plaintext deny-body leak anchor (no field needs redaction), and (2) drop the "secret value still projects as output.Sentinel on allow paths even when authority came via grant" assertion. The four-test shape (role matrix / revoked+expired / wrong org / grant containment) stays identical, including the engine-level cross-tenant deny+support-exception subtests and the four wire tie-ins inside grant containment.
  - The action constants for variables vs environments are intentionally different despite living in the same hierarchy: variables route uses policy.ActionEnvRead ("env.read" — env-vars), environments route uses policy.ActionEnvironmentRead ("environment.read" — env *entity*). Both are CapRead, both go through projectIDResolver. Mixing them up would silently regress tenant isolation; always grep the route registration in routes.go and the existing project_environments_test.go OpenAPI assertion to confirm which action a route is gated on before writing the policy matrix.
  - The fakeProjectEnvironmentReader, listProjectEnvironmentsHandlerFor, getProjectEnvironments, decodeListProjectEnvironments, and seedEnvironmentWire helpers from project_environments_test.go (BE-0148) are sufficient scaffolding — no new fakes were needed. Confirms the pattern: the contract story (BE-0148) lands the test scaffolding, and the policy-matrix story (BE-0150) reuses it without addition.

## 2026-05-15 - BE-0151
- What was implemented: POST /v1/projects/{project_id}/environments, the first
  mutating endpoint on the environments surface. It creates an environment
  under the project named by the {project_id} path parameter, returning the
  source-of-truth row in a 201 yalla.output.v1 envelope.
  - internal/controlplane/store/environmentservice.go (new): EnvironmentService
    is the reference unit-of-work orchestrator. Create composes — in this
    fixed order, inside one Store.Write transaction — (1) validate the input
    before any database work runs, (2) confirm the parent project exists in
    (OrganizationID, ProjectID) — tenant-scoped, so a cross-tenant or unknown
    project_id surfaces as apierr.NotFound never a 500, (3) in-transaction
    authorize action environment.create against the resource org (defense-in-
    depth against grant changes between the HTTP RequireAuth gate and the
    write), (4) reserve quota against QuotaResourceEnvironments, (5) insert
    the environments row, (6) enqueue the environment.provision job, (7)
    append an immutable audit record under the actor's home organization
    with metadata {slug, project_id} — no secret material since environments
    carry none. Validation rejects invalid OrganizationID/ProjectID/
    EnvironmentID kinds (domain.ParseID + Kind check), non-canonical slugs
    (domain.ParseSlug), and unbounded/blank/control-char/non-UTF-8 display
    names (validateEnvironmentDisplayName), each as a typed FieldViolation
    naming the field but never echoing the submitted value. Actor
    organization missing is reported as apierr.Internal — a wiring error,
    not client input — so the audit row can never miss its tenant column.
    NewEnvironmentService rejects every nil dependency at construction so a
    misconfigured service fails fast rather than on first request.
  - internal/controlplane/store/environment.go: added EnvironmentRepository.
    Insert(ctx, tx, e) — writes a new environments row inside the supplied
    *Tx and returns the persisted row in environmentColumns order (the
    caller sees the database-assigned timestamps and the initial version
    without re-reading). The schema's composite (organization_id, project_id)
    FK to projects(organization_id, id) rejects an organization/project
    mismatch at the database; a duplicate (project_id, slug) tuple violates
    UNIQUE and is mapped by mapWriteError to apierr.Conflict (the same
    chokepoint projects/variables use), never a 500 leaking the constraint
    name. A nil *Tx is apierr.Internal.
  - internal/controlplane/httpapi/project_environments.go: added the
    EnvironmentCreator narrow port (Create(ctx, store.CreateEnvironmentInput)
    -> (store.Environment, error)) — *store.EnvironmentService satisfies it
    in production; tests supply fakeEnvironmentCreator. The handler
    (createProjectEnvironmentHandler) reads the principal off the context
    (RequireAuth attaches it), rejects a wired-nil creator with the typed
    errNoEnvironmentCreator internal error, strictly decodes the request
    body via validate.DecodeJSON (rejects unknown fields and oversized
    payloads, never echoes input), forwards the resolved (principal home
    org id, path {project_id}, decoded EnvironmentID/Slug/DisplayName,
    principal id+kind, actor home org id, request id, correlation id)
    tuple to the creator, and renders the resulting row through
    projectEnvironmentOf in a 201 yalla.output.v1 envelope. The request
    body intentionally exposes no organization_id or project_id field —
    the strict decoder rejects either as an unknown field at 400 — so a
    caller cannot point the write at another tenant or another project by
    smuggling them in the body.
  - internal/controlplane/httpapi/routes.go: registered the POST route
    with OperationID=createProjectEnvironment, Tags=[tagProjects,
    tagEnvironments] (the same dual-tag shape PUT
    /v1/projects/{project_id}/variables uses), RequiresAuth=true,
    RequiredAction=policy.ActionEnvironmentCreate (CapWrite in the
    catalog), SuccessStatus=201, resolver=projectIDResolver.
  - internal/controlplane/httpapi/server.go: NewHandler signature gained
    the environmentCreator port (one new positional arg threaded into
    newRouteTable).
  - cmd/yalla-api/main.go: wires *store.EnvironmentService at startup
    composed over dataStore + project repository + environment repository
    + placeholder Authorizer/QuotaReserver/JobEnqueuer (the same
    alwaysAllowAuthorizer / noopQuotaReserver / noopJobEnqueuer
    ProjectService uses until the real adapters land) + auditRepo.

  go test ./... PASS (Postgres-backed integration suites skip without
  YALLA_TEST_DATABASE_URL — they validate in CI), go test -race
  ./internal/controlplane/... PASS.
- Remaining risks/follow-ups:
  - The Authorizer/QuotaReserver/JobEnqueuer wired in cmd/yalla-api/main.go
    are still placeholders (alwaysAllowAuthorizer, noopQuotaReserver,
    noopJobEnqueuer) — the real adapters land in their own stories. The
    HTTP RequireAuth middleware is the authoritative gate today; the
    in-transaction Authorizer is defense-in-depth.
  - BE-0152 (contract tests) and BE-0153 (policy matrix) for POST
    /v1/projects/{project_id}/environments stay open. The contract-test
    surface already exists in project_environments_create_test.go;
    BE-0152 can either be marked complete against the same file or
    extend it with additional fixture-driven cases. BE-0153 follows the
    BE-0150 environment GET policy matrix one-for-one but for
    environment.create (CapWrite).

- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - New mutating endpoint on a hierarchy resource whose persistence
    table already exists (environments table from migration 0002 +
    version trigger from 0011 — same pattern BE-0148 used for the GET
    reader): the create story collapses to (a) one *Repository.Insert
    method on the existing repo file, (b) a new *Service file
    (environmentservice.go) that mirrors projectservice.go for the
    unit-of-work composition, (c) a new *Creator port + handler in the
    existing http file alongside the GET handler, (d) a new POST route
    in routes.go, (e) NewHandler / newRouteTable signature gains one
    positional port. No migration, no repository file rename, no
    domain id package changes.
  - Mechanical handler-port churn (n test files have to receive a
    positional zero-value fake or an extra nil) is best handled by a
    one-shot javascript walk that locates the last top-level comma of
    every NewHandler/newRouteTable invocation and inserts the new arg
    before the final positional (logger or the new port itself for
    newRouteTable). The depth=0 split tolerates nested struct literals
    like fakeProjectGrantReplacer{} without confusion. A sed-style
    line-anchored substitution would have failed on the calls that
    wrap differently — the AST-aware comma walk handles them
    uniformly.
  - The orchestrator's first step must be the tenant-scoped
    parent-Get, NOT the in-tx authorize. Authorize takes (action,
    resource_org_id); if the project is wrong we have no proof yet
    that the action even has a resource to apply to. Get-first also
    short-circuits a cross-tenant or unknown id into a clean NotFound
    before any quota or audit cost is paid; deferring it would either
    disguise NotFound as Forbidden (which confirms the foreign
    resource's existence) or open a transaction that rolls back after
    every step. The same ordering is now load-bearing for every
    hierarchy create endpoint that follows (env-scoped service creates,
    etc.).
  - The store layer must keep its action/job/quota names as plain
    string constants in the service file
    (environmentCreateAction = "environment.create",
    environmentProvisionJob = "environment.provision",
    QuotaResourceEnvironments from quota.go) rather than importing the
    policy/jobs/quota catalogs. The catalogs are private to their
    packages; the duplication is intentional. The HTTP layer
    references the typed policy.ActionEnvironmentCreate constant in
    routes.go for the same reason — the wire boundary type-checks
    against the policy catalog, the store boundary doesn't.
  - The audit record's metadata{slug, project_id} carries no secret
    material — environment slugs are canonical [a-z0-9-], project ids
    are structural — so no redaction chokepoint is needed at the
    projection, unlike variables which need an output.Sentinel. This
    is the same narrowing BE-0148 documented for the GET reader: when
    a resource table stores only structural data, the projection
    still exists as a single review chokepoint but does not need a
    redaction transform.

## 2026-05-15 - BE-0153 - Add policy matrix coverage for POST /v1/projects/{project_id}/environments
- Added `internal/controlplane/httpapi/projects_environments_create_policy_test.go`
  (~720 lines, four top-level tests) modelling the same projectIDResolver-

  CapWrite role/cross-tenant split BE-0123 / BE-0147 use.
- Tests added:
  - `TestCreateProjectEnvironmentPolicyMatrixRoles` drives all six built-in
    roles through real NewHandler + real policy.NewEngine(). The matrix
    splits on CapWrite: Owner/Admin/Developer allow via
    ReasonAllowedByRole (201, creator reached with the principal's home
    org + path project_id + grantee's id as ActorID); Viewer/CI/Support
    deny via ReasonDeniedNoCapability (403, creator never runs, body
    leak guard fires on the canonical request body and the canned
    created-environment row).
  - `TestCreateProjectEnvironmentPolicyRevokedAndExpiredKeys` pins
    `principal.Disabled = true` is load-bearing: an Owner credential
    that has been revoked or expired is denied with
    ReasonDeniedPrincipalDisabled, the creator never runs, and the
    body never echoes the principal id, the home org, the path
    project_id, or the request body.
  - `TestCreateProjectEnvironmentPolicyWrongOrganizationPrincipal` pins
    the cross-tenant boundary. Wire-level: an attacker in org_attacker
    hitting POST /v1/projects/{prj_victim}/environments — handler
    derives org from the principal's home, reaches the orchestrator
    with (org_attacker, prj_victim_envs), creator returns NotFound,
    wire surfaces 404 E_NOT_FOUND, body never echoes org_victim. Then
    the engine-level twin: a foreign-org resource against every role
    INCLUDING Support is denied via ReasonDeniedCrossTenant (CapWrite
    is outside the support cross-tenant exception — the load-bearing
    distinction from environment.read in BE-0150 which DID admit
    support cross-tenant via ReasonAllowedBySupport).
  - `TestCreateProjectEnvironmentPolicyGrantContainment` proves all
    four scoped-grant containments: project-scoped Admin grant on THIS
    project allows (ReasonAllowedByGrant; wire 201, creator reached
    with home org + path project_id + grantee actor id); project-
    scoped Admin grant on a SIBLING project denies
    (ReasonDeniedOutOfScope; wire 403, creator never runs, body leak
    guard fires); project-scoped Viewer grant denies
    (ReasonDeniedNoCapability — scope is sufficient, role's caps are
    not); env-scoped grant on staging denies the parent project
    (ReasonDeniedOutOfScope; wire tie-in proves creator never runs);
    env grant on staging cannot reach production (ReasonDeniedOutOfScope
    on env.write); service-scoped grant denies sibling service, denies
    parent env.write, and denies the parent project's
    environment.create (wire tie-in proves creator never runs); org-
    level Viewer grant denies (ReasonDeniedNoCapability — same
    capability gap that pins the wire CapWrite property); org-level
    Developer grant allows (ReasonAllowedByGrant; wire 201, creator
    reached with home org + path project_id + sa_org_dev actor id);
    project-scoped Admin grant planted in a foreign home org is denied
    by the cross-tenant guard.
- Verification:
  - `gofmt -w internal/controlplane/httpapi/projects_environments_create_policy_test.go` — no diff
  - `go vet ./...` — clean
  - `go test ./...` — all packages pass
  - `go test -race ./internal/controlplane/httpapi/...` — clean
  - `goimports` is not installed locally, so the formatting step is
    `gofmt` only (same posture as BE-0150).
- Remaining risks / follow-ups: none for this story. Mirrors BE-0150
  and BE-0123 verbatim except for the action constant and the resource
  Kind, so a future regression in projectIDResolver, the action
  catalog, or builtinRoleCaps fails here.
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - The most analogous template for a "policy matrix for a project-
    scoped MUTATING endpoint" is BE-0150 (project-scoped resolver
    shape and cross-tenant-as-NotFound) intersected with BE-0123
    (CapWrite role split and ALL-roles-cross-tenant-deny including
    Support). Copy structure from BE-0150 for the wire shape and from
    BE-0123 for the engine matrix.
  - The cross-tenant wire-level test for a CapWrite endpoint with a
    projectIDResolver MUST expect the creator to be called exactly
    once (engine admits same-tenant resource because resolver pins
    org to the principal's home; persistence layer rejects). This is
    the same posture BE-0150 establishes for the GET — the only
    difference is that on a CapWrite endpoint, the engine's support
    cross-tenant exception does NOT apply, so the engine deny matrix
    enumerates ALL six roles (including Support), not just five.
  - The wire-tie-ins MUST verify `callCount == 0` for every deny
    path. `gotInput.OrganizationID == "" && gotInput.ActorID == ""`
    is not load-bearing on its own because the fake's pointer fields
    are only populated when called; `callCount` is the structural
    signal that the creator never ran.
  - For an env-grant containment test, the existing GET file uses
    `policy.ActionEnvWrite` on a production env scope to prove the
    staging-grant can't reach production. The CREATE file needs the
    same `ActionEnvWrite` probe AND a fresh
    `ActionEnvironmentCreate`-on-parent-project probe because the
    parent-project resource is what projectIDResolver builds, and
    that's the only resource the route's RequireAuth actually
    authorizes against.
  - The deny-body leak guard for a CREATE endpoint needs to needle
    the caller-supplied request-body fields AND the canned creator-
    output row. Re-using the GET file's `environmentsDenyBodyLeak`
    would miss the request-body echo case, so a per-endpoint leak
    guard (`createEnvironmentDenyBodyLeak`) is justified.
  - The shared fixtures `canonicalEnvironmentsProject`,
    `seedEnvironmentWire`, `fakeEnvironmentCreator`, `orgPrincipal`,
    `createProjectEnvironmentHandlerFor`, `postProjectEnvironments`,
    `createProjectEnvironmentRequestBody`,
    `decodeCreateProjectEnvironment`, `decodeCreateProjectEnvironmentError`,
    and `decodeError` already cover everything this test file needs.
    No new scaffolding beyond two small canonical-fixture builders
    and one leak-guard helper was required, matching the BE-0150
    learning that a new policy-matrix file should be ~0 KB of new
    fixtures.

## 2026-05-15 - BE-0154
- What was implemented: GET /v1/environments/{environment_id}, the
  bare top-level environment lookup-by-id endpoint — the first
  customer-facing route that addresses an environment by its global
  env_id without carrying the parent project_id in the path.
  - internal/controlplane/store/environment.go: EnvironmentRepository
    grew GetByID(ctx, q, organizationID, environmentID) — a
    tenant-scoped SELECT under the composite (organization_id, id)
    predicate, so a cross-tenant or unknown environment_id yields
    apierr.NotFound("environment", env_id) rather than another tenant's
    row, and never a 500 leaking the cause. EnvironmentReader grew
    GetEnvironment(ctx, organizationID, environmentID) — the adapter
    composes GetByID inside Store.Read (a short-lived read-only
    transaction) so the predicate's tenant guarantee is inherited by
    the HTTP boundary for free. The constructor (NewEnvironmentReader)
    needed no change because it builds the repositories the new method
    uses.
  - internal/controlplane/store/environment_test.go: six new
    integration tests against an isolated migrated Postgres database —
    GetByID happy path (returns the persisted row through
    environmentColumns with Version=1 for a fresh INSERT), GetByID
    tenant-scoping (a cross-tenant (orgA, envB_id) tuple yields
    apierr.NotFound and the error string never echoes envB.ID,
    projB.ID, or envB.Slug), GetByID unknown-id (same NotFound shape),
    and three reader-level mirrors (happy path, cross-tenant
    rejection, unknown id). The cross-tenant tests anchor on
    yerr.CodeNotFound + a leak guard over the cross-tenant identifier
    set so a future regression in the SQL predicate is caught at the
    persistence boundary.
  - internal/controlplane/httpapi/environments.go (new): the
    HTTP-layer vertical for the new endpoint. EnvironmentReader is a
    new narrow port (GetEnvironment) — distinct from
    ProjectEnvironmentReader (which backs the LIST endpoint) so a
    handler change to one doesn't ripple through the other.
    environmentIDResolver builds policy.Resource{Kind:
    domain.KindEnvironment, Scope: {OrganizationID: principal.home,
    EnvironmentID: path.environment_id}} — pinning OrgID to the
    principal's home (never the caller's id) is the structural
    anti-spoof. The resolver deliberately does NOT pin ProjectID
    because the bare top-level path carries no parent project_id;
    that's a load-bearing decision documented inline (see "Resolver
    cannot pin ProjectID" pattern below). getEnvironmentHandler is
    thin: read principal, check reader, call port, render
    yalla.output.v1 envelope through projectEnvironmentOf — the
    existing wire-shape projection is reused, so the GET-by-id
    response is byte-identical to one element of the LIST response
    (modulo the wrapping {environment: ...} object instead of
    {environments: [...]}).
  - internal/controlplane/httpapi/environments_test.go (new): 11
    contract tests in package httpapi exercising the real NewHandler +
    real policy engine (fake Authenticator + fake EnvironmentReader
    only) — happy-path forwarding (org_id and env_id reach the reader
    verbatim, every projectEnvironment field renders correctly),
    not-found typed envelope (E_NOT_FOUND + 404), cross-tenant behaves
    as the same NotFound (no oracle), unauthenticated 401 (no reader
    call), invalid credentials 401 (uniform message, no token echo),
    reader outage 503 (typed E_UNAVAILABLE + no raw cause leak),
    nil-reader-wiring 500 (E_INTERNAL), envelope shape lock
    (asserts the documented field set against a generic decode so a
    future store.Environment column added without updating
    projectEnvironmentOf is caught), bearer-token never-logged guard
    (slog JSON handler over a buffer), OpenAPI route registration
    (operationId getEnvironment, RequiredAction environment.read,
    tagEnvironments, single environment_id path param, non-nil
    resolver), and two environmentIDResolver unit tests (pins home
    org + path env_id; no panic when called for a context with no
    principal).
  - internal/controlplane/httpapi/routes.go: newRouteTable signature
    grew one trailing parameter (environmentReader EnvironmentReader)
    and registered the new route entry between the
    createProjectEnvironment route and getOrganization. The route
    description is the longest in the table so an agent reading the
    OpenAPI document discovers the load-bearing distinction the
    handler enforces (org-wide read roles allowed; scoped grants
    structurally denied because the resolver cannot pin ProjectID;
    cross-tenant id is 404 by tenant-scoped persistence; resource
    carries no credentials).
  - internal/controlplane/httpapi/server.go: NewHandler grew the
    same new positional parameter (environmentReader EnvironmentReader)
    immediately before logger, and forwards it to newRouteTable.
  - cmd/yalla-api/main.go: passes the existing projectEnvironments
    (which is *store.EnvironmentReader) twice — once for the
    ProjectEnvironmentReader port (LIST) and once for the new
    EnvironmentReader port (GET-by-id). The same store-side adapter
    satisfies both ports because both methods are on the same
    *store.EnvironmentReader struct; no second startup wiring is
    needed.
  - 33 *_test.go files swept to add fakeEnvironmentReader{} as the
    new last positional arg before the trailing nil) or logger) on
    NewHandler call sites, plus 9 newRouteTable stubs (7 all-nil
    forms, 2 with-named-fakes forms) updated to add one more nil/fake
    in the same positional slot.
- Files changed:
  - internal/controlplane/store/environment.go
  - internal/controlplane/store/environment_test.go
  - internal/controlplane/httpapi/environments.go (new)
  - internal/controlplane/httpapi/environments_test.go (new)
  - internal/controlplane/httpapi/routes.go
  - internal/controlplane/httpapi/server.go
  - cmd/yalla-api/main.go
  - 33 internal/controlplane/httpapi/*_test.go files (sweep adding
    fakeEnvironmentReader + nil to NewHandler / newRouteTable
    call sites)
- Verification run: gofmt -w ., go mod tidy, go vet ./..., go test
  ./..., go test -race ./..., plus targeted go test -v -run on the
  new env tests. goimports not installed locally — same posture as
  prior stories.
- Results: all green. Postgres integration tests skip when
  YALLA_TEST_DATABASE_URL is unset (the documented contract); the
  new store-level tests follow the same skip posture as every other
  *_test.go in store/. The httpapi-layer tests run unconditionally
  against fake ports and all pass under -race.
- Remaining risks / follow-ups:
  - Scoped-grant principals (project-, environment-, service-scoped
    grants WITHOUT an org-wide role) are denied at the policy
    middleware on this endpoint by structural design — the resolver
    cannot pin ProjectID without a DB lookup, and the engine's
    covers() rule requires every level the grant pins to match the
    resource. They must use the parent-scoped GET
    /v1/projects/{project_id}/environments instead. This is
    documented inline in the route description, the resolver doc, and
    the handler doc, so BE-0156 (the policy matrix story this story
    unblocks) can assert the deny matrix on the bare endpoint without
    changing the policy engine.
  - The endpoint is read-only; no audit event is emitted on success
    (matches every other GET endpoint). A future "audit denied
    authorization decisions" story (separate from BE-0154) would add
    that behavior at the middleware seam, not in this handler.
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - Resolver cannot pin ProjectID for a bare /v1/{resource}/{id}
    path (BE-0154 environments, will recur for /v1/services/{id}):
    the policy engine's Scope.covers() rule (internal/controlplane/
    policy/policy.go) requires each level the grant pins to match
    the resource; an empty resource ProjectID against a grant with
    pinned ProjectID returns false, so project-/env-/service-scoped
    grants are structurally denied at the middleware on bare
    lookup-by-id endpoints. The accepted design is: resolver pins
    {OrgID = principal.home, EnvironmentID = path.env_id} (just the
    one scope leg the path carries), the middleware admits org-wide
    read roles + org-wide grants, scoped-grant principals are
    redirected to the parent-scoped /v1/projects/{project_id}/
    environments endpoint. Document this in the route description,
    the resolver doc, and the handler doc so a reader doesn't
    interpret the deny as a bug. BE-0156 (the matching policy
    matrix) tests the deny — it is part of the contract, not a gap.
  - Reusing an existing wire-shape projection across the LIST and
    GET-by-id endpoints (projectEnvironmentOf for both
    listProjectEnvironmentsPayload.Environments[i] and
    getEnvironmentPayload.Environment) means a single chokepoint
    reviews any future store.Environment column for wire exposure.
    The new GET-by-id handler imports nothing new from the store
    package because the projection lives in project_environments.go
    and is package-private — same package, free reuse.
  - When a new HTTP port is added to the same store-side struct
    that already satisfies an existing port (here:
    *store.EnvironmentReader satisfies both ProjectEnvironmentReader
    via ListProjectEnvironments and the new EnvironmentReader via
    GetEnvironment), cmd/yalla-api/main.go does NOT need a second
    construction — pass the same projectEnvironments value twice.
    This is the cheapest wiring posture for "second method on
    existing reader" stories.
  - The newRouteTable test-stub sweep has TWO shapes: (a) the
    all-nil form newRouteTable(runtime.BuildInfo{}, nil*N) which
    needs one more nil per signature change (now 35 nils after this
    story), and (b) the named-fakes form ending in
    ", fakeEnvironmentCreator{})" or
    ", fakeEnvironmentCreator{}, nil)" which needs one more positional
    fake/nil. Both were swept programmatically with regexes anchored
    on those exact tails — server_test.go has TWO such call sites
    (lines 591 + 614) and a per-file regex over each handles them
    in one pass.
  - Do NOT add a CodeStoreUnavailable constant when writing a new
    test — it does not exist in internal/errors/. The store-outage
    typed code is yerr.CodeUnavailable (single source of truth in
    internal/errors/errors.go); StoreUnavailable() and
    QueueUnavailable() both wrap it, the apierr_test.go matrix pins
    the mapping. A first-pass test that uses the wrong constant
    name will fail go vet at the "undefined: yerr.CodeXxx" stage
    before any test runs.
  - The "missing principal on context" guard (errNoPrincipalOnContext)
    is shared across handlers. Reuse it in any new handler that
    reads a principal — a handler that defines its own sentinel
    would split the typed-error surface for no benefit.

## 2026-05-15 - BE-0156
- What was implemented: policy-matrix coverage for GET
  /v1/environments/{environment_id}, proving the bare-id route's
  authorization contract cannot be bypassed by — or leak an
  environment row because of — the principal's role, revoked or
  expired credentials, home organization, or scoped grants. The
  contract test (BE-0154) proves WHAT the endpoint returns; this
  matrix proves WHEN it is allowed to return anything at all.
  - internal/controlplane/httpapi/environments_get_policy_test.go
    (new, ~570 lines): four matrix tests driving the real
    NewHandler + real policy.NewEngine() (the production request
    path, fake Authenticator only).
    - TestGetEnvironmentPolicyMatrixRoles: all six built-in roles
      (owner/admin/developer/viewer/ci/support) ALLOW via
      ReasonAllowedByRole at a same-tenant resource, the reader is
      called with (principal.OrganizationID, path environment_id),
      and the wire body carries the canonical environment in a
      stable yalla.output.v1 envelope. ci runs as a service-account
      kind, every other role runs as a user-kind principal.
    - TestGetEnvironmentPolicyRevokedAndExpiredKeys: a Disabled
      principal carrying an Owner role is 403 with
      ReasonDeniedPrincipalDisabled, the reader never runs
      (callCount=0, gotOrg="", gotEnv=""), and the denied body
      never echoes the principal id, the organization id, or any
      seeded environment identifier — the load-bearing property
      that a revoked or expired credential cannot read an
      environment of its former tenant.
    - TestGetEnvironmentPolicyWrongOrganizationPrincipal: pins the
      engine-vs-wire split for cross-tenant access. On the WIRE,
      an attacker in org_attacker hitting GET
      /v1/environments/{env_victim} surfaces as 404 E_NOT_FOUND
      (the resolver pins OrganizationID to principal.home, the
      engine admits the same-tenant resource, and the tenant-
      scoped GetByID rejects the (org_attacker, env_victim) pair);
      the reader IS called once but with the attacker's home org,
      so a production store could not have surfaced the victim's
      row regardless. The body never echoes the foreign org id.
      At the ENGINE LAYER (independent of the resolver), every
      non-support role denies a foreign-org Resource via
      ReasonDeniedCrossTenant, and Support allows via
      ReasonAllowedBySupport — pinning the documented support
      exception for CapRead actions even though the customer-facing
      route cannot reach that engine branch by construction.
    - TestGetEnvironmentPolicyGrantContainment: the load-bearing
      distinction from the projectIDResolver siblings. The
      acceptance criteria's three containment properties are pinned
      at the engine against their natural resources (project-scoped
      Viewer ALLOWS environment.read at a project resource, sibling
      DENIES; env-staging grant doesn't reach env.write on
      production; service grant doesn't reach env.write on the
      parent environment), THEN — because environmentIDResolver
      pins NO ProjectID leg — every scoped-key type is also
      proven DENIED on THIS endpoint by ReasonDeniedOutOfScope,
      even when the grant names the target environment's own
      project (a target-project Viewer grant) or the target
      environment's own id (an env-target Admin grant). Wire tie-
      ins for project-scoped, env-scoped, and service-scoped keys
      all 403 with ReasonDeniedOutOfScope, reader never reached
      (callCount=0), no canonical environment data echoed. The
      org-level Viewer grant ALLOWS via ReasonAllowedByGrant
      end-to-end (its grant scope pins nothing past
      OrganizationID, so covers() admits a resource without
      ProjectID), the reader reached on (home_org, path env_id).
      Engine-twin: a project-scoped grant from org_acme planted
      on a principal whose home org is org_sibling is denied
      independently of CapRead/CapWrite — the cross-tenant guard
      fires before the grant is even considered.
  - internal/controlplane/httpapi/environments_get_policy_test.go
    introduces ONE new helper local to the file:
    getEnvironmentByIDHandlerForIdentity(id, authErr, reader). The
    BE-0154 contract test's getEnvironmentHandlerFor(t, reader)
    bakes in a single canonical principal via authForEnvGet and is
    unsuitable for a matrix; the new helper mirrors
    listProjectsHandlerFor / listProjectEnvironmentsHandlerFor's
    shape and uses the shared fakeAuthenticator from
    middleware_test.go. No changes to the contract test file or
    its 9 existing tests.
  - ralph/prd.json: BE-0156 passes=true. Remaining open: 502/614.
- Verification run:
  - gofmt -l . (clean)
  - go mod tidy (clean)
  - go vet ./... (clean)
  - go test ./... (all packages pass)
  - go test -race ./internal/controlplane/httpapi/... (passes)
- Remaining risks / follow-ups:
  - BE-0156's structural sibling stories for the rest of the
    bare-id family (BE-0186 service.read on /v1/services/{service_id},
    BE-0189 service.update, BE-0192 service.delete, etc.) can
    copy this shape verbatim — same suppression of the support
    cross-tenant exception on the wire by construction, same
    universal scoped-grant deny via ReasonDeniedOutOfScope, same
    org-level role + org-level Viewer/Developer/Admin grant as
    the only allow vectors. The action-constant gotcha (env vs
    environment) does NOT apply to services because there is
    only one service.read in the catalog.
  - The matrix proves grant-only principals cannot use this
    endpoint at all. The parent-scoped GET
    /v1/projects/{project_id}/environments (BE-0148/BE-0150)
    remains the route for project- and env-scoped keys to address
    an environment by its (project, env) tuple. If a future story
    adds a service-scoped or env-scoped lookup-by-id endpoint
    that DOES want to admit scoped keys, the resolver will need
    to do a tenant-scoped Get FIRST to resolve the parent
    project_id before the policy engine runs — an architectural
    choice with its own consequences (the resolver gains I/O, the
    tenant-scoped Get becomes part of the auth path, and a
    cross-tenant id is detected at the resolver instead of the
    handler). Not in scope for BE-0156 — the docstring on
    environmentIDResolver and the route description already
    pre-empt the confusion.
  - golangci-lint / staticcheck / govulncheck still not installed
    locally (documented in earlier iterations).
- Learnings for future iterations:
  - When a contract test (BE-0154) bakes in a single canonical
    principal through a hardcoded authenticator (authForEnvGet),
    do NOT refactor the existing helper to accept identity — that
    cascades through every test in the contract file. Add a
    parallel identity-injected helper LOCAL to the policy test
    file, modelled on the listFooHandlerFor(id, authErr, reader)
    shape from projects_test.go / project_environments_test.go,
    and reuse the shared fakeAuthenticator from middleware_test.go.
    Two helpers in two files is structurally simpler than one
    helper with two call shapes; the contract suite stays
    unchanged.
  - Bare-id resolvers (path carries only the resource id, no
    parent ids) have a SYSTEMATIC consequence the matrix must
    pin: the engine's one-way Scope.covers() rule
    (internal/controlplane/policy/policy.go) requires every level
    the grant pins to match the resource scope. A grant with
    pinned ProjectID cannot cover a resource scope without
    ProjectID, so EVERY project-, env-, and service-scoped
    grant — including grants on the target environment's own
    id — is structurally denied by ReasonDeniedOutOfScope. The
    matrix must pin this in BOTH directions: the engine-level
    containment properties from the acceptance criteria
    (sibling-project, production-not-implied, parent-secret-non-
    leak) at their natural resources, AND a fixture set that
    proves a target-id grant ALSO denies at this resolver,
    because that's the regression direction a future relaxation
    of covers() (admitting EnvID=env_X to cover Resource with
    EnvID=env_X regardless of ProjectID) would break.
  - The action-constant gotcha pinned in BE-0150 cuts deeper than
    documented: env-vars (env.read / env.write — variables under
    /v1/organizations/{org_id}/variables and
    /v1/projects/{project_id}/variables) and env entities
    (environment.read / environment.update — the env entity
    itself on /v1/projects/{project_id}/environments and
    /v1/environments/{environment_id}) use DIFFERENT catalog
    constants even at the bare-id route. Confirm the action by
    reading routes.go AT the route registration BEFORE writing
    the matrix — for /v1/environments/{environment_id} the line
    is "RequiredAction: string(policy.ActionEnvironmentRead)"
    (the entity action), NOT ActionEnvRead.
  - Reader-running-on-deny-path counters (callCount=0, gotOrg="",
    gotEnv="") are the structural anti-leak guard the matrix
    needs alongside the body-echo leak guard. The body guard
    proves the renderer didn't echo data; the counter guard
    proves the data wasn't read in the first place — so a
    production store with a future "log on read" side effect
    cannot silently observe the cross-tenant or out-of-scope
    request. Both directions are needed because a future
    regression could land either way (the renderer could grow a
    "render on 403" mode without the reader running, or the
    reader could run despite the engine denying through a
    middleware ordering bug).

## 2026-05-15 - BE-0157
- What was implemented: PATCH /v1/environments/{environment_id}, the
  partial-update endpoint for environments through the Yalla
  control-plane API. The store-layer orchestrator commits desired-state
  and the immutable audit record in one transaction; the HTTP layer is
  thin and threads the principal's home organization + path
  environment_id into the store, never trusting a caller-supplied org
  id. Mirrors the BE-0127 (PATCH project) pattern exactly: same
  validator shape, same buildXxxUpdate split, same classifyXxxConcurrencyMiss
  helper, same Update-path-trusts-HTTP-gate authorization model.
  - internal/controlplane/store/environment.go: added
    EnvironmentRepository.Update (slug + display_name, tenant scoped
    by composite (organization_id, id) predicate, *Tx-only mutation,
    optimistic concurrency via ifMatchVersion *int64) and
    classifyEnvironmentConcurrencyMiss (disambiguate gone vs stale on
    the version-checked UPDATE returning zero rows — runs inside the
    same tx so the disambiguation is consistent with the failed
    UPDATE). The UPDATE touches only the mutable columns
    (slug, display_name) and never the composite
    (organization_id, project_id) tenant key, so parent reparenting
    cannot happen by accident — and is not exposed through this
    endpoint by design (an environment belongs to exactly one project
    for its lifetime).
  - internal/controlplane/store/environmentservice.go: added
    UpdateEnvironmentInput (OrganizationID, EnvironmentID, *Slug,
    *DisplayName, *IfMatchVersion, Actor*, RequestID, CorrelationID),
    EnvironmentService.Update orchestrator, buildEnvironmentUpdate
    validator (split out + unit-testable, rejects empty patches as
    400 InvalidInput). Added environmentUpdateAction const. The
    orchestrator reads current row, optionally enforces If-Match
    pre-check (stale -> ConflictStale with row's authoritative
    version), applies the patch in-memory, then calls
    EnvironmentRepository.Update under the same *Tx, then appends
    the audit event — all in ONE Store.Write. Unlike Create, the
    orchestrator does NOT invoke the in-tx Authorizer or QuotaReserver
    — the HTTP RequireAuth gate is authoritative for the update path
    (the in-tx Authorize is reserved for Create's race against grant
    changes during quota reservation). Update-path-trusts-HTTP-gate is
    a load-bearing pattern: a Postgres assertion in
    TestEnvironmentServiceUpdateSuccess proves authz/quota/jobs are
    untouched.
  - internal/controlplane/httpapi/environments.go: added
    EnvironmentUpdater port + updateEnvironmentHandler. Request shape:
    only the {environment_id} path parameter, an optional If-Match
    header (parsed via the shared parseIfMatchVersion helper), and a
    strictly-decoded JSON body carrying optional pointer fields `slug`
    and `display_name`. The body intentionally exposes no
    organization_id, project_id, or environment_id field — tenant
    isolation is structural. Response is yalla.output.v1 carrying
    {environment: projectEnvironment} (same wire shape as GET) plus
    the row's new version mirrored into the ETag response header.
    Reuses the parseIfMatchVersion + writeOrganizationETag helpers
    that organizations.go already defined; no new shared helpers
    introduced.
  - internal/controlplane/httpapi/routes.go: registered the new
    apiRoute under tagEnvironments with RequiresAuth=true,
    RequiredAction=policy.ActionEnvironmentUpdate,
    resolver=environmentIDResolver. The path carries no parent
    project_id, so the resource scope pins only OrganizationID +
    EnvironmentID — project-, environment-, and service-scoped grants
    are denied at the boundary by the engine's covers() rule (a grant
    with a pinned ProjectID cannot cover a resource with no
    ProjectID); principals whose only access is a scoped grant must
    use a parent-scoped route. Added the OpenAPI operation
    `updateEnvironment`.
  - internal/controlplane/httpapi/server.go: NewHandler signature
    gained EnvironmentUpdater (one new positional arg threaded into
    newRouteTable). newRouteTable likewise gained the env updater
    parameter. Doc comment updated to name the new dependency.
  - cmd/yalla-api/main.go: builds the EnvironmentService once and
    passes it BOTH as EnvironmentCreator (POST) AND as
    EnvironmentUpdater (PATCH) at startup — the single
    *store.EnvironmentService now satisfies both narrow ports.
  - internal/controlplane/store/environment_update_test.go (new): six
    integration tests against isolated migrated Postgres — Update

  - internal/controlplane/httpapi/environments_update_test.go (new):

- Remaining risks / follow-ups:
  - Two pre-existing tests fail when YALLA_TEST_DATABASE_URL is set:
    `TestEnvironmentRepoListByProjectReturnsDeterministicOrdering`
    (asserts seeded slug equals literal "production" but
    testutil.Factory.slug() mints `production-<token>-<n>`) and
    `TestProjectVariableServiceReplaceCrossTenantProjectIsNotFound`
    (asserts the cross-tenant project_id does NOT appear in the
    NotFound message, but apierr.NotFound names the missing id by
    construction). Both failures reproduce at the pre-BE-0157 HEAD
    commit (fe352a68) — they are NOT introduced by this story. The
    Ralph quality-checks contract runs go test without a DB, where
    both tests skip via testutil.RequireMigratedDB. Future iterations
    that touch testutil.Factory.slug() or apierr.NotFound's wire
    shape should fix these assertions.
  - The PATCH endpoint does not change parent project_id. An
    environment belongs to exactly one project for its lifetime; a
    move/reparent operation, if ever needed, would belong to a
    separate endpoint behind its own action constant.
- Learnings for future iterations:
  - The BE-0127 pattern (PATCH project) and BE-0157 pattern (PATCH
    environment) are now the canonical shape for ALL deep-resource
    PATCH endpoints (PATCH service, PATCH variables/{key}, etc.).
    Every future PATCH against a bare-id route should: (1) put the
    validated patch in a buildXxxUpdate helper split out of the
    orchestrator (unit-testable, rejects empty patches as 400, never
    echoes submitted values in violations), (2) put the desired-state
    write + audit append in ONE Store.Write transaction, (3) do the
    If-Match pre-check INSIDE the transaction BEFORE the row-bumping
    UPDATE (so a trivial no-op patch with a stale If-Match still
    surfaces ConflictStale rather than masking it), (4) trust the
    HTTP RequireAuth gate for authorization (DO NOT call
    in-transaction Authorize — that is Create's defence-in-depth
    against grant-change races during quota reservation), (5)
    classify a version-checked UPDATE returning zero rows with a
    classifyXxxConcurrencyMiss helper that disambiguates
    gone-vs-stale via a tenant-scoped Get in the same tx, (6) mirror
    the row's new version into the ETag response header via
    writeOrganizationETag (yes, the helper is org-named but is the
    shared chokepoint for every endpoint), (7) NEVER expose
    organization_id, parent_id, or self_id in the request body —
    tenant isolation is structural.
  - The factory mints unique slugs per seed
    (`<label>-<random-token>-<n>`), NOT literal labels. Any test that
    needs to provoke a slug collision must capture the actual seeded
    value (e.g. `envPreview.Slug`) and pass IT as the conflict target,
    NOT a literal "preview". The earlier-story
    TestEnvironmentRepoListByProjectReturnsDeterministicOrdering
    fails on this exact mistake — preserved as a Remaining risk
    above. Cross-tenant-isolation tests should compare
    `current.Slug == envB.Slug` (the seeded value) rather than
    asserting a literal.
  - Action-constant naming in policy.actions diverges between the
    `env` family (env.read / env.write — used for project-scoped
    variables) and the `environment` family (environment.read /
    environment.create / environment.update / environment.delete —
    used for environment lifecycle and grants). They are NOT
    interchangeable: the project-variables PATCH endpoint uses
    ActionEnvWrite (env.write), but the environment update endpoint
    here uses ActionEnvironmentUpdate. Future stories adding
    environment-scoped variable PATCH should use `env.write` (resource
    scope pins EnvironmentID); endpoints that mutate the environment
    row itself use `environment.update`.
  - The `fakeEnvironmentUpdater` sweep across 35 test files is
    representative of the cost of adding a new positional argument to
    NewHandler — every existing test pays. Future stories should
    consider a fluent-builder or options-pattern signature for
    NewHandler once 5–6 more deps land. For now, the sweep is fast
    because the call shape is uniform: anchor on the trailing
    `fakeEnvironmentReader{}, nil)` (no-logger) or
    `fakeEnvironmentReader{}, logger)` (real-logger) form and insert
    the new fake before it. The `reader, nil)` / `reader, logger)`
    outliers in the env get/policy test helpers must be handled
    separately because their helper parameter is named `reader` rather
    than a literal struct.
  - decodeError(t, rec, "E_AUTH") — NOT "E_AUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED".
    The apienvelope codepath maps unauthenticated requests to the
    short code E_AUTH; tests that assert the longer code fail with
    the unhelpful diff `error.code = "E_AUTH", want
    "E_AUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED"`. Saved here so the next iteration
    does not waste a build cycle on the same typo.

  - TestUpdateEnvironmentPolicyMatrixRoles: drives owner/admin/developer (allow via ReasonAllowedByRole) and viewer/ci/support (deny via ReasonDeniedNoCapability) through the production NewHandler path. CapWrite split — same as project.update. Allow rows assert updater receives principal home org, path env_id, actor id, decoded display_name; deny rows assert updater never runs and body never leaks canonical row.

  - TestUpdateEnvironmentPolicyGrantContainment: project-/env-/service-scoped grants all denied OutOfScope on this route (envIDResolver pins no ProjectID; covers() is one-way). Org-level Admin grant allowed end-to-end; org-level Viewer denied via ReasonDeniedNoCapability. Cross-tenant grant smuggling denied at engine.
