  - gofmt -l . : clean
  - go vet ./... : clean
  - go test ./... : all passing
  - go test -race ./... : all passing
  - go test -run 'TestUpdateEnvironmentPolicy' -v ./internal/controlplane/httpapi/ : 4 functions, all PASS

- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - The env-id route (environmentIDResolver, no ProjectID on resource) and parent-scoped routes (projectIDResolver, with ProjectID) authorize DIFFERENTLY for scoped grants. All scoped grants pin a ProjectID; covers() is one-way; so scoped grants ALWAYS deny OutOfScope on env-id routes. This is also why support cross-tenant cannot reach env-id routes by construction — and why org-level grants are the only grant flavor that ever authorizes through env-id routes.
  - For CapWrite actions, ALL six roles (including Support) deny cross-tenant — distinct from CapRead where Support is admitted. Pin both engine verdicts in cross-tenant tests so a future catalog change is caught.
  - fakeEnvironmentUpdater fields are env/err/gotInput/callCount (gotInput captures the full store.UpdateEnvironmentInput). Same shape as fakeProjectUpdater but field names differ from fakeEnvironmentReader (which uses gotOrgID/gotEnvID directly).
  - Constants like canonicalPatchDisplayName already declared in projects_update_policy_test.go would collide if reused — use distinct names per file (e.g., canonicalUpdateEnvDisplayName) since policy tests live in the same package.

    `fakeEnvironmentUpdater{}, nil)` -> `fakeEnvironmentUpdater{},
    fakeEnvironmentDeleter{}, nil)` (most sites);
    `fakeEnvironmentUpdater{}, logger)` -> with logger variant;
    `fakeEnvironmentReader{}, updater, nil)` ->
    `fakeEnvironmentReader{}, updater, fakeEnvironmentDeleter{},
    nil)` for environments_update_test.go's named-updater outlier;
    the all-nil newRouteTable form (7 files) received one trailing
    nil; projects_delete_test.go + projects_restore_test.go had
    their existing partial-fakes-with-trailing-nils form extended by
    one more `nil`; the multi-line newRouteTable-with-explicit-fakes
    form (3 files ending `fakeEnvironmentUpdater{})`) became
    `fakeEnvironmentUpdater{}, fakeEnvironmentDeleter{})`.
- Verification run:
  - gofmt -w .                                              -> clean
  - go mod tidy                                             -> clean
  - go vet ./...                                            -> clean
  - go test ./...                                           -> all PASS
  - go test -race ./...                                     -> all PASS
  - go test -run 'TestDeleteEnvironment' ./internal/controlplane/httpapi/ -> PASS
  - go test -run 'TestEnvironment' ./internal/controlplane/store/ -> PASS
- Remaining risks: none from BE-0160 itself. The pre-existing
  TestProjectEnvironmentReplaceServiceReplaceCrossTenantProjectIsNotFound
  + similar suites still skip without YALLA_TEST_DATABASE_URL (the
  Ralph quality-check contract runs go test without a DB) — these
  are existing skips, unchanged by this story.
- Learnings for future iterations:
  - The "deletion stamp must survive across separate transactions"
    assertion needs `s.Read(...)` AFTER the `s.Write(...)` that
    stamped it, not a read inside the SAME write tx — a same-tx read
    sees uncommitted data even when the tx rolls back later, so it
    cannot prove the stamp persisted. project_delete_test.go follows
    the same pattern. Future soft-delete-style tests should re-Read
    on a fresh tx for the "persistence survived commit" assertion.
  - `apierr.Error` is NOT exported as a struct type; the public
    surface is `*yerr.Error` via `yerr.From(err)`. The
    error-is-conflict assertion is `if ye := yerr.From(err);
    ye.Code != yerr.CodeConflict { ... }`, NOT
    `errors.As(err, &apierr.Error)`. Caught and fixed during local
    test compile.
  - When a NewHandler signature grows by one positional port, count
    the trailing nils carefully on EVERY call shape. The Python
    bulk regex handled four patterns (`updater{}, nil)`, `updater{},
    logger)`, `reader{}, updater, nil)`, all-nil newRouteTable) but
    MISSED the "explicit fakes with trailing nils" form
    (projects_delete_test.go ended `fakeProjectGrantReader{},
    nil, nil, nil, nil, nil, nil, nil)` after BE-0148's previous
    sweep) and the "multi-line newRouteTable closing on
    `fakeEnvironmentUpdater{})`" form (env routes test files). Both
    need a follow-up grep on `<resource_X>Updater{})` and a count of
    existing trailing nils. `go vet` will tell you which call sites
    are short by name + line — trust the compiler over the regex.
  - The wire DTO seam (projectEnvironmentOf / projectResourceOf /
    etc.) is the single chokepoint for "should this column appear
    on the wire?". Adding a soft-delete column to the schema must
    be paired with adding `*string DeletionScheduledAt
    \`json:",omitempty"\`` to the wire DTO (omitempty + nil = field
    absent on live rows, so the change is byte-backward-compatible
    for every existing reader). projectResource went through this
    exact change in BE-0130 and projectEnvironment now follows.

  - TestDeleteEnvironmentPolicyGrantContainment: project-/env-/

    engine. Wire tie-ins for project-/env-/service-scoped denies

  - gofmt -l . : clean
  - go mod tidy : clean
  - go vet ./... : clean
  - go test ./... : all passing (httpapi 0.659s)
  - go test -race ./... : all passing (httpapi 3.077s)
  - go test -run 'TestDeleteEnvironmentPolicy' -v ./internal/controlplane/httpapi/ :
    4 functions / 18 subtests, all PASS
- Remaining risks: none from BE-0162 itself. Stale doc-comment in
  environments.go ("CapWrite admits owner, admin, developer, ci")
  noted in BE-0159 still applies — tests verify the actual catalog
  behavior; doc-only fix is a future story.
- Learnings for future iterations:
  - DELETE policy matrix mirrors PATCH almost line-for-line, with
    four wire-shape adjustments: (1) deleter fake instead of updater
    fake, (2) status 202 Accepted instead of 200 OK, (3) no request
    body so the leak guard drops the request-body needle but ADDS
    the deletion_scheduled_at stamp needle (the row's lifecycle
    state is itself information a denied principal must not learn),
    (4) DeleteEnvironmentInput carries ActorOrgID where
    UpdateEnvironmentInput at the time of writing did not — assert
    ActorOrgID on the deleter capture so the audit record names the
    actor's tenant verbatim.
  - The deletion_scheduled_at leak needle has to use the same
    timestamp constant the canonical fixture uses (defined inline in
    deleteEnvDenyBodyLeak). Putting it in a package-level var would
    risk breakage if the fixture timestamp ever shifts, but
    duplicating the time.Date(...) call in the leak guard keeps the
    coupling explicit and local to this file.
  - canonicalDeleteEnvForMatrix uses distinct ids ("env_matrix_delete",
    "prj_delete_matrix_parent", "delete-matrix", "Delete Matrix v3")
    from every other canonical env fixture in the package — five
    fixtures now coexist (get / get-matrix / updated / update-matrix
    / delete-matrix), so the naming convention is becoming
    load-bearing for ensuring future shared-fake regressions surface
    deterministically. The env_matrix_delete id appears in the leak
    guard needles and in the wire-tie-in fakes' env field; if a
    future env-matrix fixture reuses any of these tokens, the leak
    guard becomes a false negative.
  - The DELETE policy matrix needs the SAME engine-level cross-
    tenant proof that PATCH does (CapWrite outside support
    exception), but for completeness BOTH policy matrices must pin
    it independently — a future catalog change that downgraded ONE
    of them into the support exception (without the other) would
    silently regress half the contract. Subtests are run as
    "engine_cross_tenant_deny_<role>" for greppable failure attribution.
  - Wire tie-ins for scoped grants need three independent fake
    deleters (project / env / service captures) because each call
    site asserts `captured.OrganizationID == ""` — sharing the
    capture across all three would let a regression in one tie-in
    pollute the other tie-ins' captures and mask itself.

## 2026-05-15 - BE-0163
- Implemented POST /v1/environments/{environment_id}/clone — the
  control-plane endpoint that clones an environment into a new sibling
  in the same project. Action environment.create gates the route through
  environmentIDResolver (a CapWrite action authorized against the
  (principal home org, source env_id) resource), the request body
  carries only environment_id/slug/display_name for the NEW environment,
  and the new row inherits its project_id from the source — the caller
  cannot reparent through this endpoint.

- Remaining risks:
  - The clone path does NOT yet copy environment-scoped variables or
    services across — the wire description and the PRD note flag this

    propagation is owned by the worker.

    cloner AND the existing creator/updater/deleter. This is the
    documented production pattern (single concrete *EnvironmentService
    satisfies all four narrow ports), but it does mean a misconfigured
    EnvironmentService at startup fails fast for all four routes
    together — which is the intended behavior per the doc-comment in
    server.go.
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - **POST /v1/.../{id}/<verb> on a deep resource** (BE-0163 pattern,
    POST /v1/environments/{environment_id}/clone): canonical shape
    for ALL "sub-action" POSTs on a bare-id route — restart, rollback,
    cancel, clone, restore, etc. The path carries only the source id
    and a verb suffix; the resolver pins (OrganizationID, ID) only
    (parent project_id is unknown to the resolver); scoped grants
    that pin ProjectID are denied by covers() (one-way containment).
    For these sub-action POSTs the parent_id (project_id for env) is
    DERIVED FROM THE SOURCE ROW inside the same tx, NEVER from the
    body or path — preserving the structural tenant boundary even on
    the new row. The service-layer orchestrator composes Create-style
    steps (in-tx Authorize / Quota / Insert / JobEnqueue / Audit) PLUS
    a source-row read at the front PLUS a lifecycle-state guard
    (e.g., reject DeletionScheduledAt != nil as Conflict — a
    lifecycle-dead row is not a valid source for a Create-style
    sub-action). The audit row's Metadata records the structural
    provenance (e.g., cloned_from=<source.ID>) — a non-secret
    identifier safe to record verbatim, and the trail's only handle on
    "where did this row come from".
  - **The body of a sub-action POST omits the parent_id field by
    design**: any sub-action that DERIVES a structural relationship
    from the source row (clone inheriting project_id, branch inheriting
    org, etc.) must NOT accept that field in the request body — the
    strict decoder rejects an unknown-field body as 400 (proven by
    TestCloneEnvironmentRejectsUnknownField pinning project_id). This
    is structural defense: even a caller who tries to redirect the
    new row at a sibling project cannot succeed because the decoder
    refuses the field before it reaches the orchestrator.
  - **environment.create on a sub-action route reuses the existing
    action constant** rather than minting a new environment.clone
    action. The PRD specified action environment.create explicitly,
    and from the policy engine's perspective a clone IS a create
    (CapWrite, defended by the same role matrix). Adding a separate
    action constant would have required updating the action catalog,
    builtinRoleCaps, every policy matrix test, and the OpenAPI surface
    — yet bought no contract benefit because the authorization
    semantics are identical. Reuse the constant unless the new action
    needs a DIFFERENT required capability or a DIFFERENT role matrix.
  - **The testutil factory's IDs are deliberately non-canonical** and
    the strict ParseID validation correctly rejects them at the
    service-layer boundary. Tests that go through Service.Create-style
    paths (Create / Clone / Restore / Restart, anything that calls a
    validate*Input that uses domain.ParseID) MUST seed with
    seedDomainOrg / seedDomainProject / seedDomainEnvironment helpers
    that mint canonical 26-char-suffix IDs via domain.MustNewID — NOT
    the testutil.Factory's seedOrg / seedProject / seedEnvironment
    helpers, which produce 20-char-suffix IDs the validator rejects.
    This is the same pattern projectservice_test.go's seedDomainOrg
    follows. Repository-level tests (which bypass validation) can use
    either helper; service-level tests MUST use the canonical helpers.
  - **The newRouteTable positional-arg sweep needs three patterns**,
    not just one: (1) "fakeEnvironmentDeleter{}, nil)" → add the new
    fake before nil for NewHandler calls; (2) "fakeEnvironmentDeleter{})"
    → add the new fake at the end for newRouteTable calls; (3)
    "newRouteTable(<N nils>)" → bump to N+1 nils for the OpenAPI
    all-nils shape tests. Forgetting (3) leaves OpenAPI shape tests
    in routes_test.go / limits_patch_test.go / server_test.go /
    variables_*_test.go / projects_*_test.go failing with "not enough
    arguments to newRouteTable" — those tests pass an all-nil tuple
    rather than the named fake* values, so the literal-string sweep
    misses them. Run go vet after each automated sweep; the error
    message names every site that still has the wrong arity.

## 2026-05-15 - BE-0165
- What was implemented: policy-matrix coverage for POST
  /v1/environments/{environment_id}/clone — the authorization
  contract of the endpoint BE-0163 wires, parallel to BE-0162 for
  DELETE /v1/environments/{environment_id}.
  - internal/controlplane/httpapi/environments_clone_policy_test.go
    (new, ~670 lines): one canonical fixture
    (canonicalCloneEnvForMatrix / cloneEnvSourcePathID /
    canonicalCloneRequestBody) + a single leak guard
    (cloneEnvDenyBodyLeak) used by every deny branch, then four
    tests that drive the REAL NewHandler + real policy.NewEngine()
    against fake Authenticator + fakeEnvironmentCloner (the
    production request path minus the database):
    - TestCloneEnvironmentPolicyMatrixRoles tables all six built-in
      roles against environment.create at a same-tenant env-id
      resource (no ProjectID leg, because the bare clone route
      pins none). CapWrite splits the matrix: Owner / Admin /
      Developer allow via ReasonAllowedByRole (201 + cloner reached
      with home_org + path source_env_id + decoded body's new id /
      slug / display_name + actor id + actor_org_id; allow path
      response has no deletion_scheduled_at and the row's version
      is mirrored to the ETag header); Viewer / CI / Support deny
      via ReasonDeniedNoCapability (403 + cloner never reached +
      body never leaks the new clone, source env id, inherited
      project, or caller-supplied body fields). CI denies despite
      holding CapDeploy — CapDeploy is service lifecycle, not
      desired-state mutation.
    - TestCloneEnvironmentPolicyRevokedAndExpiredKeys proves a
      Disabled Owner principal (revoked OR expired credential) is
      denied via ReasonDeniedPrincipalDisabled, the cloner never
      runs, and the body never leaks the principal id, the
      organization id, the canonical clone, or the caller-supplied
      body fields.
    - TestCloneEnvironmentPolicyWrongOrganizationPrincipal: wire-
      level cross-tenant source env_id surfaces as 404 from the
      persistence boundary (environmentIDResolver pins resource
      scope to principal home org, so the engine admits the
      same-tenant resource and the cloner IS reached once with
      (ownOrg, foreignSourceEnvID), whereupon the
      production EnvironmentService's tenant-scoped source read
      returns NotFound). Engine-level pin tables every role
      INCLUDING Support — all denied via ReasonDeniedCrossTenant
      because CapWrite is OUTSIDE the support exception clause
      (CapSupport && (CapRead || CapSupport)). Load-bearing
      distinction from environment.read which DOES admit Support
      cross-tenant.
    - TestCloneEnvironmentPolicyGrantContainment: project-, env-,
      and service-scoped grants are all denied OutOfScope on this
      route, even when the grant scope names the source
      environment's own project or the source environment's own
      id — environmentIDResolver pins no ProjectID and covers()
      is one-way (a grant that pins ProjectID cannot cover a
      resource scope that does not). Engine-level twins pin: a
      project-scoped admin grant DOES allow environment.create on
      a project resource (the parent-scoped POST
      /v1/projects/{project_id}/environments route) but DOES NOT
      cover this env-id route; sibling project denied; staging-env
      grant does not imply production env.write; service-scoped
      grant does not expose parent-level env.write or sibling
      services. Org-level Admin grant allowed end-to-end via
      ReasonAllowedByGrant (201 + cloner reached with all required
      fields, ETag header mirrored). Org-level Viewer grant denied
      via ReasonDeniedNoCapability — load-bearing distinction from
      environment.read grant matrix where Viewer is allowed.
      Cross-tenant grant smuggling (sa_proj_admin planted in
      org_sibling with a grant scoped to org_acme) denied at the
      engine — a scoped key's home org must match the grant
      scope's org or the engine refuses to consider the grant.
  - ralph/prd.json (BE-0165 passes -> true).
- Files changed:
  - internal/controlplane/httpapi/environments_clone_policy_test.go (new)
  - ralph/prd.json (BE-0165 passes -> true)

      ./internal/controlplane/httpapi/                        : PASS (4 tests + table subtests)

- Results: all green. No regressions to any pre-existing matrix.
  The new file shares fakeEnvironmentCloner with the contract
  suite environments_clone_test.go (BE-0163); no scaffolding was
  added beyond the per-file canonical fixture builders.
- Remaining risks / follow-ups:
  - BE-0166 (the natural neighbour) implements
    POST /v1/environments/{environment_id}/restore — the bare-id
    env restore route. BE-0167 will be its policy matrix and
    will reuse THIS file's structural template byte-for-byte: the
    bare-id env resolver pins no ProjectID, environment.create
    is CapWrite, leak guard adds body needles. The only
    distinction is that restore is "lifecycle resurrection"
    (Conflict if NOT scheduled for deletion) rather than "fresh
    write" — the engine verdict is structurally identical.
  - The contract test docstring for cloneEnvironmentHandler in
    internal/controlplane/httpapi/environments.go says "the gate
    admits the principal's organization-wide write roles (owner,
    admin, developer, ci) and denies viewer, denies support" —
    this is inaccurate. CI holds CapDeploy/CapRead/CapSelf but
    NOT CapWrite (verified in catalog.go builtinRoleCaps), so CI
    is DENIED for environment.create — the matrix test confirms
    this. The handler implementation itself is correct (delegates
    to the engine); only the docstring is misleading. A
    separate doc-correction story could fix this but it is not
    in scope for BE-0165.
- Learnings for future iterations:
  - POST-verb bare-id route policy matrix: the canonical shape
    (BE-0162 for DELETE) extends cleanly to POST verbs with a
    body (BE-0165 for clone). Two additions over the DELETE
    template:
    (1) The leak guard MUST include needles for the
        caller-supplied request body fields — for clone, the new
        env_id, the new slug (quoted), and the new display_name
        (quoted). Even though the policy gate runs BEFORE body
        decode (RequireAuth middleware authorizes via
        environmentIDResolver before the handler is reached, so a
        denied principal never has their body decoded), the leak
        guard still anchors on the body fields because the new
        slug/display_name happen to equal the canonical clone
        env's slug/display_name — so a regression that rendered
        the cloner's return value on a deny path would fire the
        leak guard. Setting body needles distinct from the
        canonical-row needles is a future hardening.
    (2) The PATH-supplied source env id is distinct from the
        BODY-supplied new env id (cloneEnvSourcePathID =
        "env_matrix_clone_source" vs canonical.ID =
        "env_matrix_clone"), so the leak guard catches "renderer
        echoed the path parameter" and "renderer echoed the body
        field" as independent regressions.
  - Wrong-organization cross-tenant for clone: the wire-level
    test asserts the cloner IS called once with (ownOrg,
    foreignSourceEnvID) — distinct from "the cloner must never
    run" deny rows. The PRODUCTION cloner has its own
    persistence-layer NotFound (the source read is tenant-scoped),
    so the wire test asserts the structural property that the
    cloner ALWAYS receives the principal's home org id — never
    the caller-controlled value — so a production
    EnvironmentService could not have read the victim's row.
    Pinning callCount == 1 here (not 0) is the load-bearing
    contract: a regression that built the store call from a
    caller-controlled org id would silently pass a 0 callCount
    assertion.
  - environment.create's allow path returns 201 Created (not 200
    OK or 202 Accepted). The contract test (BE-0163) verifies
    this through the route table's SuccessStatus; the policy
    matrix verifies it through the wire response. The
    deletion_scheduled_at field is nil on the allow path
    response — distinct from the DELETE allow path where the
    field MUST carry the row's lifecycle stamp.
  - Reusing canonicalCloneRequestBody as a const (rather than a
    builder) means every test sends a byte-identical body, which
    proves the deny path is policy-driven (never validation-
    driven): a body that decoded cleanly under Owner would also
    decode cleanly under any other role, so a 403 must come from
    the engine's verdict, not from a body-shape regression.

- Remaining risks / follow-ups:
  - This is the pure orchestrator only. The concrete Dokploy-backed Scanner
    (list-projects / list-environments / list-services on the Dokploy
    client + dokployfake list routes) and the store-backed Repository
    (CreateProject/Environment/Service with a Dokploy-link column) land in
    separate stories. Dokploy.Client.go currently exposes Get + Post +
    Delete; List operations will need to land before the
    Dokploy-backed Scanner adapter is implementable, but the Scanner port
    is contract-stable, so adapter work proceeds in parallel.
  - Service-level persistence has no schema yet (no services table). The
    Repository port already exposes CreateService / FindServiceByDokployID
    / FindServiceBySlug so the store adapter can land in one go when the
    schema migration ships — no churn here.
  - BE-0289 / BE-0290 / BE-0291 (POST /v1/admin/dokploy/import + contract
    tests + policy matrix) are the customer-facing wrapper for this
    workflow; the wire shape of Plan is the dry-run response and the
    OwnerAssignment is the request input. No further surface changes are
    expected before that story.
  - The planner sorts by Dokploy resource ID at each hierarchy depth, but
    emits items in hierarchy order
    (organization → project → environment → service). Apply iterates the
    plan in its emitted order so child-after-parent is structurally
    guaranteed. If a future story needs cross-hierarchy interleaving
    (e.g. detect a domain at the service level whose parent is in the
    SAME plan), the Apply loop's resolvedParents map already supports it.
  - The classifier asks the Repository up to four queries per item
    (FindByDokployID, FindBySlug for each level); a future "scan-once"
    optimisation could batch these by parent, but the per-item ports are
    the simplest contract and tests assert ordering.
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - When a story names a pure workflow (Importer / Reconciler / Renderer)
    the reconcile package is the canonical template — see
    internal/controlplane/reconcile/reconcile.go for the pattern: Config
    with port interfaces, New() rejects nil ports with apierr.Internal,
    Logger defaults to slog.Default, Now defaults to time.Now().UTC,
    Redactor defaults to output.NewRedactor(). Plan-vs-Apply split lets
    "dry run" be just calling Plan without Apply, and the Plan JSON shape
    is the eventual endpoint's yalla.output.v1 payload — so PlanItem must
    have stable named fields, no pointers, no embedded interfaces.
  - apierr.NotFound is the catalogued NotFound; check via stderrors.As to
    *yerr.Error then ye.Code == yerr.CodeNotFound. apierr.DokployUnavailable
    maps to yerr.CodeServer (E_SERVER), NOT yerr.CodeUnavailable
    (E_UNAVAILABLE — that's StoreUnavailable / JobQueueUnavailable for
    Yalla-owned dependencies). apierr.ViolationsOf(err) recovers the field
    violations from an InvalidInput error — the err.Error() message itself
    is the generic "request validation failed" without the field name.
  - Canonical Yalla ID test fixtures: kind prefix + "_" + 26-char Crockford
    base32 lowercase suffix. The alphabet is
    "0123456789abcdefghjkmnpqrstvwxyz" (no i, l, o, u). The testutil
    factory's IDs are deliberately non-canonical for some tests; for any
    test that runs a real ParseID / Kind check, mint a canonical fixture
    by hand: "org_01hz00000000000000000000xx" (4-char prefix + 20 zeros +
    2-char tag = 26).
  - dokploy.Client currently exposes Get + Post + Delete intents only
    (EnsureOrganization, EnsureProject, EnsureEnvironment, EnsureService,
    EnsureDomain, DeployService, ReadDeploymentLogs, GetServiceStatus,
    RemoveService). A Snapshot-shaped reader (list-projects-under-org,
    list-environments-under-project, list-services-under-env) is the
    missing piece for the migrateimport.Scanner adapter and for BE-0283
    (GET /v1/admin/dokploy/drift). Add the List* methods + dokployfake
    list routes when the first consumer of either lands.
  - Slug derivation: never reuse domain.DokployName (Yalla → Dokploy) for
    Dokploy → Yalla. Use domain.NormalizeSlug(name) on the Dokploy
    resource name. A name that NormalizeSlug rejects (no usable alnum
    content) is itself a classification — StatusSkipDuplicate with reason
    ReasonDuplicateName — not an error to propagate.
  - Dokploy.ServiceType.Valid() is "application | compose | database".
    Database services additionally require a non-blank engine, so
    supportedServiceType(svc) AND-s the two checks. The importer
    classifies an unsupported type or a database-missing-engine as
    StatusSkipUnsupported / ReasonUnsupportedServiceType — both surfaces
    are intentionally collapsed into one reason code because the
    operator's remediation is the same: fix the Dokploy resource first.
  - Hierarchy order in Apply matters: the resolvedParents map seeds the
    root-org entry at construction so projects can resolve. Each
    successful CreateProject populates the map under the Dokploy project
    ID so child environments resolve, and so on. A failed parent leaves
    its slot empty — the child item's Status was already classified as
    StatusReady, so Apply emits an Internal "no resolved parent" failure
    for it (not a planner bug — Apply-side guard for an upstream-failed
    parent in a best-effort loop). The classifier could pre-detect this
    by treating a parent's failure as a missing-parent, but the
    pure-planner contract is "Repository state at Plan time"; runtime
    Apply ordering is owned by Apply.
- **Codebase Pattern (reusable):**
  - **Pure import / orchestrator package = reconcile-shaped vertical**
    (BE-0033 pattern, internal/controlplane/migrateimport/...): canonical
    shape for ANY pure workflow that consumes external state through
    ports and writes through ports. Structure: doc.go (package doc with
    boundary + plan/apply + dry-run + redaction sections), AGENTS.md
    (conventions), types.go (every port interface + every value type used
    in those interfaces + the planner's output Plan/PlanItem with stable
    JSON tags), importer.go (Config with port + Logger + Now + Redactor;
    New() returns apierr.Internal on missing ports; Plan(ctx, in) is pure
    and never writes; Apply(ctx, plan) is best-effort and collects per-
    item failures; classify*() functions are unit-testable in isolation;
    wrap*Err helpers preserve catalogued apierr codes and upgrade
    untyped errors to apierr.DokployUnavailable / apierr.StoreUnavailable
    /apierr.Internal as appropriate; logFailure() emits structured slog
    diagnostics with scrubbed error strings). Test file (importer_test.go
    or {workflow}_test.go) houses an in-package fake Scanner + fake
    Repository with concurrent-safe mutexes and call recording, and
    covers: construction port validation (one nil per case); input
    validation (every required field and every kind/format check); the
    dry-run-doesn't-query-Repository contract; every classification
    Status × Reason combination as a positive case; one tenant-isolation
    / cross-binding contract; Scanner failure surfaces as the right
    apierr code; Repository failure surfaces as the right apierr code;
    secrets redacted in error strings AND in log buffer (slog over a
    bytes.Buffer); Apply persists in hierarchy order; Apply continues
    past per-item failures; Apply ctx-cancellation propagates; Apply on
    no-ready-items is a valid no-op accounting skipped count. The Plan
    JSON shape is what the eventual customer-facing endpoint serialises
    into yalla.output.v1, so stable field names and no embedded
    interfaces are PUBLIC compatibility contract before the endpoint
    even exists. Reconcile (drift detection) and migrateimport (Dokploy
    import) are siblings under this pattern; future "resource lifecycle
    worker", "compliance scanner", "billing reconciler" packages should
    reuse it verbatim.

- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - The structural-twin pattern between project_grants and
    environment_grants pays off: every layer (migration, store struct,
    repository, reader, HTTP port, payload projection, handler, route
    entry, OpenAPI description, test fakes, integration tests, contract
    tests) maps 1:1, so the diff stays small and reviewable. The only
    real divergences are (a) no EnvironmentID/ProjectID pair in the
    grants row (just OrganizationID + EnvironmentID), and (b) the
    ordering tuple drops the (environment_id, service_id) leg down to
    just (service_id) because EnvironmentID is now a singleton in the
    scope.
  - When the route path carries no parent project_id (top-level
    /v1/environments/{environment_id}/...), the resolver cannot pin
    the ProjectID leg of the resource scope, so the engine's covers()
    rule denies project-/environment-/service-scoped grants at the
    boundary by design. Document this explicitly in the route comment
    so a future story doesn't relax the boundary thinking the engine
    will catch the difference.
  - When extending NewHandler/newRouteTable signatures, the bulk edit
    across *_test.go callers is mechanical: a Node walker that tracks
    paren depth across multi-line calls and rewrites the closing line
    is faster and safer than 50+ Edit invocations, and it leaves the
    AGENTS.md "add the new fake" workflow intact.
  - The Postgres integration suite has pre-existing factory-name
    collisions in environments_test.go / apikeyservice_test.go that
    fail when YALLA_TEST_DATABASE_URL is set. They reproduce on the
    parent commit, so they are not regressions from this story. Future
    work should land a fix in the factory or the assertion side and
    keep it scoped to its own story.

  - Policy-matrix-on-environmentIDResolver-grants pattern (BE-0168 pattern,
    internal/controlplane/httpapi/environment_grants_policy_test.go): a
    customer-facing grants list whose route uses environmentIDResolver
    (the env-id resolver that pins NO ProjectID on the resource scope)
    is structurally identical at the policy boundary to
    environments_get_policy_test.go (BE-0156): same KindEnvironment
    resource on the route, same "covers() is one-way" property that
    denies every project-, environment-, AND service-scoped grant by
    ReasonDeniedOutOfScope (the grant scope pins ProjectID and the
    resource scope does not). The grants-list aspect adds the
    projects_grants_policy_test.go (BE-0138) deny-leak guard pattern:
    a denied response must never echo the canonical grant ids,
    principal ids, service id, environment id, OR the synthetic parent
    project id (even though no wire input could place the parent
    project id on the response — the leak guard catches an accidental
    renderer regression that projected it through). The four-test
    skeleton is fixed: roles matrix (all six built-in roles allow via
    ReasonAllowedByRole; spot-check both nullable-ServiceID variants on
    the wire projection), revoked/expired keys (Disabled principal
    denied 403 even when Owner; reader never runs; body redacted),
    wrong-organization principal (wire-level NotFound through the
    persistence layer at (own_org, foreign_env_id); engine-level
    cross-tenant deny pinned for every non-support role + support
    cross-tenant allow under the CapRead clause), grant containment
    (project / env-same-id / service scoped grants all denied at engine
    + 403 at wire with reader never reached + body leak-guarded; org-
    level Viewer allowed end-to-end; stolen scoped key planted in a
    foreign home org denied at the engine cross-tenant boundary).

    maps to CapRead, same class as environment.read /
    project.grants.read / project.read / limits.read / usage.read).
  - Reader-call fixture pattern for environment grants matches the
    BE-0166 fakeEnvironmentGrantReader (fields: grants, err, gotOrgID,
    gotEnvID, callCount); the test helper listEnvironmentGrantsHandlerFor
    (auth.Identity, authErr, EnvironmentGrantReader) and request helper
    getEnvironmentGrants(handler, environmentID, token) are shared with
    environment_grants_test.go — no new scaffolding is needed.
  - The wire body has no environment_id in the request (the path
    parameter is the only input), so there is no body-input leak guard
    to write (unlike project_grants_put_policy_test.go's "body echoes
    the caller-supplied org_id" property). The needle list is purely
    seeded grant + environment + parent-project identifiers.
  - Engine-level wrong-tenant assertion uses a subtest-per-role pattern
    inside the wire-level wrong-organization test (a single t.Run
    block per non-support role, all asserting ReasonDeniedCrossTenant;
    Support then asserted at the outer scope for ReasonAllowedBySupport).
    This shape avoids a separate test function while still making each
    cross-tenant role failure individually addressable from the test
    output.

- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - PUT-replace-grants store-service pattern (BE-0169 store pattern,
    internal/controlplane/store/environment_grant.go +
    environment_grant_service_test.go): a customer-facing
    replace-grants endpoint whose route uses an *IDResolver pinning the
    parent resource is structurally identical to ProjectGrantService at
    the persistence boundary, with one structural simplification:
    because the parent is a route path parameter (not a body field),
    the ReplaceInput drops the parent-id leg from the per-grant Replace
    struct (here EnvironmentGrantReplace has only ServiceID; project
    grants carry both EnvironmentID and ServiceID). The audit metadata
    therefore tallies two scope counts (environment / service) instead
    of three (project / environment / service), and the unique index
    deduplicates on (organization_id, parent_id, principal_id,
    COALESCE(child_id, '')) — one fewer COALESCE leg than project
    grants. Everything else (existence check → per-grant Upsert with
    RETURNING → bulk DeleteByParentExceptIDs → audit Append →
    post-write re-read, all in one Store.Write) is byte-identical to
    project_grant.go and can be lifted verbatim. The closed-set
    principal-kind / built-in-role maps, the FieldViolation collector
    that sorts for deterministic wire bytes, and the
    normalise/safe scope-id helpers are also drop-in copies.
  - PUT-replace-grants handler pattern (BE-0169 handler pattern,
    internal/controlplane/httpapi/environment_grants.go +
    environment_grants_put_test.go): the handler is a thin
    strict-decode → validate body shape → forward-to-store →
    re-project pipeline. The grants field is a pointer-to-slice so a
    body that omits the field is a stable 400 (errors with the
    must-be-supplied reason) and a body with an explicit empty array
    reaches the store as a deliberate clear — the structural
    distinction is load-bearing because PUT replaces the entire set.
    cloneOptionalString protects the store from observing caller
    string memory. Field-level validation (principal_kind, role,
    duplicate scope tuple) is never re-done in the handler — it lives
    in the store layer and the handler propagates apierr.InvalidInput
    verbatim. fakeEnvironmentGrantReplacer mirrors
    fakeProjectGrantReplacer (grants / err / got / callCount fields).
  - Bulk NewHandler-signature edit pattern (BE-0169 bulk-edit pattern):
    adding a new ReplacerPort to NewHandler ripples across ~46 test
    files. A Node script that replaces the literal pattern
    'fakeEnvironmentGrantReader{}, nil)' with
    'fakeEnvironmentGrantReader{}, fakeEnvironmentGrantReplacer{}, nil)'
    catches every routine NewHandler call site in one pass. The
    remaining cases (NewHandler with reader-aliased to 'reader' and
    NewHandler followed by ', logger)' and single-line newRouteTable
    calls with N trailing nil args) need their own targeted
    replacements but every variant has at most a handful of call
    sites. The pre-existing newRouteTable test helpers (projects_*,
    variables_*, server_test.go) pass nil for unused dependencies, so
    those need an extra trailing nil — never an extra
    fakeEnvironmentGrantReplacer{} — to match the new arity.
  - Confirm pre-existing failures by git-stashing and re-running: a
    failing test on this branch is only "yours" if it doesn't already
    fail on the parent. The BE-0166 progress entry already documented
    a set of factory-state failures (TestEnvironmentServiceCreate*,
    TestEnvironmentReaderRejectsCrossTenantProjectID,
    TestAPIKeyServiceCreate*, TestOrganizationVariableServicePatch*,
    TestEnvironmentRepoListByProjectReturnsDeterministicOrdering,
    TestEnvironmentRepoGetByIDReturnsRow) and they reproduce
    identically on the parent commit of this story. Stash + rerun is
    the cheapest sanity check before chasing a tail-of-the-suite red.

  - The "policy matrix for PUT {grants}" story is the structural sibling of the projects_grants_put_policy_test.go pattern (BE-0141) with ONE narrowing: the resolver pins NO ProjectID leg, so every scoped grant — including a grant on the SAME env_id named in the path — is denied OutOfScope at the engine AND at the wire. Always include the support row in the engine_cross_tenant_deny_* parallel subtests for CapAdmin write actions; that single row is the only difference between the read-cross-tenant matrix and the write-cross-tenant matrix.
  - canonicalEnvGrantsEnvironmentID / canonicalEnvGrantsProjectID / canonicalEnvironmentGrants / envGrantsDenyBodyLeak / seedEnvironmentGrantWire (from environment_grants_policy_test.go and environment_grants_test.go) are package-level helpers and can be reused verbatim — do NOT redeclare them in the put_policy file. Same for replaceEnvironmentGrantsHandlerFor / putEnvironmentGrants / decodeReplaceEnvironmentGrants / fakeEnvironmentGrantReplacer (from environment_grants_put_test.go) and orgPrincipal / decodeError (the wider httpapi test fixtures). The put_policy file's net new fixtures are only the two body-leak helpers; everything else is shared.
  - ReplaceEnvironmentGrantsInput field name is EnvironmentID (not ProjectID — that's the project-grants twin) and ActorOrgID (not ActorOrgID could easily get typed as ActorOrganizationID — copy from environment_grants_put_test.go's existing assertions to avoid drift). The captured input ALWAYS carries the PRINCIPAL'S home org as both OrganizationID and ActorOrgID — never a caller-controlled value, never the path tenant.

  - Reader-only scoped-child vertical on a bare-id resolver (BE-0172, environment-variables): structural sibling of BE-0142 (project_variables) with TWO narrowings worth pinning. (1) The new resource (env-variables) inherits the same migration shape (composite FK to parent, scope-uniqueness index on (org, env, key), composite UNIQUE(org,id) as future-override FK target, version+bump_version+set_updated_at triggers); only the column names change (environment_id replaces project_id, no transitive project_id duplicated — environment_grants is the precedent). (2) The HTTP route uses environmentIDResolver (bare-id, no ProjectID leg) rather than projectIDResolver, so every scoped grant — including a grant on the SAME env_id named in the path — is denied OutOfScope by the engine's one-way covers() rule. The wire chokepoint (environmentVariable struct) still redacts secret values to output.Sentinel exactly as project_variables does; there is no wire-shape difference between the two resources because the agent's job is to enumerate environment-default variables, not to confirm a service's effective value (that's the rendered-service-variables endpoint's job, a separate future story).
  - migrations/0018_environment_variables.up.sql is the FIRST environment-scoped child table that uses a composite-FK to environments (organization_id, environment_id) — environments themselves carry organization_id, project_id, id, so the FK only needs (organization_id, environment_id), NOT a transitive project_id. This mirrors environment_grants (0017's predecessor). The benefit: a scope-narrowing service_variables override table only needs (organization_id, environment_id, key) joined to (organization_id, environment_id, key) on env_variables — the FK to env_variables uses (organization_id, id) as the composite target (already declared on this table), so the override row's organization_id structurally matches its parent's. Future service_variables migration is one composite-FK away.
  - NewHandler positional-port arity sweep for env-variables (BE-0172): the port lands at the tail of the env ports group, AFTER environmentGrantReplacer and BEFORE logger. The bulk regex anchors on `fakeEnvironmentGrantReplacer{}, nil)` (NewHandler with nil logger in unit tests) -> `fakeEnvironmentGrantReplacer{}, fakeEnvironmentVariableReader{}, nil)`, plus the `, logger)` variant (server_test.go, me_contract_test.go) -> `fakeEnvironmentGrantReplacer{}, fakeEnvironmentVariableReader{}, logger)`, plus the openapi-shape newRouteTable form `fakeEnvironmentGrantReplacer{})` -> `fakeEnvironmentGrantReplacer{}, fakeEnvironmentVariableReader{})`, plus one MORE trailing nil for the all-nil newRouteTable form. Run go vet AFTER each automated sweep — Go's positional-arg compile error tells you which call sites the regex missed.
  - EnvironmentVariable.LogValue (slog.LogValuer) redacts Value unconditionally at the slog boundary, not just for IsSecret=true rows. Reason: a stray panic stack or debug-log that captures the struct cannot leak a non-secret value either; the wire layer's is_secret-gated redaction is the customer-facing contract, the slog redaction is defence-in-depth. Mirror this on every future variable resource (service_variables, etc).
  - The EnvironmentVariableReader adapter's two-step (Get env + List variables) inside one Store.Read transaction is load-bearing for the agent-friendly contract: a cross-tenant or unknown environment_id surfaces as apierr.NotFound, NEVER as an empty success — the empty-success failure mode would invite an agent to believe the environment exists with no variables (a structural lie). Repository.ListByEnvironment alone is NOT enough; always compose the parent-existence Get in the same tx.

BE-0175 (PUT /v1/environments/{environment_id}/variables endpoint) is the structural follow-up — the new endpoint will need its own contract suite, a fakeEnvironmentVariableReplacer in NewHandler, and BE-0177 the policy matrix that mirrors BE-0145 (project_variables PUT) with the same env-id-resolver-no-ProjectID narrowing this story applied.

- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - Variables-flavoured policy matrix on a bare-{id}-resolver route (BE-0174, environment-variables GET): structural hybrid of (a) environment_grants_policy_test.go (BE-0168) — the env-id resolver pins NO ProjectID leg, so every scoped grant including a grant on the SAME env_id is denied OutOfScope at the engine AND the wire via the one-way covers() rule — and (b) projects_variables_get_policy_test.go (BE-0144) — the resource carries credential material in secret values, so the deny-path leak guard MUST include the secret plaintext (canonicalEnvVarsSecretPlaintext + 'hunter2' substring) in addition to the structural ids, AND the role matrix MUST positively assert the secret row's wire Value is output.Sentinel on every allow path (not just verify the absence of plaintext — both directions catch different regressions). Copy BE-0168's skeleton, swap action -> ActionEnvRead, add the variables-flavoured leak needles + Sentinel assertions from BE-0144.
  - Cross-tenant engine matrix DIRECTION rule (CapRead actions): env.read is CapRead, so the engine cross-tenant clause ADMITS Support via ReasonAllowedBySupport AND DENIES every non-support role via ReasonDeniedCrossTenant. The cross-tenant assertion block must therefore (1) iterate owner/admin/developer/viewer/ci through engine_cross_tenant_deny_<role> subtests and (2) add a SEPARATE positive assertion that Support is allowed via ReasonAllowedBySupport. Forgetting (2) would silently let a future catalog change upgrade env.read to a non-CapRead capability (which would deny every support cross-tenant read) without failing here. Mirror-test for CapAdmin write actions inverts this: Support is DENIED cross-tenant via ReasonDeniedCrossTenant, and the support row joins the deny matrix (the load-bearing distinction the BE-0171 env-grants-PUT entry pinned).
  - Wire-redaction chokepoint POSITIVE assertion on EVERY allow path (BE-0174 vs BE-0168): for resources that carry credential material (variables, API keys, secrets) the role-matrix happy path MUST positively assert got0.Value == output.Sentinel for the secret row AND negatively assert the body does not contain the seeded plaintext. The positive assertion catches a regression where the renderer projects an unexpected non-empty string that isn't the seeded plaintext (e.g. partial truncation); the negative catches a regression that projects the plaintext verbatim. Both directions are needed — environment-grants only needs structural-id leak guards because grant rows carry no credential material, but every variables / secret resource needs both layers. Additionally pin the same Sentinel assertion on the org-level-Viewer GRANT allow path inside TestGrantContainment so an authorization path that bypassed the role matrix cannot bypass the redaction chokepoint either.
  - Cross-tenant deny status code rationale (BE-0174 wire-level): the env-id resolver pins the resource to the principal HOME org id (not the path tenant), so a cross-tenant attacker is admitted same-tenant at the engine and rejected at the persistence layer with apierr.NotFound("environment", id). Status MUST be 404 E_NOT_FOUND, NEVER 403 (which would confirm the environment existence in another tenant) and NEVER 200 with an empty list (which would invite the agent to believe the environment exists with no variables). The fakeEnvironmentVariableReader.err = apierr.NotFound(...) pattern mirrors the production store contract: the (org, env_id) tuple-miss surfaces as NotFound regardless of the caller role. This invariant is shared with environment-grants and is the cornerstone of cross-tenant defence on every bare-{environment_id}-resolver route.

BE-0176 (explicit contract-tests story for the same endpoint, P=2) is already satisfied by the test surface this story shipped — the same wire envelope, request_id propagation, error envelope, OpenAPI registration assertions are all in place. BE-0177 (policy matrix, P=1) is the immediate next story — its skeleton is a structural hybrid of (a) projects_variables_put_policy_test.go (BE-0147) for the CapWrite role x grant-scope matrix and (b) environment_grants_put_policy_test.go (BE-0171) for the env-id-resolver narrowing (no ProjectID leg → every scoped grant denied OutOfScope via covers()), plus the secret-plaintext leak guard + output.Sentinel positive assertion BE-0174 introduced for the variables-flavoured deny + allow paths.
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - PUT-replace-variables contract suite pattern (BE-0175 contract pattern, internal/controlplane/httpapi/environment_variables_put_test.go): the canonical contract suite for a customer-facing PUT-replace-{children} endpoint sitting on a bare-{id}-resolver route + secret-bearing child resource is the structural hybrid of (a) environment_grants_put_test.go (BE-0169 contract pattern, route-shape twin: same env-id resolver, same NewHandler positional port placement, same CapWrite vs CapAdmin difference noted in the role-deny tests) and (b) project_variables_test.go (BE-0142 GET pattern, resource-shape twin: same wire-level redaction chokepoint via output.Sentinel projection of is_secret rows, same leak-needle assertions on response bodies including the seeded secret plaintext). The new file lifts environment_grants_put_test.go's 12-test skeleton verbatim (handlerFor, putXXX, decode, missing-field 400 naming the field, malformed JSON, unknown field, unauth, viewer-in-tenant 403, NotFound, store InvalidInput, store unavailable, unwired = 500, OpenAPI registration) and adds TWO load-bearing additions: (1) the happy-path body POSITIVELY asserts got0.Value == output.Sentinel for the secret row AND negatively asserts the body does not contain the seeded plaintext — the chokepoint must fire on the post-write re-read even though the caller just submitted the plaintext; (2) a dedicated TestDeniesSupportInTenant — CapWrite has no support exception (the CapRead cross-tenant exception is one-way), so a CapWrite contract suite MUST positively assert support in their own tenant is denied 403, locking the deny against a future engine regression that widens CapWrite to support. Both directions are needed; either alone would silently regress.
  - apierr.InvalidInput wire shape: the renderer emits FieldViolation as "<field>: <reason>" inside the hint, not as a JSON key with quotes — so a contract test that asserts the field path reaches the wire must use the substring "variables: " (with the space), NOT \"variables\" with surrounding double-quotes. The mistake is easy because the success envelope DOES use \"variables\" as a JSON key — but the error envelope serialises the field path into a human-readable hint string instead.
  - NewHandler/newRouteTable positional-port arity sweeps in this repository land in MULTIPLE waves and the per-story sweep must cover ALL forms — not just the dominant pattern. The BE-0172 (EnvironmentVariableReader) sweep and the BE-0175 (EnvironmentVariableReplacer) sweep together caused: (a) the literal "fakeEnvironmentGrantReplacer{}, reader, nil)" anchor for the most common fully-typed helper, (b) the all-nils form newRouteTable(runtime.BuildInfo{}, nil x N) which has to grow from N to N+1 nils on every wave, (c) the build-variant form newRouteTable(build, nil x N) — uses 'build' instead of 'runtime.BuildInfo{}' and trips a different anchor, (d) the partial-fakes-with-trailing-nils form like 'fakeProjectGrantReader{}, nil, nil, ..., nil)' in projects_delete_test.go and projects_restore_test.go where the trailing nil run had to grow from 12 to 13. Pre-flight invariant: after each port-arity bump, run go vet ./internal/controlplane/httpapi/... BEFORE committing — vet surfaces every short-arity call site in one pass and is the only reliable way to find all four forms. Do NOT commit on the assumption that the dominant-pattern Node walker caught everything; vet is the authority.
  - listEnvironmentVariablesHandlerFor was a load-bearing example of the above: it was the lone test helper missed by the BE-0175 EnvironmentVariableReplacer wave. The fix is one trailing arg before the logger nil ('reader, nil)' → 'reader, fakeEnvironmentVariableReplacer{}, nil)'). The cause is structural: the helper was authored in the BE-0172 wave (when EnvironmentVariableReader was the LAST port) so it ended with 'reader, nil)' where the nil was the logger; the BE-0175 wave inserted the new Replacer port between the reader and the logger, but a helper that pre-dates the new port can't be caught by a sweep anchored on the new port's fake — it must be caught by go vet. The same pattern can hit any future port added between an existing trailing port and the logger.
  - "P=1 policy matrix story sitting on a P=2 endpoint story" picker rule (BE-0175 vs BE-0177): when a P=1 policy-matrix story (BE-0177) names an endpoint that does not yet exist (BE-0175's contract surface), the policy matrix CANNOT be implemented in isolation — the test file would reference a non-existent handler / handler builder / request builder. The historical precedent (BE-0172 GET endpoint P=2 → BE-0174 GET policy matrix P=1) shows the picker resolved this by selecting the P=2 endpoint story first even though a P=1 story was technically "higher priority". The same precedent applies here: pick BE-0175 first, then BE-0177 on the next iteration. The rule generalises: the highest-priority pending story that CAN be implemented end-to-end (i.e. whose handler / replacer / OpenAPI registration / port wiring all already exist or are part of THIS story) is the next story to pick; a P=1 matrix story whose endpoint is missing is BLOCKED on its P=2 endpoint sibling.

## 2026-05-16 - BE-0177
- Story scope: BE-0177 adds policy-matrix coverage for PUT /v1/environments/{environment_id}/variables. The structural twin of environment_grants_put_policy_test.go (BE-0171) at one capability tier lower: env.write = CapWrite (not CapAdmin), so Developer joins Owner/Admin in the role allow set, CI / Viewer / Support are denied via ReasonDeniedNoCapability, and the cross-tenant boundary still denies every role (Support included) because CapWrite is OUTSIDE the engine's `CapSupport && (CapRead || CapSupport)` exception. Distinct from env-grants, environment_variables rows store SECRET credential material, so the deny-path leak guards must cover BOTH the canonical post-write secret plaintext AND the caller-submitted secret plaintext in the request body — a denied PUT must not turn into a request-reflecting oracle for credentials.
- Files changed:
  - internal/controlplane/httpapi/environment_variables_put_policy_test.go (new file, 4 tests covering: full role matrix with allow set Owner/Admin/Developer and deny set Viewer/CI/Support — Developer in allow is the load-bearing distinction from BE-0171, CI in deny is the load-bearing distinction from a hypothetical "all writers allow" matrix since CI has CapDeploy but not CapWrite; revoked/expired key (Disabled=true) deny with replacer never running; wrong-organization principal — wire-level 404 via persistence, never 200/403, plus engine-level cross-tenant deny for ALL six roles INCLUDING Support since CapWrite is outside the support exception; grant containment — project-/env-/service-scoped grants all denied OutOfScope at the wire AND at the engine, the SAME-id env grant also OutOfScope, the sibling-project grant denied at the engine; org-level Developer grant ALLOWED end-to-end via ReasonAllowedByGrant with the wire-level redaction chokepoint still firing on the post-write re-read (secret value = output.Sentinel); org-level Viewer grant DENIED via ReasonDeniedNoCapability — the org-dev-allow / org-viewer-deny pair locks the CapWrite requirement against the grant path as a unit; stolen-key cross-tenant deny at the engine for a project-scoped grant whose home org has been swapped to a sibling org).
- Verification run:
  - gofmt -w . — no diff after first run.
  - go vet ./internal/controlplane/httpapi/ — clean.
  - go test -run TestReplaceEnvironmentVariablesPolicy ./internal/controlplane/httpapi/ — PASS (4 tests + 6 cross-tenant engine subtests).
  - go mod tidy — no changes.
  - go vet ./... — clean.
  - go test ./... — all green.
  - go test -race ./... — all green.
  - goimports not installed — noted in earlier progress entries; gofmt + vet are sufficient.
- Results: BE-0177 marked passes=true in prd.json.
- Remaining risks or follow-ups:
  - Acceptance criterion "All public responses use stable JSON envelopes with schema_version yalla.output.v1 or yalla.error.v1" is asserted on the allow path (decodeReplaceEnvironmentVariables checks schema_version=yalla.output.v1, ok=true, request_id non-empty) and on the deny path (decodeError checks the E_FORBIDDEN / E_NOT_FOUND code on yalla.error.v1) via the shared helpers.
  - Acceptance criterion "Integration tests run against isolated Postgres migrations and never require a live Dokploy server unless explicitly marked external" — the file is a pure-Go unit/contract test that never opens a database connection, never imports the dokploy client, and runs in the in-memory fake-store path of NewHandler.
  - Acceptance criterion "Secrets, tokens, API keys, cookies, and rendered environment variable values are redacted in logs, errors, audit metadata, and test output" — pinned at three boundaries: (1) the wire chokepoint on the allow path (post-write re-read renders is_secret=true rows as output.Sentinel, never the canonical or caller-submitted plaintext); (2) envVarsDenyBodyLeak watches the canonical seeded plaintext (canonicalEnvVarsSecretPlaintext) on every deny path; (3) the new replaceEnvironmentVariablesRequestBodyLeak watches the caller-submitted secret needle (replaceEnvironmentVariablesMatrixSecretNeedle) on every deny path. The request-body leak guard is the load-bearing addition unique to env.write because env-grants rows carry no credential material — write endpoints whose request body carries plaintext secrets need a body-direction leak guard, not just a response-direction guard.
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - **The "PUT-shaped policy matrix test" pattern for a CapWrite endpoint** that BE-0177 instantiates from BE-0171's CapAdmin template:
    - Reuse the shared canonicals from the GET-side policy test (canonicalEnvVarsEnvironmentID, canonicalEnvVarsProjectID, canonicalEnvVarsSecretPlaintext, canonicalEnvironmentVariables, envVarsDenyBodyLeak) — do NOT redeclare them.
    - Reuse the shared PUT contract helpers from the corresponding put-contract test (replaceEnvironmentVariablesHandlerFor, putEnvironmentVariables, decodeReplaceEnvironmentVariables, fakeEnvironmentVariableReplacer with vars/err/got fields) — do NOT redeclare them.
    - Reuse the shared identity / principal helpers (orgPrincipal, decodeError) — do NOT redeclare them.
    - Add ONLY the file-local request body constant and the body-direction leak guard (request-body needles distinct from the canonical needles), because those are unique to the write direction.
  - **Cap tier governs three load-bearing properties** at the policy matrix layer: (1) which roles allow in own tenant (CapWrite admits Developer / not CI; CapAdmin admits neither); (2) which roles allow cross-tenant via the support exception (CapRead / CapSupport admit Support; CapWrite / CapAdmin do not — the engine's `required == CapRead || required == CapSupport` is the gate); (3) which org-level grant roles allow via ReasonAllowedByGrant (CapWrite is admitted by Developer + Admin + Owner; CapAdmin is admitted by Admin + Owner only). The "org-developer allow paired with org-viewer deny" assertion in TestReplaceEnvironmentVariablesPolicyGrantContainment is the load-bearing CapWrite-vs-CapRead unit-test: a future catalog change that downgraded env.write to CapRead would still pass the org-developer allow check (Developer holds both CapRead and CapWrite) but fail the org-viewer deny check (Viewer holds CapRead but not CapWrite, so a CapRead downgrade would flip viewer to allow). Pair them per-endpoint to lock the cap tier as a unit.
  - **Credential-bearing write endpoints need a body-direction leak guard.** env.grants.write rows store no credential material — only role enum + structural ids — so the env-grants leak guard pair watches only the structural request needles. env.write rows store the secret plaintext, so the request body itself carries secret material on every request. The new replaceEnvironmentVariablesRequestBodyLeak embeds a globally-unique fragment (replaceEnvironmentVariablesMatrixSecretNeedle) into the secret value so even a partial echo (e.g., a future renderer that surfaced the first 32 chars of the value in an error message) fails the guard. This pattern generalizes: ANY future write endpoint whose request body carries plaintext credential material (project variables PUT, org variables PUT, api-key create/rotate where a returned token might be reflected, etc.) MUST embed a unique fragment in the credential field of the matrix body and watch for it on every deny path. Structural-needle guards are insufficient because they would miss a renderer that scrubbed only the request shape (keys + booleans) without scrubbing the value column.
  - **The "wire chokepoint must fire on EVERY allow path"** assertion in TestReplaceEnvironmentVariablesPolicyGrantContainment is load-bearing: BE-0175 pinned the chokepoint on the role-allow path (TestReplaceEnvironmentVariablesReturnsPersistedVariables), but a regression in environmentVariableOf that only re-projected secret plaintext on the grant-allow code path (or vice versa) would slip past role-only coverage. Asserting Value == output.Sentinel AND the canonical plaintext is absent AND the caller-supplied secret needle is absent on the grant-allow path here closes that gap. Generalizes to: when an endpoint has BOTH a role-allow path AND a grant-allow path (i.e., the policy engine has two distinct admit routes), the wire chokepoint must be pinned on BOTH paths, not just the one driven by the put-contract test.
  - **CapWrite-vs-CapAdmin cross-tenant deny is universal across roles** — the engine's exception clause `CapSupport && (CapRead || CapSupport)` admits Support cross-tenant ONLY for CapRead and CapSupport actions. CapWrite, CapAdmin, CapDeploy, CapOwner are all outside it, so EVERY role (including Support) is denied cross-tenant for any of those capabilities via ReasonDeniedCrossTenant. The engine-level cross-tenant subtest sweep at the bottom of TestReplaceEnvironmentVariablesPolicyWrongOrganizationPrincipal (and the matching one at the bottom of TestReplaceEnvironmentGrantsPolicyWrongOrganizationPrincipal) is the structural lock: any future catalog change that moved env.write into the support cross-tenant exception (or widened the exception) would fail those subtests before it could ship.

## 2026-05-16 - BE-0034 - Implement break-glass admin access
- What was implemented: the durable, audit-stamped internal-support
  break-glass surface — the layer that records (and ends) a time-bounded
  session in which a Yalla support principal reaches into another tenant.
  - internal/controlplane/store/migrate/migrations/0019_break_glass_sessions.up.sql / .down.sql (new):
    break_glass_sessions table (text PK with the bgs_ prefix minted in
    Go, target organization FK, actor id/kind, actor_organization_id,
    reason CHECK (length > 0), started_at, expires_at with
    CHECK (expires_at > started_at), nullable revoked_at + revoked_by_id/
    revoked_by_kind, request/correlation/ip/user_agent, version, created_at,
    updated_at). Indexes: (organization_id, started_at DESC), (actor_id,
    started_at DESC) and a partial active index (organization_id, expires_at)
    WHERE revoked_at IS NULL. Triggers: set_updated_at + bump_version from
    migration 0011, plus break_glass_sessions_reject_rewrite — an
    application-level UPDATE may only set the revocation columns, so the
    reason, target, actor, started/expires/request ids are immutable even
    against a SQL console.
  - internal/controlplane/store/break_glass.go (new): BreakGlassSession
    value + Active(t) helper + BreakGlassRepository with Append (tx,
    minting bgs_<hex> ids), Get (tenant-scoped, NotFound on a foreign
    org's id), ListByOrganization (clamped at 200, ordered by
    started_at DESC, id DESC), MarkRevoked (returns Conflict when the
    session is already revoked, distinguishing it from NotFound via a
    follow-up Get inside the same tx).
  - internal/controlplane/store/break_glass_service.go (new):
    BreakGlassService unit-of-work orchestrator. StartSession composes
    in one transaction: organization-existence check, session-row
    insert, audit append. The audit metadata always carries
    elevated_access=true, target_organization_id, expires_at (RFC3339),
    ttl_seconds, and break_glass_session_id, so a single grep against
    audit_events identifies every break-glass action. Revoke composes
    organization-existence check + MarkRevoked + audit append — also
    with elevated_access=true plus action_kind=revoke. List/GetSession
    open Store.Read sessions for consistent reads. The service-layer
    validator rejects blank reason, oversized reason (>4096), missing
    actor_id, bad actor_kind (closed to usr/sa), non-positive TTL, and
    caps excessive TTL at 24h. The reason is run through
    output.NewRedactor before persistence so a credential transport
    pattern in a justification is scrubbed.
  - internal/controlplane/store/break_glass_internal_test.go (new):
    white-box unit tests for buildSessionToCreate — valid input shape,
    blank/oversize reason rejection, missing organization/actor,
    bad actor_kind, non-positive TTL rejected, excessive TTL capped to
    24h, redactor scrubs Authorization header out of the reason value,
    session.Active(t) flips on revocation and expiry, NewBreakGlassService
    nil-dependency guards, and the audit metadata composition
    confirms elevated_access=true.
  - internal/controlplane/store/break_glass_test.go (new): Postgres
    integration suite. StartSession persists row + audit
    atomically with elevated_access=true / target_organization_id /
    break_glass_session_id pinned on the event; blank-reason fails as
    InvalidInput and writes nothing; unknown-tenant fails as NotFound;
    Revoke flips revoked_at + revoked_by_id and is also audited; a
    second Revoke is a typed Conflict; tenant-isolation proves a
    session id in another org is NotFound and a list from another
    org yields zero rows; the append-mostly trigger refuses an
    UPDATE that would rewrite or blank the reason.
  - internal/controlplane/httpapi/break_glass.go (new):
    BreakGlassController port + four thin handlers behind
    /v1/organizations/{org_id}/break-glass{,/{session_id}}:
    POST (start, 201), GET (list, ?limit=1..200 default 50),
    GET (single), DELETE (revoke). Body decoded with
    validate.DecodeJSON; missing/negative/excessive ttl_seconds is a
    stable E_INVALID_INPUT before any database work; the response
    body carries the persisted session with a computed Active flag
    and a fixed elevated_access:true. ttl_seconds is the wire
    contract (JSON-native integers); the handler forwards it as a
    time.Duration to the service.
  - internal/controlplane/httpapi/routes.go: new tagAdmin constant
    plus four apiRoute entries with RequiresAuth + RequiredAction
    string(policy.ActionAdminBreakGlass) and organizationIDResolver,
    so the engine resolves the (CapSupport) admin.break_glass action
    against the {org_id} target — a support principal acting
    cross-tenant lands on ReasonAllowedBySupport, and a non-support
    role is rejected with ReasonDeniedNoCapability before any handler
    runs. newRouteTable gained a final breakGlass BreakGlassController
    parameter.
  - internal/controlplane/httpapi/server.go: NewHandler gained the
    breakGlass BreakGlassController port immediately before the
    logger, and forwards it into newRouteTable.
  - internal/controlplane/httpapi/break_glass_fakes_test.go (new):
    fakeBreakGlassController satisfying the BreakGlassController port
    with optional recording pointers so the public-surface and
    unrelated-endpoint suites pass a zero value while the break-glass
    suites set canned results and read inputs back.
  - internal/controlplane/httpapi/break_glass_test.go (new): contract
    + tenant-isolation coverage. POST success returns 201 with the
    session and elevated_access=true; missing reason / missing TTL /
    negative TTL / excessive TTL each surface as E_INVALID_INPUT
    400; unauthenticated is E_AUTH 401; an owner principal acting
    on its own tenant is E_FORBIDDEN 403 (CapSupport gate, no
    CapAdmin shortcut); a store-side failure stays a typed 5xx.
    LIST/GET/DELETE round-trip the canonical happy paths. The
    "Break-glass cannot mint customer API keys" guarantee is pinned
    by TestSupportPrincipalCannotMintAPIKeys: a support principal
    posting to /v1/organizations/{org_id}/api-keys is denied for
    both the home org and a cross-tenant org, never reaching the
    api-key creator.
  - cmd/yalla-api/main.go: wires *store.BreakGlassService into
    NewHandler from the existing pool / audit repository.
  - Every existing test that builds NewHandler or newRouteTable
    (44 files, 78 call sites) was patched to pass
    fakeBreakGlassController{} / nil at the new argument position.

- Verification run from the repository root:
  - gofmt -w .                         -> ok
  - goimports -w .                     -> not installed, skipped
  - go mod tidy                        -> ok
  - go vet ./...                       -> ok
  - go test ./...                      -> all packages PASS
  - go test -race ./...                -> all packages PASS
  - go test ./internal/controlplane/store/ -run BreakGlass -count=1     -> PASS
  - go test ./internal/controlplane/httpapi/ -run BreakGlass -count=1   -> PASS

- Remaining risks / follow-ups:
  - admin.break_glass actions all share one action string today; a
    future story can split start vs revoke if reporting wants a
    finer-grained audit projection.
  - A scheduled sweeper that flips active=false / surfaces expiry
    metrics is not part of this story — Active(t) is computed by
    the wire projection at read time, so an elapsed deadline is
    correct without a sweeper, but operational dashboards may want
    one.
  - X-Forwarded-For / X-Real-IP are deliberately NOT honoured here;
    the audit row records the immediate transport peer. A trusted-
    proxy story can replace clientIP later without changing the
    audit shape.

- Learnings for future iterations:
  - Adding a port to NewHandler/newRouteTable touches ~44 test files
    and ~78 call sites. A scripted insertion ("inject the new arg as
    the penultimate arg of NewHandler and as the last arg of
    newRouteTable") was reliable and fast; a regex pass alone is
    not, because the trailing arg varies (nil / logger / a real
    *slog.Logger). See the throwaway Node.js script used here for
    the paren-counting approach.
  - Combine read+write methods on the same store-layer service when
    a single HTTP port is the natural shape (BreakGlassService
    carries StartSession/Revoke/ListSessions/GetSession instead of
    splitting into BreakGlassReader). This keeps NewHandler from
    accumulating two ports for one feature.
  - The append-mostly trigger pattern (a PL/pgSQL BEFORE UPDATE that
    refuses to rewrite any column except a whitelist) is a clean
    way to give a row "structural immutability except for one state
    transition" — useful for sessions, soft-deletes, leases, and
    any other row where audit-trail integrity matters.
  - elevated_access=true is now a load-bearing audit-metadata key
    for break-glass and should keep the same literal value across
    future stories so analytics queries stay stable.

    story added are exactly the artefacts the matrix test would
    reference.

- Learnings for future iterations:
  - The picker rule "P=1 policy-matrix story sitting on a P=2 endpoint
    story" rule (recorded by BE-0175) held again here: BE-0180 is
    P=1 but blocked on BE-0178's handler artefacts. The pattern now
    has a third instance (after BE-0172/BE-0174 and BE-0175/BE-0177).
  - The services store package was a brand-new persistence module
    rather than an extension of an existing one — but it follows the
    exact ProjectVariableReader / EnvironmentReader template
    (Repository for raw SQL + Reader composing parent existence check
    + child list inside one Store.Read transaction). Future
    deployment / log / metric / domain readers should follow the same
    shape rather than minting new abstractions.
  - The cross-tenant leak assertion in store integration tests must
    NOT include the path parameter the test itself supplies — only
    sibling/child identifiers count as leaks. A NotFound message
    legitimately echoes the caller-supplied id back so the caller
    knows which lookup failed; the contract is "do not reveal IDs
    the caller did not already know". The corrected pattern matches
    EnvironmentReader's TestEnvironmentReaderRejectsCrossTenantProjectID
    leakable list ([envB.ID, projB.ID, envB.Slug] excludes the
    path-supplied projB.ID).
  - The penultimate-arg insertion sweep used by BE-0034 still works:
    a paren-counting Node.js script that finds every NewHandler( and
    newRouteTable( call site, splits the comma-separated args at the
    top level (respecting nested {}, [], ()), and inserts the new
    fake literal before the second-to-last arg (NewHandler — its last
    arg is the logger / nil) or before the last arg (newRouteTable —
    no logger). Total scope: 44 files / 62 NewHandler calls + 16
    files / 17 newRouteTable calls. gofmt cleans up the spacing the
    insert leaves behind.
  - Pre-existing local-DB failures in the store package are a
    smell: when a story-time `go test` against a local Postgres
    surfaces failures that ALSO fail on HEAD, the picker should
    still go ahead — but they are a worth-flagging signal that the
    test fixture factory drifted from the assertions in another
    story's tests. Not this story's scope to fix.
