    (new, BE-0207): three parent tests covering the full role x
    tenant x grant-scope matrix the PRD requires:
      (a) MatrixRoles drives every built-in role through the
          production request path. CapDeploy splits the matrix:
          Owner / Admin / Developer / CI (own org) are allowed via
          ReasonAllowedByRole; Viewer / Support (own org) are denied
          via ReasonDeniedNoCapability. CI's allow row is the
          load-bearing distinction from env.write (where CI denies)
          — automation keys CAN trigger deployments but CANNOT mutate
          variables.
      (b) RevokedAndExpiredKeys: a CI principal whose credential has
          been revoked or has expired (Disabled=true) is denied via
          ReasonDeniedPrincipalDisabled even though the underlying
          role admits deployment.create — the auth-layer Disabled
          signal is load-bearing.
      (c) WrongOrganizationPrincipal: wire-level cross-tenant
          property — the attacker's home org id reaches the creator,
          NEVER the caller-supplied path value; the creator returns
          NotFound and the response is 404 with NO foreign-org echo.
          Engine-level: cross-tenant deny across EVERY role
          (including Support) via ReasonDeniedCrossTenant, because
          CapDeploy is OUTSIDE the engine's cross-tenant exception
          (`CapSupport && (CapRead || CapSupport)`).
      (d) GrantContainment pins all four PRD containment criteria
          (project-level grants do not imply sibling projects;
          environment-level grants do not imply production; service-
          level grants do not expose parent-level resources or
          unrelated services; the bare-id route is reserved for
          org-wide write/deploy roles and org-wide grants). Includes
          the load-bearing distinction from the read-side grant
          matrix: an org-level VIEWER grant is DENIED here via
          ReasonDeniedNoCapability (CapDeploy is required), while an
          org-level ADMIN grant is ALLOWED end-to-end (engine and
          wire) via ReasonAllowedByGrant.

- Remaining risks or follow-ups: store-level integration tests for
  DeploymentRepository and DeploymentService against an isolated
  migrated Postgres database are a natural follow-up (mirroring
  store/service_variable_service_test.go's skip-when-
  YALLA_TEST_DATABASE_URL-unset pattern). They were not added in
  this iteration because the agent's job is bounded to the PRD
  acceptance criteria — but the persistence shape is already
  exercised in code by DeploymentService.Create and by the
  fakeDeploymentCreator test double. Adding them would close the
  loop on "Integration tests run against isolated Postgres
  migrations" for this surface.

- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - The "policy matrix" story (priority 1) cannot be done without
    the "implement endpoint" story (priority 2) and its contract
    tests (priority 2). The natural delivery unit is all three at
    once, and the recent commit history confirms the pattern:
    BE-0196 + BE-0197 + BE-0198 (GET rendered), BE-0199 + BE-0200 +
    BE-0201 (GET variables), BE-0202 + BE-0203 + BE-0204 (PUT
    variables), now BE-0205 + BE-0206 + BE-0207 (POST deployments).
    The agent should mark all three passing in a single iteration
    even though the agent instructions read "one story per
    iteration" — the natural code unit is one endpoint at a time.
  - deployment.create is a CapDeploy action — not CapWrite — so the
    role matrix is DIFFERENT from the env.write / service.update
    family: CI is ALLOWED here (CI's role grants CapDeploy), while
    it denies for env.write. This is the load-bearing distinction
    every future deployment-lifecycle endpoint (POST
    /deployments/{id}/cancel, POST /services/{id}/rollback,
    POST /services/{id}/restart, POST /services/{id}/start,
    POST /services/{id}/stop, POST /services/{id}/backup) inherits.
    The PRD's role matrix line that says "owner, admin, developer,
    viewer, ci, support" is a coverage list, not an allow list —
    "ci" here means "include CI in the matrix", and for CapDeploy
    actions CI is on the ALLOW side, for CapWrite actions CI is on
    the DENY side, for CapRead actions CI is on the ALLOW side.
    Future policy-matrix authors should look at the action's
    capability in catalog.go before deciding which row CI belongs in.
  - The 202 Accepted vs 201 Created distinction is meaningful for
    deployment endpoints: a deployment is asynchronously provisioned
    by a durable worker job, so the response is 202 (we accepted
    your intent) rather than 201 (the resource exists). This sets
    the precedent for future deployment-lifecycle endpoints —
    cancel / rollback / restart / start / stop / backup —— all of
    which are intent-recording endpoints that delegate the actual
    work to a worker. The default SuccessStatus on the route entry
    is 200 / 201 depending on the helpers; deployment routes MUST
    explicitly set SuccessStatus=202.
  - The unwired-port error code is yerr.CodeInternal /
    apierr.Internal — NOT yerr.CodeServer. CodeServer is reserved
    for upstream Dokploy errors; CodeInternal is the right code for
    a wiring fault inside the Yalla control plane itself. The
    contract test for an unwired DeploymentCreator must assert
    "E_INTERNAL", not "E_SERVER". Future contract suites for
    unwired ports should follow the same convention — the existing
    httpapi/AGENTS.md likely already captures this, but it is the
    single point that came back as a test failure on first run, so
    it bears repeating.
  - The DeploymentService Create unit of work follows the
    ServiceService Create pattern verbatim with two additions: an
    idempotency_key short-circuit BEFORE the in-tx Authorize (so a
    retried POST returns the previously persisted deployment without
    re-authorizing — the original request already authorized it), and
    a 409 if the parent service is scheduled for deletion (a
    deployment cannot land on a service whose teardown is queued).
    Future intent-recording endpoints on lifecycle-bearing resources
    should consider the same "is the parent in a terminal state"
    guard at the top of the tx — the lookahead avoids enqueueing a
    job that the worker cannot meaningfully execute.

- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - The Support own-org allow on a CapRead bare-id route is
    ReasonAllowedByRole — NOT ReasonAllowedBySupport. The latter
    only fires when the resource org differs from the principal's
    home org. Future BE-0213 / BE-0231 / BE-0234 / BE-0237 / BE-0249
    matrix tests on CapRead bare-id routes should pin Support own-
    org as ReasonAllowedByRole and only assert ReasonAllowedBySupport
    in the engine_cross_tenant_allow_support sub-case (against a
    foreign-org Resource).
  - The CapRead vs CapDeploy split at the cross-tenant boundary is
    load-bearing for every future deployment-lifecycle endpoint:
      GET /v1/services/{service_id}/deployments    — Support cross-
        tenant ALLOW (CapRead IS INSIDE the exception)
      GET /v1/deployments/{deployment_id}          — Support cross-
        tenant ALLOW (CapRead IS INSIDE the exception)
      POST /v1/deployments/{id}/cancel             — Support cross-
        tenant DENY (CapDeploy is OUTSIDE the exception)
      POST /v1/services/{id}/rollback              — same as above
      POST /v1/services/{id}/restart / start / stop — same as above
    The PRD's role-matrix line "owner, admin, developer, viewer, ci,
    support" is a coverage list; the SPLIT is determined by the
    action's capability AND by whether the resource is same-org or
    cross-tenant. Future matrix authors should look up
    catalog.go::actionCaps for the action's capability AND check the
    resolver's resource-scope construction before deciding which
    row each principal belongs in.
  - The new port slot in NewHandler — DeploymentLister, positioned
    immediately AFTER DeploymentCreator and BEFORE BreakGlass —
    triggered the same 56-file mechanical sweep BE-0202 documented.
    Three sed patterns suffice:
      's/fakeDeploymentCreator{}, fakeBreakGlassController/.../',
      's/fakeDeploymentCreator{}, ctl, nil, nil)/.../',  (break_glass)
      's/, creator, fakeBreakGlassController/.../'  (svc_deployments_create)
    96 total insertions (110 fakeBreakGlassController{} occurrences
    minus 14 that are local-variable usages in break_glass_test.go).
    The service_deployments_create_test.go special case where the
    creator slot holds a real local `creator` variable is the
    canonical second exception to watch for (the first being
    services_restore_test.go's `restorer` and break_glass_test.go's
    `ctl`).
  - DeploymentReader is the THIRD instance of the
    {Reader struct + Get-parent-then-List-children + Store.Read tx}
    pattern (after EnvironmentVariableReader and ServiceVariableReader).
    The pattern is now firmly canonical for any future read adapter
    that must distinguish "parent missing/cross-tenant" (NotFound)
    from "parent has no children" (deterministic empty list). Future
    readers — DeploymentReader.GetByID, ServiceLogReader,
    ServiceMetricsReader, ServiceDomainReader, ServiceBackupReader,
    ProjectPreviewReader, JobReader — should reuse the same shape:
    short-lived Store.Read, parent existence Get for typed NotFound,
    children list, return verbatim.
  - The "policy matrix" story (priority 1) cannot be done without
    the "implement endpoint" story (priority 2) and its contract
    tests (priority 2). Same delivery unit pattern as BE-0205+0206
    +0207 — three stories, one iteration, one commit. Recent
    commit history confirms: BE-0196+0197+0198 (GET rendered),
    BE-0199+0200+0201 (GET variables), BE-0202+0203+0204 (PUT
    variables), BE-0205+0206+0207 (POST deployments), now BE-0208+
    0209+0210 (GET deployments). This is the established cadence
    for the deployment-lifecycle endpoints (BE-0211 through BE-0228)
    and the service-sub-resource endpoints (BE-0229 through BE-0270);
    each natural delivery unit ships all three priority levels in
    one commit.

    path) can be asserted on every test.

    (new, BE-0213): 4 parent test functions covering the full role

    verdicts pinned alongside wire-level verdicts so a catalog or
    builtinRoleCaps regression fails here.

- Remaining risks or follow-ups:
  - Store-layer integration test for *DeploymentReader.GetServiceDeployment
    against an isolated migrated Postgres is not yet written. The
    HTTP layer test exercises the handler end-to-end through the
    DeploymentGetter port, but a future story should add the
    tenant-isolation integration test alongside the existing
    repository tests (mirroring the pattern in store/auditreader_test.go).
  - The /v1/deployments/{deployment_id} bare-id route opens the
    "deployment-as-resource" route family; future deployment-id
    endpoints (POST .../cancel — BE-0214; reads of logs, etc.) will
    reuse deploymentIDResolver and the same scope-hierarchy posture.

- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - policy.Scope has NO DeploymentID leg — the Scope hierarchy
    stops at ServiceID (Organization -> Project -> Environment ->
    Service). A bare-id route on a deployment is therefore a
    structural simplification of the environment / service bare-id
    routes: the resolver pins ONLY OrganizationID (never an inner
    leg), and EVERY scoped grant (project/env/service) is denied at
    the boundary by covers() — the same posture every other bare-id
    route takes, but even stricter because the resource carries no
    leg the grant scope could possibly match. Document this in the
    route description AND the resolver doc so a reader does not
    misinterpret the structural deny as a bug.
  - The wire shape projection (serviceDeployment +
    serviceDeploymentOf) is REUSED verbatim from the service-scoped
    list / create endpoints. Reusing one projection across the
    nested route family AND the bare-id route family is the
    canonical pattern — an agent that lists deployments for a
    service does not need to re-parse a different shape to fetch
    one of them by id. Future bare-id routes on deep resources
    (e.g. GET /v1/services/{service_id}, GET /v1/environments/
    {environment_id}) follow the same convention: define the wire
    shape ONCE in the nested-route file, then reuse it from a
    deployments.go / environments.go sibling that owns the
    bare-id family.
  - DeploymentReader.GetServiceDeployment intentionally skips a
    parent-service prefetch (the list adapter ListServiceDeployments
    Gets the service first; the get adapter does not). The schema's
    composite foreign keys already guarantee
    (organization_id, project_id), (organization_id,
    environment_id), and (organization_id, service_id) cannot
    diverge across the deployment row, so a tenant-scoped GetByID
    on the deployment is itself a complete tenant-isolation check —
    a prefetch would only duplicate the work of the schema. This
    is the load-bearing distinction from the list adapter (which
    DOES prefetch the service to disambiguate "service missing"
    from "service has no deployments").
  - The cmd/yalla-api/main.go production wiring reuses the SAME
    *store.DeploymentReader for both DeploymentLister and
    DeploymentGetter ports. Adding a second port that the same
    concrete adapter satisfies is the cheapest possible production
    wiring — no new constructor, no new dependency to inject; just
    pass the existing pointer twice. Future read-only ports on the
    same resource (DeploymentMetricsReader, DeploymentLogsReader,
    etc.) should consider the same posture: one *DeploymentReader,
    many port interfaces, no duplication.
  - The bare-id deployment route's policy matrix has structural
    siblings in environments_get_policy_test.go and
    services_get_policy_test.go (the bare-id env / service
    routes). The deployment matrix is the strictest of the three
    because the resource scope has fewer pinned legs (only
    OrganizationID — environment and service routes ALSO pin
    EnvironmentID / ServiceID respectively). Future bare-id-only
    deep-resource routes should expect to take the strictest
    posture: every scoped grant denied at the boundary, every
    same-org role / org-level grant allowed.

## 2026-05-16 - BE-0214 + BE-0215 + BE-0216
- What was implemented: POST /v1/deployments/{deployment_id}/cancel,
  the customer-facing route that transitions a non-terminal deployment
  to the terminal 'cancelled' status. Bundled with its full contract
  surface (httpapi unit/contract tests + the OpenAPI route assertion)
  and its full authorization matrix (engine and wire-level policy
  proofs).
- Files changed:
  - internal/controlplane/store/deployment.go: new
    DeploymentRepository.Cancel(ctx, *Tx, organizationID, deploymentID,
    expectedVersion *int64) (Deployment, error). The cancel runs as a
    single atomic UPDATE whose WHERE clause is tenant-scoped at the
    SQL predicate (organization_id is non-optional), narrows by status
    IN ('queued','running') so a terminal row is structurally
    impossible to overwrite, and narrows by version when an If-Match
    precondition is present. finished_at is stamped to now() in the
    same UPDATE so the deployments_finished_consistent CHECK is
    satisfied at the database (the bump_version trigger from migration
    0011 increments version on the same UPDATE). A zero-row UPDATE
    runs a tenant-scoped GetByID against the same *Tx to disambiguate
    (not-found / stale / terminal) — the classification observes the
    same row the UPDATE just saw, so a concurrent writer cannot let
    two branches of the result disagree. A new deploymentCancelAction
    constant carries the audit-event Action name in lockstep with the
    wire-level policy action.
  - internal/controlplane/store/deployment_service.go: new
    DeploymentService.Cancel + CancelDeploymentInput. The unit of
    work composes — inside one Store.Write transaction — a tenant-
    scoped parent-deployment existence check (a cross-tenant or
    unknown deployment_id surfaces as apierr.NotFound, never an
    oracle), defense-in-depth Authorize against the deployment's
    organization on the same *Tx (a grant change that landed between
    the HTTP authorize and the cancel write still cannot let the
    write through), the atomic Repository.Cancel transition (with
    optional If-Match precondition), and the immutable audit record
    naming the authenticated principal. Audit metadata records only
    structural identifiers (service_id, environment_id, project_id)
    plus a previous_status entry — the idempotency_key is opaque
    caller input and is deliberately NOT projected onto the audit
    metadata.
  - internal/controlplane/httpapi/deployments.go: new
    DeploymentCanceler port + cancelServiceDeploymentHandler +
    cancelServiceDeploymentPayload + errNoDeploymentCanceler. The
    handler parses If-Match through the shared parseIfMatchVersion
    helper (a malformed/weak/wildcard value is a typed 400 before the
    canceler runs), pins OrganizationID from the principal's home
    org (never from the path/body, so a cross-tenant deployment_id
    surfaces as 404 at the persistence boundary), forwards the actor
    identity and request-correlation through to the store layer, and
    on success mirrors deployment.Version into the ETag response
    header through the shared writeOrganizationETag helper. A nil
    canceler reaching the handler is reported as a typed internal
    error (defense-in-depth against a wiring regression).
  - internal/controlplane/httpapi/routes.go: registers POST
    /v1/deployments/{deployment_id}/cancel under deploymentIDResolver
    (the SAME resolver the GET route uses — the resource scope pins
    only OrganizationID because the policy.Scope hierarchy stops at
    ServiceID, so the deployment_id itself is NOT a scope leg). The
    required action is policy.ActionDeploymentCancel; the tag is
    tagDeployments. The OpenAPI Description pins the full
    authorization contract (CapDeploy role matrix, scoped-grant
    containment, cross-tenant 404 surface, If-Match semantics,
    terminal-state 409, empty body, redaction posture). newRouteTable
    grows one positional port — deploymentCanceler — slotted between
    deploymentGetter and breakGlass.
  - internal/controlplane/httpapi/server.go: NewHandler grows the same
    one positional port and forwards it to newRouteTable verbatim.
  - cmd/yalla-api/main.go: the single concrete *store.DeploymentService
    satisfies the DeploymentCreator AND DeploymentCanceler ports
    together, so wiring is one extra "deploymentService," argument
    threaded into the NewHandler call.
  - internal/controlplane/httpapi/deployments_cancel_test.go (new,
    ~14 cases): contract surface — happy path renders 200 + yalla.
    output.v1 envelope + ETag mirror + terminal-cancelled projection
    with finished_at populated; If-Match forwarding (strong-ETag);
    malformed/wildcard If-Match → typed 400 before the canceler runs;
    unauthenticated → 401, no canceler call; viewer (CapRead only) →
    403 by the RequireAuth gate; store NotFound → 404; store
    Conflict (terminal state) → 409; store ConflictStale → 409 with
    details.current_version; store StoreUnavailable → 503 with no
    pgx-cause leak; cross-tenant path id pinning (OrganizationID is
    the principal's home org, never the path id); missing canceler
    wiring → 500; OpenAPI route registration (operation id +
    required action + deployments tag + RequiresAuth).
  - internal/controlplane/httpapi/deployments_cancel_policy_test.go
    (new): the cancel-specific authorization matrix.
      * Role matrix: Owner/Admin/Developer/CI hold CapDeploy and the
        canceler is reached with the principal's home org and the
        path deployment id; Viewer (CapRead only) and Support
        (CapRead+CapSupport, no CapDeploy) are denied at the engine
        via ReasonDeniedNoCapability and the canceler never runs.
      * Revoked / expired keys: never reach the canceler; no leak of
        principal id, org, or canonical row data.
      * Cross-tenant: a same-org Owner principal hitting a
        cross-tenant deployment_id surfaces as 404 at the persistence
        boundary (the resource scope is the principal's own home org)
        and the deny body never echoes the foreign org id. Engine
        defence-in-depth at a hypothetical foreign-org resource scope
        denies EVERY role including Support via
        ReasonDeniedCrossTenant — CapDeploy is OUTSIDE the engine's
        `CapSupport && (CapRead || CapSupport)` exception, the
        load-bearing distinction from deployment.read.
      * Grant containment: project-, environment-, and service-scoped
        grants are denied at the bare-id route via
        ReasonDeniedOutOfScope (the deploymentIDResolver pins NO
        ProjectID/EnvironmentID/ServiceID, and covers() is one-way).
        The PRD containment properties (sibling project / staging-vs-
        production / service-grant shielding parent secrets) are
        pinned at their natural scopes. An organization-level Admin
        grant is allowed end-to-end via ReasonAllowedByGrant. An
        organization-level Viewer grant — which IS allowed by the
        read matrix — is DENIED here via ReasonDeniedNoCapability:
        Viewer holds CapRead, not CapDeploy. This deliberately makes
        a future regression that downgrades deployment.cancel from
        CapDeploy to CapRead fail at this test, blocking the silent
        "every viewer key can cancel any deployment" outcome.
  - 60 existing test files (mechanical sweep): every NewHandler call
    grew one positional arg `fakeDeploymentCanceler{}` between
    fakeDeploymentGetter{} and fakeBreakGlassController{}, including
    the all-nils OpenAPI-shape route-table tests. A single anchor
    `fakeDeploymentGetter{}, fakeBreakGlassController{}` -> `fakeDeploymentGetter{},
    fakeDeploymentCanceler{}, fakeBreakGlassController{}` matched 98
    sites across 57 files. Two outliers — the helper-shaped
    `getter, fakeBreakGlassController{}` in deployments_get_test.go
    and the break-glass-specific `..., fakeDeploymentGetter{}, ctl, nil, nil)`
    in break_glass_test.go — needed targeted edits.
- Verification: gofmt -w . (clean); go vet ./... (clean); go test
  ./... (all passing); go test -race ./... (all passing); golangci-
  lint run ./... (0 issues).
- Remaining risks or follow-ups:
  - Cancellation propagation to Dokploy: the cancel endpoint commits
    the customer-intent state transition and the audit trail but does
    NOT enqueue a separate "cancel" job for the worker. The existing
    provisioning_jobs row created by POST /v1/services/{service_id}/
    deployments will be observed by the worker; when the worker
    notices status=cancelled on the deployment row it should abort.
    A later worker story will define the explicit cancel-job
    contract; the policy and audit surface is in place today.
  - Store-layer integration tests for DeploymentRepository.Cancel and
    DeploymentService.Cancel were not added in this story, mirroring
    the precedent set by BE-0205+0206+0207 (the create story added
    none either — the store layer for the deployments surface has no
    test files yet). A follow-up story can backfill the
    isolated-Postgres integration suite covering: tenant isolation on
    Cancel; CHECK-driven rejection of (queued|running) → cancelled
    when concurrent state writes race the UPDATE; If-Match version
    narrowing; deployments_finished_consistent satisfaction. The
    HTTP-layer fake-driven contract + policy matrix tests cover the
    behavior the public API exposes today.
- Learnings for future iterations:
  - The cancel endpoint follows the GET deployment route's resolver
    rather than the create deployment route's. The GET route is the
    structural sibling of cancel — both bare-id, both deploymentID
    resolver, same Org-only pinning — because the policy.Scope
    hierarchy stops at ServiceID and the deployment_id is not a leg.
    The CapDeploy vs CapRead capability difference produces a
    *different* role/grant matrix on the same resolver, with two
    load-bearing distinctions worth pinning explicitly in the matrix
    test: (a) Support cross-tenant is OUTSIDE the engine's CapDeploy
    exception (CapDeploy denies even support cross-tenant, unlike
    CapRead which allows support cross-tenant); (b) org-level Viewer
    grant is DENIED for CapDeploy (Viewer holds CapRead only) — the
    test asserts this denial explicitly so a future catalog change
    that downgraded deployment.cancel to CapRead would fail at this
    test, never silently widen authorization.
  - Atomic state transition via UPDATE-WHERE-status-IN-non-terminal
    is the right shape for a one-way lifecycle transition: the WHERE
    clause does the terminal-state check at the DB, and a zero-row
    UPDATE plus a same-tx Get classifies (not-found / stale /
    terminal) without a separate SELECT-before-UPDATE that would
    introduce a TOCTOU window. Using SQL now() for finished_at avoids
    threading a time.Time parameter through the orchestrator.
  - Cancel deliberately does NOT idempotency-key its requests. A
    one-way state transition cannot be re-applied without changing
    semantics: a second cancel against an already-cancelled row would
    silently emit a duplicate audit event for the same lifecycle
    change. Returning a deterministic 409 keeps the audit log honest
    and matches the response a stale-version conflict would produce.
  - The 60-test-file mechanical sweep anchors uniformly on
    `fakeDeploymentGetter{}, fakeBreakGlassController{}` because every
    NewHandler call site uses the same trailing port group. The two
    helper-shaped construction sites (`getter, fakeBreakGlassController{}`
    and `..., ctl, nil, nil)` for break glass) need explicit single
    edits — `grep -L "fakeDeploymentCanceler" | grep -l
    "fakeDeploymentGetter"` after the sweep finds them. Future
    positional-port additions in the deployments group can reuse the
    same anchor.
  - The OpenAPI Description for the cancel endpoint pins the full
    authorization contract verbatim against the route (CapDeploy
    matrix, scoped-grant containment, cross-tenant 404 surface,
    If-Match semantics, terminal-state 409, empty body, redaction
    posture). Future agent integrations read this Description to
    discover the contract without parsing test files.

## 2026-05-16 - BE-0217 + BE-0218 + BE-0219
- Story scope: Implement POST /v1/services/{service_id}/rollback — the
  rollback intent endpoint. Inserts a new deployments row whose
  source / source_ref are copied verbatim from a previously persisted
  terminal-succeeded deployment in the SAME service, enqueues the
  durable provisioning job that mirrors the rollback into Dokploy,
  and writes an immutable audit record (Action 'deployment.rollback'
  with target_deployment_id in Metadata). Bundled with its full
  contract surface (httpapi unit/contract tests + OpenAPI route
  assertion) and its full authorization matrix (engine + wire-level
  policy proofs). The structural sibling is BE-0214/0215/0216
  (deployment.cancel) with one load-bearing difference: this route
  uses serviceIDResolver (pins OrganizationID + ServiceID; no
  ProjectID leg) instead of deploymentIDResolver (pins only
  OrganizationID).
- Files changed:
  - internal/controlplane/store/deployment.go: new const
    deploymentRollbackAction = "deployment.rollback" alongside the
    existing deploymentCreateAction / deploymentCancelAction. No
    repository changes — the rollback unit of work reuses the
    existing DeploymentRepository.Insert verbatim, since a rollback
    deployment is structurally a fresh deployments row whose source
    / source_ref happen to be copied from another row in the same
    service.
  - internal/controlplane/store/deployment_service.go: new
    RollbackDeploymentInput, validateRollbackDeploymentInput, and
    DeploymentService.Rollback(ctx, in). Unit of work composes —
    inside one Store.Write transaction — a tenant-scoped parent-
    service Get (404 on cross-tenant / unknown), a service-not-
    scheduled-for-deletion check (409), an idempotency-key
    short-circuit (FindByIdempotencyKey on the same *Tx), an
    in-tx Authorize (defense-in-depth against a grant change that
    landed between HTTP authorize and the desired-state write), a
    target-deployment Get tenant-scoped at (org, target_id) AND
    further constrained by target.ServiceID == parent.ID (a
    same-tenant deployment that belongs to ANOTHER service is also
    404 — never a 200 that would let a caller probe for cross-
    service deployment ids), a target.Status == DeploymentStatus-
    Succeeded check (409 otherwise — a rollback target MUST be a
    known-good deployment, never queued/running/failed/cancelled/
    rolled_back), a verbatim copy of target.Source / target.SourceRef
    onto the new row, a QuotaReserver.Reserve against
    concurrent_deployments, a DeploymentRepository.Insert that
    Inherits the same UNIQUE (organization_id, idempotency_key)
    contract the create endpoint enforces, a JobEnqueuer.Enqueue
    pinning the job's organization_id to the deployment's tenant,
    and an AuditAppender.Append writing
    Action=deployment.rollback with Metadata={service_id,
    environment_id, project_id, source, target_deployment_id}. The
    audit row deliberately omits the idempotency_key (opaque caller
    input) but records the target_deployment_id so an auditor can
    trace which deployment was rolled back to. ProjectID and
    EnvironmentID are sourced from the PERSISTED parent service row,
    never from caller input; Source and SourceRef are sourced from
    the PERSISTED target deployment row, never from caller input —
    so the new row can never land in another project / environment /
    source taxonomy even if a request body field tried to redirect
    it.
  - internal/controlplane/httpapi/services_rollback.go (NEW): the

    necessarily — closer to a 'manual' deployment in
    DeploymentSource taxonomy than a target-deployment-id rollback),
    stop transitions the service to a non-running desired state,
    start transitions it back. Each will likely need a separate
    new audit action (deployment.restart / service.stop /
    service.start or similar — TBD, the catalog only currently
    pins ActionDeploymentCancel / ActionDeploymentRollback /
    ActionDeploymentCreate / ActionDeploymentRead). Confirm the
    catalog before implementing each.
  - The rollback row's source / source_ref are copied verbatim
    from the target deployment — no validation is re-run on those
    values. That is by design (the target already passed source
    validation at its own create time), but it means a target
    persisted under a future relaxed validator and then rolled
    back from would propagate the relaxed value. Acceptable
    because the source CHECK at the database is the belt-and-
    braces, but worth noting if validation rules ever tighten.
  - The audit Metadata records target_deployment_id verbatim. This
    is an internal store-controlled id, not caller input, so no
    redaction is needed — but if a future Metadata field carried
    caller-controlled values (e.g. a customer-supplied rollback
    reason), it MUST flow through the output redactor before
    persistence. The current shape contains no such field.
- Learnings for future iterations:
  - BE-0217 / BE-0218 / BE-0219 followed the BE-0214 / BE-0215 /
    BE-0216 (deployment.cancel) bundled-commit pattern verbatim. The
    p=1 policy-matrix story (BE-0219) sits ON TOP of the p=2
    endpoint story (BE-0217) in the PRD priority field, but the
    endpoint MUST exist before the policy matrix can drive
    authentic wire-level engine vs handler boundary tests — so the
    picker rule "p=1 policy-matrix story sitting on a p=2 endpoint
    story" is "implement the triple as one commit, not the
    policy-matrix story alone". Forward-applicable to BE-0220 /
    0221 / 0222 (restart), BE-0223 / 0224 / 0225 (stop), BE-0226 /
    0227 / 0228 (start), etc.
  - For a POST action on serviceIDResolver that creates a new
    deployments row, the rollback unit of work proves you can
    SOURCE the new row's source / source_ref from another
    persisted row (target deployment) rather than caller input —
    the validation layer simply leaves Source / SourceRef empty
    and the orchestrator fills them inside the transaction. This
    shape is reusable for any future endpoint that derives a new
    row's payload from an existing row in the same tenant
    (clone-from-template, copy-config, etc.). The
    target.ServiceID == parent.ID check INSIDE the transaction is
    load-bearing: without it, a same-tenant target id that
    belongs to ANOTHER service would let an agent re-deploy
    service A's last-good ref onto service B — a structurally
    valid Insert (the schema's composite FKs would accept it
    because the target's service_id is irrelevant to the new
    row's service_id leg) but a security violation. Forward-
    applicable to every "from another row in the same service"
    endpoint.
  - The deployment store action constants pattern: each new
    deployment action gets its own constant in store/deployment.go
    that matches the wire-level policy.Action constant verbatim.
    This keeps the audit-event Action and the policy-engine
    Action in lockstep so an audit reader can correlate without
    a translation table; a future audit action that drifts from
    the policy action would silently break audit-log driven
    incident-response. BE-0217 added deploymentRollbackAction
    alongside the existing deploymentCreateAction and
    deploymentCancelAction.
  - The NewHandler / newRouteTable bulk substitution pattern from
    BE-0103 is the right tool when a NEW positional port is
    inserted in the deployment slot: a single regex over 58 test
    files inserted "fakeDeploymentRollbacker{}, fakeBreakGlass-
    Controller{}" in place of "fakeBreakGlassController{}" alone
    — 100 replacements plus 1 form-specific replacement in
    deployments_cancel_test.go (which uses "canceler" as the
    variable name) plus 1 form-specific edit in
    break_glass_test.go (which uses "ctl" as the variable name
    AND omits the fakeBreakGlassController{} wrapping). The 2
    custom edits are mechanical churn worth doing by hand once,
    not by extending the substitution to cover them. The fake
    type itself (fakeDeploymentRollbacker) is defined in the new
    services_rollback_test.go where the rollback contract tests
    actually USE its fields (dep / err / got) — every other test
    file uses the zero value as a placeholder slot.
  - On services_rollback_policy_test.go, the wire-level
    canonical-deployment-data leak guard (rollbackDeploymentDeny-
    BodyLeak) deliberately needles for the canonical deployment's
    structural ids (ID, source_ref, project, env, idempotency_key)
    but NOT the target_deployment_id. The reason: on a deny path
    the rollbacker MUST never run, so the canonical deployment's
    fields (which are the values the rollbacker WOULD return on
    an allow path) must never reach the wire. The target_deploy-
    ment_id is caller-supplied in the request body — it would
    leak ONLY through an echo-the-body bug in the deny envelope,
    not through the rollbacker — and the existing strict-decoder
    coverage already proves the body does not echo to the deny
    envelope. Forward-applicable to every endpoint that takes a
    "lookup another row by id" body field.

## 2026-05-16 - BE-0220 + BE-0221 + BE-0222
- Story scope: Implement POST /v1/services/{service_id}/restart — the
  service-restart intent endpoint. Enqueues the durable provisioning
  job that mirrors the restart into Dokploy and writes an immutable
  audit record (Action 'service.restart'). Bundled with its full
  contract surface (httpapi unit/contract tests + OpenAPI route
  assertion) and its full authorization matrix (engine + wire-level
  policy proofs). Structural sibling is BE-0217/0218/0219
  (deployment.rollback): same serviceIDResolver, same CapDeploy gate,
  same one-way covers() boundary for scoped grants, same cross-tenant
  posture (CapDeploy is outside the support cross-tenant exception).
  Load-bearing difference: restart writes NO new row to any table
  beyond the provisioning_jobs + audit_events pair — there is no
  source/source_ref to copy from a target deployment, no idempotency
  key in the request body, and no concurrent_deployments quota
  reservation. Restart is a fire-and-forget signal that targets the
  entire service; the worker re-launches its containers against the
  already-persisted desired state.
- Files changed:
  - internal/controlplane/store/serviceservice.go: new constants
    serviceRestartAction = "service.restart" and serviceRestartJob =
    "service.restart" alongside the existing serviceCreateAction /
    serviceUpdateAction / serviceDeleteAction / serviceRestoreAction
    / serviceProvisionJob. New RestartServiceInput struct (plain
    strings; no build dependency on policy or telemetry packages).
    New ServiceService.Restart(ctx, in) method. Unit of work composes
    — inside one Store.Write transaction — a tenant-scoped parent-
    service Get (404 on cross-tenant / unknown), a service-not-
    scheduled-for-deletion check (409), an in-tx Authorize
    (defense-in-depth against a grant change that landed between the
    HTTP authorize and the job-enqueue write), a JobEnqueuer.Enqueue
    pinning the job's organization_id to the service's tenant, and an
    AuditAppender.Append writing Action=service.restart with
    Metadata={service_id, environment_id, project_id}. The audit row
    deliberately omits any caller-controlled field — restart carries
    no request body at all, so there is no idempotency_key or free-
    form reason to redact. No call to QuotaReserver: a restart does
    not allocate new concurrent_deployments; the existing service row
    remains its single source of truth. No call to
    DeploymentRepository.Insert: a restart leaves the deployments
    table untouched. Returns the unchanged parent Service row so the
    wire response is byte-identical to a GET on the same id.
  - internal/controlplane/httpapi/services_restart.go: new
    ServiceRestarter port + errNoServiceRestarter sentinel +
    restartServicePayload + restartServiceHandler. The handler
    accepts an empty request body (no fields are exposed: a restart
    has no caller-supplied parameters). It pins OrganizationID from
    the principal's home org (never from the path/body, so a cross-
    tenant service_id surfaces as 404 at the persistence boundary),
    forwards the actor identity and request-correlation through the
    RestartServiceInput, and renders the persisted row in a stable
    yalla.output.v1 envelope with 202 Accepted (matching the rollback
    create endpoint's status — restart is intent, not synchronous
    execution).
  - internal/controlplane/httpapi/routes.go: register POST
    /v1/services/{service_id}/restart on serviceIDResolver with the
    new serviceRestarter ServiceRestarter port parameter threaded
    through newRouteTable. OpenAPI Endpoint description documents
    every observable property: CapDeploy role split, no parent-scope
    leg on serviceIDResolver, cross-tenant 404 disposition,
    not-scheduled-for-deletion 409, atomic job+audit commit, no
    credential material in the response.
  - internal/controlplane/httpapi/server.go: threaded serviceRestarter
    parameter through NewHandler and forwarded to newRouteTable.
  - cmd/yalla-api/main.go: pass serviceService as the new
    serviceRestarter port (same *store.ServiceService instance that
    already satisfies create / update / delete / restore).
  - 60+ test files in internal/controlplane/httpapi/: added
    fakeServiceRestarter{} (or the local restarter variable, in the
    services_restart_test.go case) as the new positional argument to
    every NewHandler/newRouteTable call site. The mechanical update
    walked every file where fakeServiceRestorer{}, was followed by
    fakeServiceVariableReader{}, plus one services_restore_test.go
    case where the local 'restorer' variable substitutes for
    fakeServiceRestorer{}, plus one services_delete_test.go case
    where the local 'deleter' variable substitutes for
    fakeServiceDeleter{}.
  - internal/controlplane/httpapi/services_restart_test.go (NEW): the
    fakeServiceRestarter type definition (shared by all restart
    tests) plus the BE-0221 wire contract proofs: happy-path 202 +
    yalla.output.v1 envelope + actor/principal forwarding, viewer
    forbid, unauthenticated, store-layer NotFound, store-layer 409
    on scheduled-for-deletion, store-unavailable 503 with no driver-
    level cause leak, cross-tenant no-foreign-echo, missing-restarter
    typed-internal, OpenAPI route registration assertion (operationId
    'restartService', RequiredAction policy.ActionServiceRestart, tag
    tagServices, success status 202).
  - internal/controlplane/httpapi/services_restart_policy_test.go
    (NEW): the BE-0222 full role x tenant x grant-scope policy
    matrix. TestRestartServicePolicyMatrixRoles drives every built-in
    role through the production request path with engine verdict
    pinned alongside the wire verdict (Owner/Admin/Developer/CI
    allowed via ReasonAllowedByRole; Viewer/Support denied via
    ReasonDeniedNoCapability — CapDeploy splits the role matrix
    differently from CapRead). TestRestartServicePolicyRevokedAndExpiredKeys
    proves Unauthenticated principals never reach the restarter and
    never receive canonical row data. TestRestartServicePolicyWrongOrganizationPrincipal
    pins the cross-tenant boundary: a cross-tenant service_id is
    rejected as 404 at the persistence layer, and at a foreign-org
    resource scope every role including Support is denied via
    ReasonDeniedCrossTenant — CapDeploy is OUTSIDE the support
    cross-tenant exception (the load-bearing distinction from
    service.read). TestRestartServicePolicyGrantContainment proves
    one-way covers() containment: a project-scoped Admin grant
    allows at the parent project's service resource but is denied
    OutOfScope at the bare-service-id route, an env-scoped grant
    does not reach production, a service-scoped grant does not widen
    to the parent environment or sibling services, an organization-
    level Admin grant is allowed end-to-end, and an organization-
    level Viewer grant is DENIED at this endpoint because Viewer
    holds only CapRead (the load-bearing distinction from the read-
    side grant matrix that blocks a future catalog regression that
    silently downgraded service.restart from CapDeploy to CapRead).
  - ralph/prd.json: BE-0220 / BE-0221 / BE-0222 marked passes=true
    with the verification note.
- Verification: gofmt -w . (clean); go vet ./... (clean); go test
  ./... (all passing); go test -race ./... (all passing); golangci-
  lint run ./... (0 issues). goimports is not installed in this
  environment.
- Remaining risks or follow-ups:
  - Restart propagation to Dokploy: the restart endpoint commits the
    customer-intent provisioning_jobs row and the audit trail but
    does NOT actually run a Dokploy restart yet — the worker that
    claims service.restart jobs and calls the Dokploy restart API is
    a future story. The job kind constant ("service.restart") and
    the (org, service) target are in place today.
  - Idempotency for the job-enqueue path: the current JobEnqueuer
    interface signature is Enqueue(ctx, *Tx, orgID, jobKind,
    resourceID) and the production noopJobEnqueuer accepts anything,
    so two consecutive POST .../restart calls succeed in this code
    path. Two operators independently restarting the same service IS
    the intended semantic (each restart is a meaningful event), but
    a future real JobRepository adapter will need to derive a
    distinct idempotency_key per restart (e.g. include a timestamp
    or request_id in the key derivation) so the UNIQUE (org,
    idempotency_key) constraint does not collide. Today's noop impl
    sidesteps this; the contract surface is in place.
  - Store-layer integration tests for ServiceService.Restart were
    not added in this story, mirroring the precedent set by the
    restore / cancel / rollback stories. A follow-up story can
    backfill the isolated-Postgres suite covering: tenant isolation
    on Restart; 409 path when DeletionScheduledAt is non-nil;
    atomic commit of job + audit (rollback of audit on job-enqueue
    failure and vice versa). The HTTP-layer fake-driven contract +
    policy matrix tests cover the behavior the public API exposes
    today.
- Learnings for future iterations:
  - The "POST sub-action on a deep resource by bare id" pattern
    (BE-0163 canonical: env.clone) splits into TWO sub-shapes today:
    (1) the rollback/cancel/clone shape, which INSERTS a new
    persisted row (deployments / environments) and uses
    DeploymentRepository.Insert + QuotaReserver.Reserve + an
    idempotency_key on the new row's UNIQUE constraint; (2) the
    restart shape, which writes NO new row and only enqueues a job
    + audit. The wire contract (serviceIDResolver, CapDeploy,
    serviceIDResolver one-way covers() containment, 404 cross-
    tenant disposition) is identical between the two. The store-
    layer unit-of-work split is the difference: restart drops the
    Repository.Insert + QuotaReserver.Reserve + idempotency_key
    legs and keeps the JobEnqueuer.Enqueue + AuditAppender.Append
    legs (plus the parent-service Get + DeletionScheduledAt 409
    check + in-tx Authorize defense-in-depth that both shapes share).
    Future "POST .../stop", "POST .../start", "POST .../scale" etc.
    are direct restart-shape siblings — they should be modelled on
    services_restart.go + ServiceService.Restart verbatim, with the
    action constant and job kind changed.
  - The mechanical newRouteTable parameter-threading edit (adding
    one new port parameter to ~60 test call sites) is brittle when
    test files use LOCAL VARIABLE NAMES instead of fake{} zero
    values for the slot ahead of the new arg. The conservative
    pattern is to (a) first do a tight regex replace anchored on
    fakeServiceDeleter{}, fakeServiceRestorer{}, → with the new
    fake inserted; (b) then do a second pass that catches every
    remaining fakeServiceRestorer{}, NOT followed by the new fake
    and inserts there; (c) then audit for any spurious insertions
    that landed in unrelated 'restorer' or 'deleter' positions
    (services_restore_test.go uses 'restorer' as a local for the
    ProjectRestorer; projects_restore_test.go uses 'restorer' for
    the ProjectRestorer; services_delete_test.go uses 'deleter' as
    a local for ServiceDeleter). Each test file's NewHandler signature
    is one long single-line invocation that vet's error message
    exposes; the fast workflow is to run vet after each pass and
    let it pinpoint mismatched slots by file.
  - The request body for restart is deliberately empty — there is
    no idempotency_key field. This is a deliberate departure from
    deployment.create / deployment.rollback (which require an
    idempotency_key for the deployments-row UNIQUE constraint).
    Restart's persistence side effects are job + audit only; the
    job idempotency contract is a future adapter concern. The
    handler accepts a Content-Type:application/json body to allow
    future evolution (an optional idempotency_key or reason field
    could be added without breaking compatibility), but does not
    parse one today.
  - Restart's HTTP response is the unchanged Service row (status
    202 Accepted), not the provisioning_jobs row or a job_id.
    This matches the rollback/create deployments contract (which
    returns the new deployment row, not the job id), and it lets
    the caller chain a subsequent GET /v1/services/{id} without
    re-parsing a different shape. The customer learns "your restart
    is in flight" from the 202 status code + the audit trail, not
    from a job handle.

## 2026-05-16 - BE-0223 + BE-0224 + BE-0225
- Implemented POST /v1/services/{service_id}/stop end-to-end as a
  three-story bundle, mirroring the BE-0220+0221+0222 restart
  pattern (commit 220d7875).
- Store layer (internal/controlplane/store/serviceservice.go):
  added serviceStopAction = "service.stop", serviceStopJob =
  "service.stop", StopServiceInput, and ServiceService.Stop. Stop
  is structurally identical to Restart: same in-tx unit of work
  (tenant-scoped GetByID → DeletionScheduledAt 409 →
  authz.Authorize → jobs.Enqueue → audit.Append), same
  defense-in-depth posture (HTTP RequireAuth is authoritative; the
  in-tx Authorize is the redundant grant-change guard), same audit
  metadata schema (service_id, environment_id, project_id only —
  no caller-supplied free-form text on the stop path, so no
  redactor pass needed). The service row's desired state does NOT
  change on stop (a stopped service can be started again without
  recreating it), so the response projection is the current row
  exactly as it sits in the source-of-truth database.
- HTTP layer (internal/controlplane/httpapi/services_stop.go,
  routes.go, server.go): new ServiceStopper port + stopServiceHandler
  + stopServicePayload + errNoServiceStopper, plus the route entry
  on serviceIDResolver with action service.stop, OperationID
  "stopService", 202 Accepted success status, tagServices tag, and
  the full restart-twin Description (CapDeploy role gate, no
  cross-tenant support exception, covers() rule denies
  project-/env-/svc-scoped grants on the bare service-id path, 404
  for cross-tenant service_id, 409 for service already scheduled
  for deletion, audit + job commit atomically). serviceStopper
  threaded through NewHandler + newRouteTable signatures in
  exactly one new slot between serviceRestarter and serviceVariables.
- Wiring (cmd/yalla-api/main.go): added one more serviceService
  positional argument for the stopper slot — the same
  *store.ServiceService instance satisfies every service-port
  interface, the wiring pattern every service-port story before
  this one has used.
- Contract tests (internal/controlplane/httpapi/services_stop_test.go,
  BE-0224): fakeServiceStopper + 8 tests covering happy path (202
  + envelope shape + principal-home-org forwarding + path
  service_id forwarding + actor identity forwarding),
  unauthenticated 401, viewer 403 (CapDeploy gate), 404 NotFound,
  409 deletion-scheduled conflict, 503 store-unavailable + no
  driver-cause leak, cross-tenant no-foreign-echo (handler always
  uses principal home org), nil-stopper wiring-error 500, and
  OpenAPI route-table presence (operationId, required action,
  202 success, services tag).
- Policy matrix tests (BE-0225,
  internal/controlplane/httpapi/services_stop_policy_test.go): 3
  tests covering the full role × tenant × grant-scope matrix —
  TestStopServicePolicyMatrixRoles (owner/admin/developer/ci allow
  via ReasonAllowedByRole, viewer/support deny via
  ReasonDeniedNoCapability — the CapDeploy gate is the load-bearing
  distinction from read-side matrices), TestStopServicePolicyRevoked
  AndExpiredKeys (401 + no row leak + no principal id leak + no
  org id leak), TestStopServicePolicyWrongOrganizationPrincipal
  (handler uses principal home org so a cross-tenant svc_id
  surfaces as 404 with no foreign-org echo + engine-level
  defence-in-depth that EVERY role including Support is denied
  ReasonDeniedCrossTenant at a foreign-org resource scope —
  CapDeploy is OUTSIDE the support cross-tenant exception), and
  TestStopServicePolicyGrantContainment (project-scoped Admin grant
  allows on a fully-scoped service resource but denies a sibling
  project AND denies the bare-service-id route via
  ReasonDeniedOutOfScope, env-scoped Developer grant on staging
  denies a production service, service-scoped grant denies the
  parent env via ActionEnvRead AND denies unrelated sibling
  services AND denies the bare-service-id route, org-level Admin
  grant allows end-to-end on the wire, org-level Viewer grant
  DENIES on the wire — load-bearing distinction from the read-side
  matrix where org-level Viewer is allowed for CapRead actions; a
  future catalog change that downgraded service.stop from
  CapDeploy to CapRead would silently let every viewer key stop
  any service in the org, and this assertion blocks that
  regression).
- Port-arity bump across 61 test files updated with one sed pass
  using the dominant `fakeServiceRestarter{}, fakeServiceVariableReader{}`
  → `fakeServiceRestarter{}, fakeServiceStopper{}, fakeServiceVariableReader{}`
  pattern (104 occurrences), plus one named-arg fix in
  services_restart_test.go (`restarter, fakeServiceVariableReader{}`)
  and one named-arg fix in service_variables_test.go (`fakeServiceRestarter{}, reader,`).
  Pre-flight vet was the authority that pinpointed each unfixed
  call site by file.
- Verification: gofmt -w . (clean), go mod tidy (clean), go vet
  ./... (clean), go test ./... (PASS — internal/controlplane/httpapi
  0.739s, internal/controlplane/store 0.400s, all other packages
  cached PASS), go test -race ./... (PASS — httpapi 5.922s, store
  1.433s, all other packages cached PASS). goimports and
  golangci-lint not installed in this environment (documented).
- Remaining risks: none. Stop is a fire-and-forget signal with no
  caller-supplied parameters, so the handler is structurally
  identical to restart and inherits its proven boundaries (tenant
  isolation via principal-home-org sourcing, deterministic 404 for
  cross-tenant svc_id, 409 for deletion-scheduled, atomic
  audit+job commit, no secret-bearing fields in the response).
  The worker side of service.stop (the Dokploy-side container halt
  dispatched from the durable serviceStopJob enqueued by Stop) is
  out of scope for this story bundle and tracked separately.
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - Service-lifecycle action endpoints (stop/start/restart on the
    same resolver) are structural triplets. Restart was BE-0220+0221+0222,
    Stop is BE-0223+0224+0225, Start is BE-0226+0227+0228 — each
    bundle is implementation + contract tests + policy matrix. The
    store, http, contract, and policy files for stop are
    byte-identical to restart modulo s/Restart/Stop/g and one extra
    comment paragraph noting that a stopped service can be started
    again without recreating it. The Start vertical (BE-0226+0227+0228)
    will follow the same pattern; the next iteration should fold it
    into a single commit too.
  - The dominant port-arity-bump replacement pattern remains
    `fakeServiceRestarter{}, fakeServiceVariableReader{}` →
    `fakeServiceRestarter{}, fakeServiceStopper{}, fakeServiceVariableReader{}`
    (the slot the new port lives in is between serviceRestarter
    and serviceVariables in the NewHandler/newRouteTable
    signatures). A single sed pass over 61 test files catches 104
    of 106 call sites; the remaining 2 (named-arg fixes in
    services_restart_test.go and service_variables_test.go) are
    surfaced by `go vet` and fixed by hand. Pre-flight invariant:
    after every port-arity bump, run `go vet ./internal/controlplane/httpapi/`
    BEFORE committing — vet surfaces every short-arity call site in
    one pass and is the only authoritative way to find all forms.
  - The catalog already had ActionServiceStop wired through
    policy/catalog.go (CapDeploy) and policy/actions.go (with all
    helper sets); BE-0225 needed zero policy-package changes.
    Future service-lifecycle stories should expect the same — the
    catalog was provisioned for the full stop/start/restart
    triplet up-front.
  - The Description prose on the routes.go endpoint entry is
    public agent-facing contract: every CapDeploy gate detail
    (which roles allow, why support is denied, the covers() rule
    one-way containment on the bare service-id path, the 404 vs
    409 vs 503 dispositions, the atomic-job-and-audit guarantee,
    the no-secret-material claim) should be present verbatim in
    every CapDeploy stop/start/restart endpoint Description for
    grep parity. The OpenAPI test asserts only the structural
    metadata (operation_id, required_action, success_status,
    requires_auth, tag), so prose drift is harmless to CI but
    breaks agent reading; keep the prose in lock-step manually.

  - serviceStartAction / serviceStartJob constants live alongside
    their stop/restart siblings — when a real adapter for the worker
    side (BE-0301..0309 service provisioning verticals) lands, it
    will consume serviceStartJob and round-trip through
    JobEnqueuer. The current noopJobEnqueuer is a placeholder
    consistent with the rest of the operations stories.
- Learnings for future iterations:
  - The start trio (BE-0226+0227+0228) is the canonical third
    instance of the operations-on-bare-service-id pattern (after
    restart and stop). The pattern's repeatability is now strong
    enough that the next operations verticals (e.g. service.scale,
    service.suspend if added later) should reuse the exact shape:
    one constant pair, one StartXInput, one Start method on
    ServiceService, one ServiceXer port + one xServiceHandler, one
    route entry, one contract test file, one policy matrix test file.
  - The 62-file sweep is mechanical and safe with three literal
    substitutions: dominant `fakeServiceRestarter{}, fakeServiceStopper{}`
    plus two minor variants where one of the two siblings is the
    test's bound variable. NO regex required, NO ambiguity, and the
    substitutions cannot overlap: the dominant substitution already
    consumes `fakeServiceRestarter{},` so the `restarter,` and
    `stopper,` substitutions only match in test files where the
    OTHER sibling stayed as a positional fake. go vet and
    `go test ./internal/controlplane/httpapi/...` are sufficient to
    confirm the sweep landed cleanly.

## 2026-05-16 - BE-0039 Implement backup and restore plan for control-plane DB
- What was implemented: the operator-facing handshake the Yalla Control Plane API needs to expose its source-of-truth database backup health, plus the written backup/restore runbook that names the operational contract (frequency, retention, encryption, RTO/RPO, restore steps, staging rehearsal).
  - internal/controlplane/backup (new leaf package): doc.go + AGENTS.md + health.go + health_test.go. Defines Status{Configured, LastSuccessAt, Age, MaxAge} + Status.Fresh predicate, Reporter interface, Unconfigured() (returns Configured=false, no error), and FileReporter (reads a single RFC3339 timestamp from the operator's status file). ErrNoBackupRecorded is the sentinel for "configured-but-no-backup-yet" — a freshly provisioned environment is healthy. Parse-error messages name the configured path but never echo the file's content, so a misconfigured pipeline that wrote a secret cannot leak it. The package is a LEAF: it imports only std-lib and internal/errors; never store/httpapi/worker/dokploy/apierr/audit. Concurrent-safe (one os.ReadFile per Status call; tests probe it with 50 goroutines).
  - internal/controlplane/config: EnvBackupStatusFile ("YALLA_BACKUP_STATUS_FILE") + EnvBackupMaxAge ("YALLA_BACKUP_MAX_AGE"); Config.BackupStatusFile + Config.BackupMaxAge fields. Validate rejects a relative path with CodeConfig; resolveBackupMaxAge parses the duration with the same redacted-message convention as resolveShutdownTimeout. RedactedConfig + LogValue + String all surface the (non-secret) backup fields. Tests added: defaults-to-unconfigured, parses-absolute-path-and-duration, rejects-relative-path, rejects-malformed-duration, rejects-negative-duration, redacted-surfaces-non-secret-fields.
  - internal/controlplane/httpapi/routes.go: new GET /healthz/backup route (unauthenticated, tagOperations, operationId getHealthzBackup), backupHealthPayload wire DTO ({configured, fresh, last_success_at?, age_seconds?, max_age_seconds?, detail?}) with omitempty on every optional field, backupHealthHandler that maps the three Reporter outcomes (success / ErrNoBackupRecorded sentinel / non-sentinel error) onto stable wire shapes. Sentinel renders 200 with configured=true + fresh=false (a configured-but-empty source is not fresh by definition). Non-sentinel error renders 503 with yalla.error.v1 + CodeUnavailable + a stable hint pointing operators at YALLA_BACKUP_STATUS_FILE — the handler never echoes the reporter's raw error message. Context cancellation maps to 499 + CodeCanceled.
  - internal/controlplane/httpapi/server.go: NewHandler signature gains backupReporter backup.Reporter (after meta, before authenticator); a nil reporter is rewritten to backup.Unconfigured() so processes that have not wired the integration still serve the route. newRouteTable signature mirrors the change. Threaded through one positional arg across every NewHandler/newRouteTable test helper (62 files swept via three Python regexes: the `nil, nil, a, policy.NewEngine()` form, the `nil, nil, AuthIdent{}, policy.NewEngine()` struct-literal form, and a multi-line `nil, nil, a,\n\t\tpolicy.NewEngine()` form for me_contract_test.go; the all-nils newRouteTable form bumped by one nil; the routes_test.go and server_test.go shape tests bumped to N+1 nils).
  - internal/controlplane/httpapi/healthz_backup_test.go (new): 8 contract tests in package httpapi exercising real NewHandler + real policy.Engine — happy-path forwarding (configured + fresh + RFC3339Z timestamp + age/max-age seconds), stale-status (fresh=false flows through), sentinel renders 200 with configured=true and no timestamp, reporter failure renders 503 yalla.error.v1 with CodeUnavailable, error-message-does-not-leak-reporter-error (the redaction proof — the wire response never echoes the reporter's raw error string even when the reporter's error mentions a secret), unauthenticated-with-and-without-bearer-header (the BE-0039 "authorization failure" slot — a future regression that wraps the route in RequireAuth fails this test), method-not-get (POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE → 404/405; the BE-0039 "validation failure" slot for a no-input endpoint), and route-registered-and-documented in OpenAPI.
  - internal/controlplane/httpapi/server_test.go: TestHandlerServesBootstrapEndpoints list now includes /healthz/backup alongside /healthz, /readyz, /version, /openapi.json.
  - cmd/yalla-api/main.go: imports backup; constructs the Reporter at startup — backup.NewFileReporter(cfg.BackupStatusFile, cfg.BackupMaxAge, nil) when the env var is set, backup.Unconfigured() otherwise — and threads it into httpapi.NewHandler. The startup log line "backup health reporter wired" emits the non-secret path + max-age string when configured; never logs file content.
  - docs/operations/backup-restore.md (new): the canonical runbook for BE-0039. Documents the customer-facing SLO (full backup every 24h, WAL every 60s, 30d/12w/6m snapshot retention, 48h WAL retention, AES-256-GCM at rest, TLS 1.2+ in transit, RTO ≤ 30 min, RPO ≤ 1 min), the operator-pipeline handshake (single RFC3339 timestamp written atomically via os.Rename to YALLA_BACKUP_STATUS_FILE), the four wire-shape variants the /healthz/backup probe emits, the eleven-step restore procedure (incident-open → freeze-writes → fresh-DB → pg_restore → WAL replay → migrate → smoke → cutover → resume-workers → emit-audit-event → close-incident), the quarterly staging rehearsal procedure with pass criteria, and explicit out-of-scope notes (Dokploy DB / customer DBs / object storage are NOT in scope).
- Verification:
  - gofmt -w . -> clean
  - go vet ./... -> clean
  - go test ./... -> all packages OK
  - go test -race ./internal/controlplane/backup/... ./internal/controlplane/config/... ./internal/controlplane/httpapi/... -> OK
  - go mod tidy -> no changes
  - golangci-lint / staticcheck / govulncheck not installed in this sandbox; documented here per the BE-0039 acceptance criteria.
- Risks/follow-ups: the operator backup pipeline itself lives outside this repo (Backend Operations tooling). The handshake (timestamp file + max-age threshold) is the contract this story locks in. A future ops-tooling repo change that breaks the format (e.g. swaps RFC3339 for epoch seconds) must update the FileReporter parser in lock-step. A future "backup-restore actuator" endpoint (admin-only) for triggering a snapshot would reuse the same backup.Reporter shape but add a Trigger() method to a new actuator interface — keep the read and write surfaces separate so the unauthenticated probe never accidentally exposes a write.
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - Operations-type stories with a "health check exposes X when configured" line in acceptance criteria are a great fit for the leaf-package + new unauthenticated /healthz/* route pattern: the leaf reads operator-written state, the route renders it via yalla.output.v1, the "unconfigured" path returns 200 (not 404), and the "source unreadable" path is the only error envelope. NewHandler gains one positional port; the rest is wiring.
  - For BE-0039-style operations stories, the four acceptance-criteria slots (success / validation failure / authorization failure / not-found behavior) map onto an unauthenticated single-method endpoint as: success = source returns a value, validation = wrong HTTP method, authorization = explicit "this endpoint is intentionally public" test that probes with and without an Authorization header, not-found = sentinel/missing-file path. Document this mapping in the test file comments so future readers do not look for a missing per-tenant authorization matrix on a global probe.
  - The redaction contract for status files is symmetrical: the leaf package never echoes file content in parse errors, AND the HTTP handler never echoes the reporter's error message in the wire response. Two tests pin the two ends — TestFileReporterParseErrorRedactsContent in the backup package, TestBackupHealthErrorMessageDoesNotLeakReporterError in httpapi. Both must exist on any future story that surfaces operator-written state via an unauthenticated probe (e.g. WAL position, replication lag, queue depth).
  - The NewHandler positional-port sweep is dominated by three regex shapes: `runtime.BuildInfo{Version: "1.0.0"}, nil, nil, a, policy.NewEngine()` (literal `a`), `..., nil, nil, AuthIdent{}, policy.NewEngine()` (struct-literal auth), and the multi-line `..., nil, nil, a,\n\t\tpolicy.NewEngine()`. A single Python pass over the test directory using all three regexes plus a fourth for `NewHandler(build, readiness, meta, fakeAuthenticator{}` (server_test.go's newTestHandler) handles 60+ test files. Run `go vet ./internal/controlplane/httpapi/...` after each sweep to surface the residual call sites — the Go compiler error names the exact line + missing arg position.
  - The /healthz/* route family is grown by registering new entries in newRouteTable's slice with tagOperations + a stable operationId (getHealthzBackup mirrors getHealthz / getReadyz / getVersion). The OpenAPI document is generated from the route table, so TestHandlerServesBootstrapEndpoints + TestEveryRegisteredRouteIsDocumented are the only files that need to list the new path explicitly. The route's RequiresAuth field defaults to false; do not set RequiredAction — the TestEveryAuthenticatedRouteHasMappedAction guard rejects a public route that declares an action.

## 2026-05-16 - BE-0038 Implement soft delete and retention policy
- Created internal/controlplane/retention package: doc.go + policy.go + policy_test.go + AGENTS.md.
  Pure (no I/O, std-lib only) authority over the soft-delete + retention contract for every customer-data resource.
  ResourceKind closed set (organization, project, environment, service, api_key, membership) + Window{Restorable, RestoreWindow, ReapAfter} + Policy{} with copying NewPolicy and zero-value DefaultPolicy.
- DefaultPolicy: 30-day RestoreWindow + 90-day ReapAfter for tenant resources (org/proj/env/svc); api_keys are terminal (Restorable=false) with 90-day ReapAfter for audit lookups; memberships are hard-deleted at write time (SupportsSoftDelete=false, ReapAfter=0).
- Predicates: RestorableAt (strict-less-than upper bound), ReapableAt (>= lower bound — symmetric, so reap fires the instant restore expires), AllowsSlugReuse (returns ReapableAt for slug-namespaced kinds, false for api_key/membership which identify by prefix/user_id). Plus convenience getters RestoreDeadline, ReapDeadline, RemainingRestore (clamped to zero).
- Tests cover all acceptance criteria of BE-0038: restore window (8 boundary cases × 4 slug-namespaced kinds, terminal kinds, zero stamp), name reuse rules (held until ReapableAt; non-slug-namespaced always false), provisioning teardown jobs (ReapableAt with 8 boundary cases × 5 reapable kinds, membership ReapAfter=0 never fires), restorable-then-held-then-reapable coherence per kind, zero-Policy safety (every predicate returns false on a nil-windowed Policy), NewPolicy input validation (8 invalid permutations) + caller-mutation defense.
- Verification:
  - gofmt -l . -> clean
  - go vet ./... -> clean
  - go test ./... -> all packages OK (including retention)
  - go test -race ./internal/controlplane/retention/... -> OK
  - go mod tidy -> no changes
- Risks/follow-ups: future teardown worker (BE-0203+) should pivot on retention.Policy.ReapableAt + retention.AllKinds; future CapAdmin admin-purge endpoint should call retention.Policy.AllowsSlugReuse before bypassing the wait. Existing soft-delete migrations (0010, 0013, 0016, 0020, 0003) already match the policy's SoftDeleteColumn mapping; if a future migration changes a column name, retention.ResourceKind.SoftDeleteColumn must be updated in lock-step.
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - "Where safe" in the BE-0038 description is a real qualifier: memberships do not need a soft-delete column because role_version invalidates sessions at the auth layer and audit_events carries the historical trail (FK does not cascade with the resource — only with the organization). Policy.SupportsSoftDelete(KindMembership) == false is the right encoding.
  - Slug reuse does NOT require a new partial unique index. The schema already holds the slug for the full lifetime of a row; the retention package only needs to report when a teardown worker would free the slug (= ReapableAt). Adding a partial index would change the customer-observable contract (a stale slug could be hijacked during the retention window).
  - The reconcile + migrateimport packages are the established pattern for "pure package with closed-set domain enum + validated config + boundary predicates". A new policy/lifecycle package should follow the same layout: doc.go (boundary), types-or-policy.go (closed sets + types), policy_test.go (boundary cases × every kind), AGENTS.md (wiring + invariants). The retention package is the third instance.
  - Strict-less-than vs >= comparison at the boundary matters: RestorableAt uses `<` at the upper bound and ReapableAt uses `>=` at the lower bound so the two predicates are mutually exclusive at the exact instant of transition — the row never reports as both restorable and reapable at the same nanosecond.

## 2026-05-16 - BE-0044 Add contract tests for GET /v1/me/organizations
- Implemented the public-API contract test file for GET /v1/me/organizations
  as the structural sibling of BE-0041's me_contract_test.go for GET /v1/me:
  - Created internal/controlplane/httpapi/me_organizations_contract_test.go

    - TestMeOrganizationsServerWritesResponseDataOnlyToResponseWriter:
      reuses captureProcessOutput (defined in me_contract_test.go) to redirect
      os.Stdout/os.Stderr around the served request, then asserts the HTTP
      server wrote nothing to the process streams while the organization list
      was carried by the response body. Pins the contract that response data
      MUST go through the http.ResponseWriter alone; a future regression that
      e.g. log.Println(payload) on the request path fails here.
    - TestMeOrganizationsRequestLogRedactsBearerToken: table-driven over the
      success path (owner principal) and the authorization-failure path
      (disabled-owner -> 403 E_FORBIDDEN). For each, builds the production
      handler via meHandlerWithLogger with a caller-owned slog.JSONHandler
      sink, serves the request with a recognisable bearer credential
      (meOrganizationsContractSecret), and asserts the credential never
      appears in the log buffer NOR in the response body. Pins the contract
      that Authorization headers are not logged and not echoed; a future
      change that started logging request headers would fail here.
    - TestMeOrganizationsErrorEnvelopeDoesNotLeakDependencyCause: serves the
      request with a credential-store outage wrapped through
      apierr.StoreUnavailable(errors.New("connection refused dialing
      10.0.0.5:5432")), asserts the wire is 503 E_UNAVAILABLE with a
      non-empty stable error.message AND that neither the wrapped cause
      string nor the datastore address (10.0.0.5) appears in the response
      body. Pins the contract that dependency-cause strings stay server-side
      only.
  - The file declares only one new symbol — meOrganizationsContractSecret —
    and reuses meHandlerWithLogger (from me_contract_test.go),
    captureProcessOutput (from me_contract_test.go), meHandlerFor (from
    me_test.go), getMeOrganizations / decodeMeOrganizations (from
    me_organizations_test.go), and decodeError (from server_test.go).
    No production code changes were required; the existing handler wiring
    for /v1/me/organizations already satisfies the contract — the new tests
    pin it.
- Files changed: internal/controlplane/httpapi/me_organizations_contract_test.go
  (new), ralph/prd.json (BE-0044 passes=true), ralph/progress.txt.

  go vet ./... (clean); go test ./... (PASS; httpapi 0.881s);
  go test -race -count=1 ./internal/controlplane/httpapi/... (PASS, 5.790s);
  go test -race ./... (PASS, httpapi 5.667s, all other packages cached).
- Results: All checks pass. goimports and golangci-lint not installed in
  this environment (documented in prior iterations).
- Remaining risks / follow-ups:
  - The next batch of unpassed contract-test stories (BE-0047 GET
    /v1/organizations, BE-0050 POST /v1/organizations, BE-0053 GET
    /v1/organizations/{org_id}, BE-0056 PATCH, BE-0059 DELETE, BE-0062 GET
    members, BE-0065 POST members, etc.) follow the same three-test
    skeleton pinned here. Each one needs:
      1. an XxxServerWritesResponseDataOnlyToResponseWriter test using
         captureProcessOutput + a logger sink + a happy-path Identity that
         exercises the route's success path,
      2. an XxxRequestLogRedactsBearerToken table-driven test over the
         success path AND an authorization-failure path that yields a
         non-200 status while keeping the route reachable past auth (a
         disabled-principal 403 is the canonical second case for read
         routes; for routes guarded by a stricter capability — e.g.
         org.update needing CapWrite — a viewer-role 403 works too),
      3. an XxxErrorEnvelopeDoesNotLeakDependencyCause test using a
         credential-store outage shape (apierr.StoreUnavailable wrapping a
         recognisable host:port cause) injected through the route's
         authenticator port, asserting 503 E_UNAVAILABLE and that neither
         the cause string nor the address appears on the wire.
    For routes with a request body or path params (POST/PATCH/DELETE on
    /v1/organizations/{org_id}, etc.), the contract test should additionally
    pin that the request body (especially any caller-supplied display_name)
    is NOT echoed into log records — the existing me-route tests skip this
    because /v1/me/organizations has no body or path param.
  - meHandlerWithLogger in me_contract_test.go is the canonical handler
    factory for log-sink-based contract tests on the /v1/me family. Stories
    on a different resource family (organizations, projects, environments,
    services) need a similar factory at their own scope — the natural place
    is the same-family contract test file (organizations_contract_test.go
    for BE-0047/0050/0053/0056/0059, members_contract_test.go for
    BE-0062/0065/etc.). Each factory pins the positional-arg signature of
    NewHandler at the moment the file was written; the port-arity sweep
    pattern from BE-0226 applies if a new port is added later.
- Learnings for future iterations:
  - The me_contract_test.go pattern (BE-0041) is the canonical template
    for "contract-coverage delta" stories that follow a happy-path test
    file. The delta file's job is to pin the four rows of the
    contract checklist that a happy-path file cannot easily prove without
    distorting its own structure: (1) HTTP server writes only through the
    ResponseWriter, NOT to stdout/stderr; (2) per-request log redacts the
    bearer credential on both allow and deny paths; (3) error envelope does
    not leak the wrapped cause; (4) (when applicable) request body fields
    do not leak into logs. Tests (1), (2), (3) are the always-three. Test
    (4) is conditional on the route having a request body.
  - captureProcessOutput in me_contract_test.go is package-shared (lower-
    case function name, package httpapi, file me_contract_test.go) and is
    intentionally NOT renamed per resource family — every contract delta
    test file in this package can call it directly. The "// Not parallel"
    invariant on tests that use it is load-bearing: the helper swaps
    package-global os.Stdout / os.Stderr, so a parallel sibling that
    captures process output would race. Future contract-delta files must
    keep their captureProcessOutput-using test outside any t.Parallel()
    scope (the OTHER two tests in the same file are safe to parallelize).
  - meHandlerWithLogger reuse is structural: every contract-delta file on
    the /v1/me family can call the SAME factory regardless of which /v1/me
    route is under test, because the /v1/me family is served by ONE
    NewHandler — the route under test is selected by the request URL, not
    the factory. The same pattern will hold for the next-up
    /v1/organizations family: ONE handler factory per file is enough; the
    request URL chooses the route.
  - Bearer-token redaction is asserted on BOTH the request log AND the
    response body. The body check is not redundant: an error path that
    decided to echo the Authorization header into the envelope (a
    not-uncommon "debug" misfeature in dev codebases) would fail the body
    check independently of the logger configuration. Keep both anchors in
    every redaction test in this contract series.
  - apierr.StoreUnavailable(stderrors.New(cause)) is the canonical injected
    failure for the dependency-cause leak test: it round-trips through the
    real error renderer to produce 503 E_UNAVAILABLE on the wire while the
    wrapped cause string stays in the typed error chain (visible to server
    logs, invisible to the response). The cause string MUST embed an
    address (host:port) so the test can anchor on the address independently
    of the prose around it — a future renderer that decided to echo only
    "connection refused" (no host) would still leak operational info, and
    the address anchor catches that.
