    iteration sees this is a known scope boundary, not an oversight.
  - The Rollback path is NOT covered by a dedicated concurrent test
    because the test cost (seed a parent service + a previously
    persisted successful deployment per goroutine) would dwarf the
    Create coverage's value-per-line and the unit-of-work code path
    is byte-identical (same `svc.quota.Reserve(ctx, tx, orgID,
    string(QuotaResourceMonthlyDeployments))` line in both methods).
    The Create concurrent test is the load-bearing assertion; the
    Rollback story should be added if a regression ever decoupled the
    two paths.
  - Pre-existing failures NOT introduced by BE-0335: when
    YALLA_TEST_DATABASE_URL is set and the full store suite runs
    against a real Postgres, the four environment-related tests
    documented in BE-0331/BE-0332/BE-0333/BE-0334 progress entries
    (TestEnvironmentServiceCreate* drift, the
    TestEnvironmentRepoListByProjectReturnsDeterministicOrdering
    timing flakiness, and the
    TestServiceVariableServiceReplaceInvalidInputNeverOpensTransaction
    fixture issue) still surface — unchanged by this story.
- **Learnings for future iterations:**
  - When a quota dimension's constant + DOMAIN membership + closed-set
    guard already exist (from an earlier baseline migration or an
    earlier "add the constant + membership map ahead of the call
    site" story), the call-site story does NOT need a new migration.
    Check `grep -rn '"<dimension>"' migrate/migrations/` and
    `grep 'QuotaResource<X>' internal/controlplane/store/quota.go`
    BEFORE writing a new migration — duplicating ALTER DOMAIN against
    a value already in the CHECK constraint will fail the migration.
    The BE-0334 backup_schedules story DID need a migration because
    the constant was added but the DOMAIN was not widened; BE-0335 did
    NOT because BOTH were already in place from migration 0006.
  - When a Create unit of work reserves multiple quota dimensions in
    series, the ORDER matters for the rejection-message-first
    experience. The convention pinned in deployment_service.go's doc
    comments: reserve the NARROWER-TEMPORAL-WINDOW dimension first
    (concurrent_deployments, in-flight TTL-bound) and the BROADER
    dimension second (monthly_deployments, billing-period). A tenant
    that exhausts both at once observes the rejection on the dimension
    whose remediation is the FASTER ("wait for in-flight jobs" beats
    "wait for next billing period").
  - A "dimension is independent of sibling dimension" assertion does
    NOT require seeding a policy for the sibling and then asserting no
    rejection from it. The structurally stronger assertion is to seed
    NO policy for the sibling — then the Checker's "no policy => allow
    without recording a reservation" branch fires, and the assertion
    becomes "active <sibling> reservations = 0 after the run". This
    is the assertion the BE-0335 concurrent test added for
    concurrent_deployments specifically: if a future regression
    accidentally inserted a reservation despite the absence of a
    policy, the count would drift above 0 and the test would fail
    even though no per-attempt rejection would have surfaced.
  - DeploymentSourceManual is the canonical "no-real-ref" source for
    quota concurrent tests on DeploymentService. The validator accepts
    a short label or an empty string for it; using
    DeploymentSourceGit would require a valid branch / SHA per
    goroutine and DeploymentSourceImage would require a valid image
    ref — both pull the test focus off the quota boundary into ref
    validation. The pattern: use the source whose validator is the
    most permissive for the field under test, NOT the most "realistic"
    source.
---

    backup_schedules / monthly_deployments). The Reserve call sites

    AuditRepository.Append). The constant QuotaResourceConcurrentDeployments
    and its DOMAIN membership were ALREADY in migration
    0006_quota_policy_schema.up.sql plus internal/controlplane/store/quota.go,
    quota_internal_test.go's TestQuotaResourceValid valid slice, and
    quota_schema_test.go. So this story is a pure CONCURRENT-TEST
    clone of the BE-0335 monthly_deployments template, NOT a domain
    widening, NOT a migration, NOT a call-site addition: the entire
    delivery is one new _test.go file.
  - Added internal/controlplane/store/deployment_quota_concurrent_deployments_concurrent_test.go
    with two tests structurally cloned from
    deployment_quota_monthly_deployments_concurrent_test.go:
    * TestDeploymentServiceCreateRejectsParallelOversubscriptionForConcurrentDeploymentsQuota
      seeds a concurrent_deployments plan policy at limit=5, leaves
      monthly_deployments INTENTIONALLY unpoliced (so the Checker's
      "no policy => allow without recording" branch fires for it),
      pre-seeds the concurrent_deployments quota_usage counter row,
      then races 20 goroutines through DeploymentService.Create.
      Asserts: exactly 5 successes / 15 rejections; every rejection
      is yerr.CodeQuotaExceeded with quota.ExceededDetail whose
      Resource="concurrent_deployments", Limit=5, Requested=1,
      Reserved=5 (proves the row lock serialised every winner before
      the loser observed the limit), Current=0 (no usage committed
      mid-race); the diagnostic string leaks no manual-XX /
      idem-cdep-XX / req_cdep_XX / corr_cdep_XX caller input;
      exactly 5 deployments rows in the (org, service) scope; exactly
      5 active concurrent_deployments reservations; zero
      monthly_deployments reservations (pins that the unpoliced
      sibling never accumulates rows); SumActiveReservations agrees
      with the raw count; authz.calls == attempts; jobs.calls ==
      successes (proves the Reserve sits before the Enqueue — a
      reordering regression would surface here as jobs.calls
      exceeding successes).
    * TestDeploymentServiceCreateAppliesConcurrentDeploymentsQuotaIndependentlyOfMonthlyDeployments
      is the negative complement: exhausts concurrent_deployments by
      creating 5 deployments serially against a hard limit of 5
      (the in-flight reservations stay active for the 15-minute
      DefaultReservationTTL, far longer than the test run), then
      proves a SIXTH Create rejects on the concurrent_deployments
      dimension specifically — never on monthly_deployments (no
      policy seeded for it) or another dimension. Pins zero
      monthly_deployments reservations and zero services
      reservations to guard against a regression that accidentally
      consumed an unrelated dimension's quota.

  - BE-0337 (api_keys), BE-0338 (members) are the next quota dimensions
    in the priority-1 queue. Both are likely count-axis dimensions and
    should clone the BE-0325..BE-0328 count-axis template directly.
    api_keys is NOT yet in the QuotaResource closed set per the
    BE-0335 progress entry's enumeration (which listed nine count-axis
    dimensions: projects/environments/services/applications/
    compose_stacks/databases/domains/preview_environments + the
    cpu/memory/storage/backup_schedules/concurrent_deployments/
    monthly_deployments magnitude-axis dimensions). BE-0337 and BE-0338
    will likely require a migration that ADDs api_keys and members to
    the quota_resource CHECK constraint plus the constant/membership
    map widening in store/quota.go and the schema-test surface. The
    next iteration should verify the closed-set membership BEFORE
    cloning the call-site template.
  - The pre-existing testutil.Factory id-prefix vs domain.Kind drift
    failures in TestEnvironmentService Create / TestServiceVariableService /
    TestEnvironmentRepoListByProjectReturnsDeterministicOrdering
    remain out-of-scope (already documented in
    BE-0324..BE-0335 progress entries and the Codebase Patterns
    section). They reproduce on the BE-0336 base commit when the full
    store suite runs against a real Postgres at default parallelism.
- Learnings for future iterations:
  - When the call site for a quota dimension is ALREADY in place
    (concurrent_deployments was added during BE-0323's deployment
    service scaffold), a dimension story collapses to a SINGLE new
    _test.go file. The BE-0335 monthly_deployments delivery proved the
    "call site already there" case once; BE-0336 confirms that the
    deployment service's two-dimension (concurrent_deployments,
    monthly_deployments) Reserve sequence is structurally complete
    AND can be tested independently by leaving the OTHER dimension
    unpoliced. Future test clones for new sibling dimensions inside
    multi-Reserve unit-of-work boundaries should follow the same
    "policy seeded ONLY for the dimension under test" pattern so the
    rejection's Resource string is unambiguously the dimension the
    story enforces.
  - The order of Reserve calls inside a unit of work has a TESTABLE
    consequence: a Reserve placed AFTER the JobEnqueuer.Enqueue would
    be detected by the "jobs.calls == successes" assertion because a
    failed quota check rolled back the *Tx and the Enqueue is part of
    the same *Tx. This is a load-bearing structural assertion that
    any future dimension test inside DeploymentService.Create or
    .Rollback should retain — it pins both the placement of the
    Reserve and the atomicity of the *Tx.

  - The pre-existing 23-test Factory-drift failure set in the
    store package (TestAPIKeyService*, TestEnvironmentService*,
    TestOrganizationVariableServicePatch*, TestProjectVariable*,
    TestServiceVariableServiceReplaceInvalidInputNeverOpensTransaction,
    TestEnvironmentReader*, TestEnvironmentRepo*, TestAPIKeyReaderGetAPIKey)

    BE-0337 working tree.
- Learnings for future iterations:
  - When a new quota dimension's owning service does NOT already
    have a quota port, the minimum atomic delivery grows from "one
    new test file" (BE-0331..BE-0336 sibling shape) to four
    coordinated change axes — see the Codebase Patterns entry for
    BE-0337. BE-0338 members is the next clone target; the
    MembershipService constructor likewise predates QuotaReserver,
    so the same four-axis delivery applies. BE-0339..0342 variable
    stories are NOT quota-dimension stories at all and use a
    different template.
  - The sealing-trap in quota_internal_test.go::TestQuotaResourceValid
    (`len(valid) == len(quotaResources)`) is the single test that
    catches a forgotten constant + membership-set entry pair in ONE
    failing line; the rest of the unit suite cannot, because Valid()
    only checks the map, never the constant set. Future quota
    dimension stories should expect this test to fail on the first
    `go test` and learn that the contract is "every QuotaResource
    constant MUST be in the membership set MUST be in the valid
    slice". The three things move together.
  - Pre-flight checking with `git stash` validates whether broad
    store-suite failures are pre-existing or introduced by the
    current change. The procedure is: stash tracked changes, move
    untracked new files to /tmp, run the failing test set, capture
    the failure-name set into /tmp/head_failures.txt, restore
    everything, re-run, diff. If the test-name sets are identical
    (only durations differ), the failures are pre-existing and
    out-of-scope. BE-0337 used this procedure to confirm the
    23-test Factory-drift failure set is HEAD-baseline and not
    BE-0337 regression. Future stories should adopt the same
    procedure when a broad-suite run shows more failures than the
    focused story-specific runs.

## 2026-05-16 - BE-0339 (Manage organization environment variables)
- What was implemented: secret-value encryption-at-rest for the
  organization-scoped variable surface (PUT/PATCH/DELETE
  /v1/organizations/{org_id}/variables and the matching reader).
  Customer-supplied is_secret=true values are now sealed by a
  documented secret-provider abstraction (internal/controlplane/secrets)
  before reaching the source-of-truth table; the on-disk `value`
  column for a secret row is `''` (CHECK constraint enforced) and the
  AES-GCM ciphertext, provider id, and key id live in three new
  columns the future Dokploy renderer Opens against. The wire-level
  redaction policy is unchanged — secret values still project as
  output.Sentinel — and the audit metadata is still counts-only on PUT
  and stable-field-names-only on PATCH (never the variable key, value,
  ciphertext, provider id, or key id).

- Remaining risks / follow-ups:
  - The remaining variable scopes (project, environment, service)
    are BE-0340/0341/0342 and still write plaintext secrets to
    their own per-scope tables today. The secrets package was
    designed cross-scope from day one (the Provider interface and
    both implementations cover every table identically), so the
    sibling stories are clones of this one with three mechanical
    swaps: project_variables/environment_variables/service_variables
    tables get the same three encryption columns + the same CHECK
    constraint via three sibling migrations; ProjectVariableService /
    EnvironmentVariableService / ServiceVariableService gain the
    same secrets.Provider dependency and the same sealVariableValue
    helper; cmd/yalla-api/main.go threads the same secretsProvider
    into all four constructors (the buildSecretsProvider helper is
    already cross-cutting). BE-0343 (variable inheritance resolver)
    needs a Provider-aware read path that Opens secret rows from
    every scope before merging; OrganizationVariable.SecretCiphertext
    is exposed so that resolver can Open without re-reading.
  - Key rotation (BE-0351) is the next at-rest story. The Provider
    already exposes everything the rotation worker needs: KeyIDs()
    enumerates the accepted set, ActiveKeyID() names the seal
    target, and the partial index
    organization_variables_secret_routing_idx ON (secret_provider,
    secret_key_id) WHERE is_secret = true lets the worker locate
    rows referencing a retired key without a full-table scan.
  - The 23 stable pre-existing -race-with-DB failures (environment-
    service / api-key-service Create paths + organization_variable_patch
    audit metadata) remain documented out-of-scope; my changes
    neither introduce nor fix any of them, confirmed by stashing the
    BE-0339 tree and re-running with the same DB.
- Learnings for future iterations:
  - Cross-cutting capability package that touches multiple
    same-shape tables (BE-0339 secrets-provider pattern, structural
    template for BE-0340..0342 sibling at-rest stories and any
    future cross-cutting source-of-truth seam — e.g. webhook
    signing secrets, deployment-config secrets, backup-target
    credentials): land the package ONCE under
    internal/controlplane/<pkg>, with the interface + a production
    implementation + a tests-only passthrough implementation + a
    package AGENTS.md that documents BOTH the contract AND the
    forward-applicable storage pattern (column shape, CHECK
    constraint shape, repository tuple shape, service-layer seam
    location). Then thread the interface into the FIRST scope's
    service constructor as a required dependency, add the FIRST
    scope's migration, and ship the first scope. The sibling
    scopes become mechanical clones of the schema + service +
    test changes because the cross-cutting package never grew a
    scope-specific surface.
  - At-rest encryption-column schema invariant: persist (provider,
    key_id, ciphertext) ALONGSIDE the existing plain `value`
    column, NOT instead of it. Force value='' for secret rows and
    cipher columns NULL for non-secret rows via ONE CHECK
    constraint that names the invariant in both directions. The
    invariant is the defence-in-depth backstop the service relies
    on — a bug in the application layer that tries to write a
    plaintext secret rolls back as a deterministic apierr.Conflict
    rather than a silent corruption. Mirror DO $$ guards in BOTH
    the up and the down migration that REFUSE to run while
    is_secret=true rows exist with the wrong shape, so a
    re-application or a rollback fails loudly rather than
    silently leaving plaintext behind or losing every sealed
    value.
  - Seal/Open seam at the SERVICE layer, never the repository:
    Seal is a side-effecting call that depends on a runtime
    Provider, not a *Tx; calling Seal before opening the
    transaction shortens the SQL critical section; the repository
    stays pure SQL. The cleanest service-layer helper is a
    one-line projector (sealVariableValue) that takes the
    customer's input shape and returns the repository's tuple
    shape — non-secret items pass through untouched, secret
    items go through Provider.Seal. The repository's Upsert /
    UpdateMutable take the projected tuple, so the SQL layer
    never knows anything about encryption.
  - Patch path for sealed rows has THREE post-state cases the
    service must enumerate explicitly: (1) caller supplied a new
    value → use it verbatim; (2) caller supplied only is_secret
    AND the current row is_secret → Open the current ciphertext
    via Provider.Open to recover the plaintext, then re-Seal under
    the active key (this is the only correct way to re-key a
    secret without surfacing the plaintext to the caller); (3)
    otherwise → use the current row's `value` column (non-secret
    row's plaintext). Skipping case (2) would either lose the
    secret bytes on a re-seal or write a "previously-sealed
    plaintext" string into the value column. The demotion path
    (is_secret=true→false) reuses case (2) to recover the
    plaintext, then writes it back to the value column with
    NULL encryption columns.
  - KeyID derivation strategy for the AES-GCM provider: take the
    first 8 bytes of SHA-256(key) and render as 16 hex chars.
    Properties:
    - Deterministic across processes: two processes booted with
      the same key list mint the same key id. The id is
      reproducible from the key material in any audit/rotation
      worker that has access to the master keys, without sharing
      state.
    - Non-secret: SHA-256 is one-way, so the id never reveals the
      key bytes. Tests explicitly assert the full hex-encoded key
      is not a substring of the id.
    - Short: 16 hex chars fits in audit metadata, log lines,
      grep'able fields, without inflating the row.
    - Collision-safe in practice: 8 bytes = 2^64 space; for any
      realistic operator's accepted-key pool (≤10 keys) the
      birthday-bound collision probability is negligible.
    The active key is element 0 of the input slice; the rest are
    accepted for Open during rotation. NewAESGCM rejects duplicate
    keys at construction so a misconfiguration that silently
    reduces the rotation pool is caught fast.
  - cmd/yalla-api wiring for a cross-cutting capability package:
    add ONE buildSecretsProvider helper near runStartupChecks,
    NOT one per scope. The helper resolves the config
    (cfg.DecodedSecretKeys), returns the AESGCM provider when
    keys are configured, and falls back to Plaintext with a
    Warn-level log line for the local/test profiles. Strict
    profiles (staging/production) refuse to start without the
    keys via an explicit sentinel error
    (errStrictProfileMissingSecretKeys), backed by the
    config.Validate() check (requireStrictFields adds
    EnvSecretKeys to the missing-set). This makes the at-rest
    seam discoverable in ONE place and avoids the
    repeat-this-block-per-scope drift that plagues placeholder
    Authorizer/Quota/Job wiring elsewhere in main.go.
  - Test-fixture shape for the new on-disk schema: when the
    schema CHECK constraint forbids the previous fixture shape,
    update the seed helper IN PLACE rather than introducing a
    second helper. seedOrganizationVariable now writes the
    encryption columns under the Plaintext provider's wire
    identifiers ("plaintext-v1" / "plaintext") for is_secret=true
    fixtures, so every legacy seedOrganizationVariable(..., true)
    call site keeps working. Pair the fixture change with a
    package-level test helper (revealVariableValue) that projects
    OrganizationVariable.Value back to the plaintext for both
    shapes — for the Plaintext provider, ciphertext IS the
    plaintext bytes, so the helper is one branch (if IsSecret →
    string(SecretCiphertext) else v.Value). Tests that previously
    asserted v.Value == "expected" become revealVariableValue(v)
    == "expected" with no further restructuring.
  - Audit-metadata redaction discipline: the audit row NEVER
    carries any of the encryption-side strings (ciphertext bytes,
    provider id, key id), in addition to the existing "never the
    customer-supplied key or value" rule. The at-rest test's
    no-leak scan reads the audit row's raw metadata column and
    fails if ANY of {plaintext, key name, hex(ciphertext),
    key_id, provider_id} appears in it. This pins the negative
    invariant even when the audit Auditor's regex backstop drifts.
  - When a contract change widens the OrganizationVariable struct
    with internal-only fields (SecretProvider, SecretKeyID,
    SecretCiphertext), the LogValue redaction MUST be updated in
    the SAME edit. Otherwise, a stray slog record that captures
    an OrganizationVariable would leak the new ciphertext field
    until a future redaction story catches it. The pattern: every
    LogValue redacts EVERY value-bearing field at every type
    boundary, even ones the wire layer doesn't surface.
  - When extracting Value/Plaintext assertions out of failing
    tests against a contract change, FIRST stash the working tree
    and re-run the failing tests on HEAD to separate "I introduced
    this failure" from "this was already failing". The diff of
    failure name sets is the cleanest signal: identical sets means
    every remaining failure is pre-existing and the new code is at
    parity. BE-0339 used this technique to confirm that 3 of 12
    org-variable test failures and 23 of 26 store-wide failures
    were pre-existing (environment-service / api-key-service /
    organization_variable_patch audit metadata, all documented in
    earlier progress entries as out-of-scope for the current
    story). Without this check it is easy to over-correct an
    already-broken test or under-correct a regression.
